Bears vs. Bengals: Backups Favored Over Possible Starters The Bears blew out the Browns 34-10 in its opener with Tyson Bagent running the offense. Cincinnati, coming off a win over Detroit in its own opener, has hinted its starters could actually see the field this week, including quarterback Joe Burrow , as the team looks to shake off a run of slow starts to the regular season. Seahawks vs. Titans: Defending Champs Hit The Road The Seahawks enter this game 0-1 after a 17-7 loss to the Cowboys , still finding its footing under a new offensive playcaller, Brian Fleury. The Titans , by contrast, opened its preseason with a win over San Francisco and heads into Sunday's nationally televised game with early momentum and a home crowd behind it. Pictured: DJ Uiagalelei The San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Chargers will face off in Week 2 of the NFL preseason tonight. Kickoff is set for 10:00 p.m. ET from SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif. The game will broadcast live on NFL Network. The 49ers are favored by -1.5 on the spread with the over/under set at 38.5 (49¢ over / 52¢ under). The 49ers are 52¢ favorites to win outright, while the Chargers are 49¢ underdogs. Let's get into my 49ers vs Chargers predictions for Thursday, August 20. 49ers vs Chargers Prediction, Pick 49ers vs Chargers pick: Chargers to Win (49%, Polymarket) My 49ers vs Chargers pick is on Los Angeles to win, currently available at 49% on Polymarket . But as always, make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. 49ers vs Chargers Odds 49ers vs Chargers Preseason Preview Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy were both vocal in proclaiming their displeasure regarding their performance in joint practices against the Chargers this week. Shanahan even went on to say he “didn’t really like how we finished the day.” As I read between the tea leaves of both their comments, it seems that, beyond the first teams on both sides of the ball, the 49ers are struggling to identify reliable depth pieces. Purdy is slated to get the start in this game, but I do not factor that much into the handicap of this preseason clash with the Chargers for two reasons. First, the health of the star players for the 49ers continues to be an issue — meaning even in the short stint Purdy will be on the field, he’ll be tasked with moving the ball without the likes of Mike Evans , Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle . Second, Los Angeles also plans to play Justin Herbert and the starting offense for a series or two. This should neutralize any advantage for either team, given the very small sample size we will have to see the well-known regular-season contributors. It is always difficult to project which defensive starters will play and how long they will remain in the game, but one key cog for the Niners, Nick Bosa , will almost certainly be resting on the sidelines. We must rely on reports from joint practices and last week’s preseason showing to project how each defense may perform in this game. Vic Tafur of the Athletic covered the joint practices between these two teams, and he made it quite clear in an article this week that outside of defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa’s disruption, the San Francisco defense was the less physical team of the two and surrendered a number of big plays. This is right in line with what we witnessed against the Titans in the 49ers' first preseason game, specifically, in terms of stopping the run. The Titans averaged 5.4 yards per rush against the Niners, while the Shanahan-led offense could only muster 3 yards per carry on 28 carries . Simply put, the 49ers lost the line of scrimmage in their 19-13 defeat. The Chargers, on the other hand, turned in an impressive, well-rounded account of their depth in a 27-7 win in Houston. Despite facing the experienced Davis Mills, the Chargers limited the Texans offense to just 5.5 yards per pass attempt on 15 passes while Mills was under center. For the game’s entirety, Houston converted just 33% of 3rd-down attempts. The Chargers were both efficient and explosive in their first outing under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. They converted 50% of the 3rd-down attempts and averaged 9.5 yards per pass attempt. McDaniel orchestrated six chunk gains of 15+ yards through the air, including a 32- and 55-yard completion from 3rd-string quarterback DJ Uiagalelei. Herbert’s direct backup, Trey Lance, had an up-and-down performance but continued to show flashes of what made him a high draft selection just a few years ago. It’s worth noting that in the 2025 preseason for the Chargers, Lance was a reliable performer, accounting for 415 total yards and three touchdowns without committing a turnover. How to Trade 49ers vs Chargers Without reading too much into one exhibition game, the Chargers felt like an operation primed for success from top to bottom. They averaged 6.3 yards per play while limiting Houston to just 4 yards per play and 209 total yards for the entire game. Given that the 49ers’ main objective for Thursday’s game might be to focus on fundamentals and keep many of their players in bubble wrap, I do not understand why they are favored in this spot. The Chargers under Jim Harbaugh have scored 23 or more points in five consecutive preseason games. Kyle Shanahan’s Niners have reached that number just once in their last seven exhibition matchups. In addition to Los Angeles seemingly having the more reliable depth, I will gladly back the team placing more emphasis on success in these games by taking the Chargers at 48% to win this game on Polymarket. If that’s the case, Mendoza could get one hell of a test right away. No Code Needed Home Right Arrow NFL 2026 NFL Offensive Line Rankings for Every Team Brandon Anderson Staff Writer Download App Updated: Aug 20, 2026, 10:16 AM EDT Updated: Aug 20, 2026, 10:16 AM EDT 15 min read Credit: Reuters/Imagn. Pictured: Quinn Meinerz (Broncos), Quenton Nelson (Colts), Joe Thuney (Bears), Tristan Whirfs (Buccaneers). Today NFL Rankings Week gets to my favorite positional rankings on the board — seriously — the offensive lines. It's not particularly glamorous analyzing those five behemoths in the trenches, but if you think about it, five is almost half of the 11 men on offense! These guys almost never touch the ball outside of snapping it, but even in 2026, football is still won and lost in the trenches. No position group in football is more impactful yet overlooked than the offensive line — and that can give us a serious edge as bettors and analysts. A good line can elevate an average supporting cast, but even the most talented quarterbacks and skill players can't do much if the defense is living in the backfield on every play. Offensive lines are more multiplicative than additive. A great line multiplies an offense's greatness, while a bad one can stymie the entire attack. Last year's offensive line rankings gave us an orange flag for two Super Bowl favorites, and the Lions and Chiefs went on to miss the playoffs. It also gave us great value on the Broncos and Bears as sleepers featuring top-five lines. So, what are some of the key considerations when ranking offensive lines? Offensive lines are a team effort. It's less about one or two stars elevating the unit and generally more of a weakest link game. Much like an NBA defense, an O-line needs five guys working together in sync at its peak. Continuity is extremely valuable, especially early in the season, since the five guys on the line are working together. This season, as usual, there's an especially high amount of turnover on the lines for some teams. Depth and versatility are always significant value adds. Guys will inevitably miss time during a long, grueling season, so which teams are built to withstand? Scheme matters. It's easier to run block (attack!) than pass block (react and defend!). Run-heavy teams tend to get better O-line results, and play-action-heavy schemes make things much easier on lines. Run blocking can be floor raising for bad teams, but elite pass blocking is harder to come by and more meaningful at the top of the league. Let's rank all 32 NFL offensive lines, focusing on continuity, depth, scheme, and balance as we head into the new season. What are the implications for NFL bettors? Be sure to check out the whole NFL rankings series: Quarterbacks Skill positions 2026 NFL Offensive Line Rankings Tier Number Category Tier 1 Consensus No. 1 Tier 2 Could End the Year No. 1 Tier 3 The Ol’ Stalwarts Tier 4 Good Not Great Tier 5a Wild Cards I Believe In Tier 5b Wild Cards I'm Skeptical Of Tier 6 Much Improved Tier 7 League Average Would Be a Surprise Tier 8 All Downside Tier 9 Dregs of the League Betting Takeaways Tier 1 — Consensus No. 1 1. Broncos (Last Year: 2) It's tough to evaluate offensive lines, so it's wise to rely on the outstanding work from experts like Brandon Thorn, PFF, and others who've done plenty of work in this area already — and virtually every expert opinion I looked at agreed the Broncos are at the top for 2026. It's been a steady climb for Denver over the past couple years and this team now returns all five starters a third consecutive season. LT Garett Bolles and RG Quinn Meinerz are the standouts, but OL coach Zach Strief makes this whole unit look good. So does the quick offensive scheme Denver uses to get the ball out of Bo Nix 's hands quickly. This unit is better pass blocking than run blocking, and it's probably not a towering No. 1 like the Eagles or Lions have been in recent seasons, but there's little doubt Denver's line is set up to finish at or near the top of the league this season. Click here to return to the table of contents. Tier 2 — Could End the Year No. 1 2. Buccaneers (Last Year: 5) 3. Colts (Last Year: 16) 4. Chargers (Last year: 26) This may not look like a big leap for the Buccaneers compared to last year's ranking, but it would be a significant step forward. Tampa Bay started last season high in my rankings but quickly fell as injuries mounted. The team lost 27 games combined to right tackle and both guard positions, and Baker Mayfield 's play suffered as the season went along. The line looks healthy now, and that sets the Bucs up for a big year. Tristan Wirfs is arguably the best tackle in football and especially elite in pass protection, and he gets a healthy return from his RT counterpart Luke Goedeke, who has really come into his own next to rising star RG Cody Mauch. This unit is better blocking for pass than run and could take a minute to adjust to new OC Zac Robinson's wide zone scheme, but Mayfield's legs help and this line should be in for a huge step forward if it stays healthy. The Colts look like the league's best run-blocking line for 2026. Indianapolis has bounced back in a huge way under OL coach Tony Sparano, with future Hall of Fame LG Quenton Nelson anchoring the unit. Four of five starters return, and really all five since second-year RT Jalen Travis started the final month of the season. The right side of the line isn't as strong as the left and there's not great depth, but there's lots to like here between continuity, coaching, scheme, and talent. The Colts may not necessarily have a QB depending on Daniel Jones ' health, but this is a top-seven QB-agnostic offensive setup because of blocking and head coach Shane Steichen's playcalling. If they ever actually get and stay healthy, the Chargers could contend for best offensive line in the league. It's the Chargers, though, so that remains a forever if. LT Rashawn Slater missed all of last season with a patellar tendon injury, and RT Joe Alt missed half of it with an ankle problem. Slater is still working his way back, and now C addition Tyler Biadasz is out indefinitely with a knee injury, which likely means second-round rookie Jake Slaughter snapping the ball at C for the foreseeable future. If that trio can get on the field together, this could be a really strong line, with potentially the best tackle duo in the league. It could take time, though, with three new starters on the interior of the line plus a major scheme change under new OC Mike McDaniel. McDaniel had great success elevating an under-talented line in Miami and developing some diamonds in the rough, so that should help. So should the quiet investment of a couple off-radar signings: FB Alec Ingold, who was key to McDaniel's rushing attack in Miami, and TE Charlie Kolar, who was practically a sixth offensive lineman for the Ravens at times. This unit finished last season ranked 30th by PFF. If the Chargers' line can stay healthy and on the field, this might be the single biggest unit improvement in the entire NFL, with the potential to swing everything for Los Angeles. NOTE: The Biadasz injury is not a great start and might already be enough reason to drop the Chargers closer to the lower top 10 until we see Slater and Alt dominating on the field. Stay tuned. No Code Needed Home Right Arrow NFL Denver Broncos Season Preview: Nix’s Development Defines Super Bowl Dreams Pablo Planovsky Download App Updated: Aug 20, 2026, 07:11 AM EDT Updated: Aug 20, 2026, 07:11 AM EDT 6 min read Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect. Pictured: Bo Nix. Denver returns as one of three teams bunched at the top of the AFC West after a season that ended one win short of the Super Bowl , losing the AFC Championship 10-7 to New England without an injured Bo Nix under center. Nix enters 2026 after two procedures on that ankle, including a spring clean-up that cost him OTA reps, and the most recent reports describe him as fully recovered heading into camp, with a new offensive coordinator in Davis Webb and a first-round trade addition at receiver in Jaylen Waddle . The odds widgets throughout this preview track how the Broncos are priced across division, playoff, conference and MVP markets in real time; here's what tends to move those numbers from Polymarket . Denver Broncos Season Preview 2026 Denver's division and playoff pricing reflects a roster the market still rates among the conference's best, even after falling just short of a Super Bowl trip. A team that reaches a conference title game typically holds firmer pricing the following year than its raw win total alone would suggest, since that level of postseason success signals real strength across the roster, not just a hot stretch. The division race itself is unusually tight this year, with three teams bunched closely together rather than one clear favorite pulling away. That kind of parity tends to keep every team's price more sensitive to early results than a lopsided race would, since a fast start or a costly loss can shift the perceived favorite within a matter of weeks. Conference and Super Bowl futures for Denver carry a specific health question this year that a fully healthy roster wouldn't. Nix's recovery from ankle surgery is the clearest single variable traders watch, since his health status was the deciding factor between Denver playing in the AFC Championship and playing in the Super Bowl last season. Denver's numbers track the division race closely: with three teams bunched at the top, the Broncos' playoff, conference and Super Bowl pricing all sit a notch below the co-favorites rather than clearly behind them: the kind of gap a single hot or cold stretch could close or widen fast. Top Denver Broncos Team Prop Contracts Team stat-leader contracts for a team returning most of its core carry less uncertainty than they do for a roster in transition, since the market has a full season of data on personnel and scheme to draw from. A new coordinator introduces some variance, but less than a full coaching change would, especially when the head coach and the rest of the staff stay in place. Adding a proven receiver through trade tends to shift these markets gradually rather than immediately, since a new player still needs to build chemistry within an existing offense before the numbers fully reflect his presence. Traders watching a team like Denver this year should expect target distribution to take a few weeks to settle into a clear pattern. Injury status remains the fastest way these prices move for any team, and that's especially true here given the quarterback situation last season. A setback in Nix's recovery, or a clean bill of health confirmed in camp, would likely move Denver's stat-leader pricing faster than any personnel change on its own. Denver's team stat-leader pricing sits well down the board in both major categories, which tracks with a backfield and receiving corps the market hasn't fully re-priced yet around this year's new pieces. That's likely to stay soft until target and carry distribution settle into a clear pattern. Top Denver Broncos Player Prop Contracts Award markets for a quarterback who missed his team's biggest game of the season carry a specific kind of asterisk into the next year. Nix's MVP price reflects both his regular-season form, which earned him a spot among the league's top 100 players, and the uncertainty of returning fully healthy from a significant injury. A new offensive coordinator adds another layer to how traders price a quarterback's market this season. Even a talented passer can see his numbers shift, up or down, when the scheme calling his plays changes, so award markets often stay conservative on a player like this until game tape confirms the new system suits him. Player-movement markets tell a complementary story for Denver this season. A first-round pick spent on an established receiver is a significant transaction, and traders often watch how that investment gets used early in the season as a signal for how the passing game is evolving under new coordination. Nix's MVP price sits well down the board, which fits a quarterback the market hasn't yet seen play a live snap since surgery. His individual passing props tell a similar story: both his yardage and touchdown markets show him as a solid favorite at the lowest thresholds, with confidence fading at the tiers that would represent a real leap from his 2025 form — the passing-yards market in particular is still thin on volume, so treat the shape as more informative than the exact numbers for now. Waddle's own receiving-yards market shows a similar pattern: comfortably favored to clear a solid floor, but the price thins out well before reaching true WR1 territory, which tracks with a receiver still adjusting to a new offense and a new quarterback. Denver added him this offseason in a trade that cost a first-round pick, pairing him with Nix as the quarterback returns from the ankle injury that ended his season in last year's AFC Championship loss. Broncos Prediction Market Outlook: How the Season Could Unfold Markets tend to price a team that reached a conference title game the way they'd price a legitimate contender, provided the core of the roster returns largely intact. Denver checks that box on paper, but the market is also pricing in real uncertainty around the one player whose health mattered most in last year's outcome. A three-way division race like this year's AFC West adds a layer of volatility beyond what Denver's own roster health creates. Every result involving Kansas City or the Chargers effectively moves Denver's price too, since the division market is a shared pool where one team's gain is close to a direct subtraction from the others. Early-season volatility should center on two threads for Denver specifically: how the quarterback performs and moves in his first live snaps back from injury, and how quickly the new pieces on offense, including the receiver added by trade, integrate into the game plan. Either thread moving in a clearly positive or negative direction would likely reprice Denver's markets faster than the win-loss record alone. Midseason separation in a division this tightly bunched often comes down to head-to-head results between the top three teams rather than performance against the rest of the schedule. Watch those direct matchups closely, along with any recurring injury report involving Nix, since both carry outsized weight for how traders price the rest of Denver's season. Denver enters the season looking to build on a 2025 campaign that ended one win short of the Super Bowl, a 10-7 loss to New England in the AFC Championship Game, played at home in the snow, with backup quarterback Jarrett Stidham starting in place of an injured Nix. No Code Needed Home Right Arrow NFL 2026 NFL Skill Position Rankings for Every Team Brandon Anderson Staff Writer Download App Updated: Aug 19, 2026, 01:40 PM EDT Updated: Aug 19, 2026, 01:40 PM EDT 15 min read Credit: Reuters/Imagn. Pictured: Bijan Robinson, Justin Jefferson, Jahmyr Gibbs, Ja’Marr Chase. Rankings week continues here at Action Network, and today I'm unveiling my second ever skill position rankings. These are the names you know well from your fantasy football leagues, but that also makes this exercise tricky because real football isn't played on draft boards or spreadsheets. So who exactly counts for today's exercise? We're talking offense only — so no bonus for kick returners or special teams — and it's just anyone that's not a quarterback or offensive lineman. That means running backs, wide receivers, tight ends, and anything in between like a fullback, H-back, etc. Of course, not all positions are created equal. I rank RBs, WRs, and TEs separately before combining for this exercise, but receivers are worth more than half of my final composite score. The passing game is so important in modern football. In fact, I actually weigh tight ends slightly more than running backs now in a league where more and more teams are playing 2- and 3-TE sets. Stars matter, but depth might be even better. Show me versatility! Do you have some tight ends that block and others that act as extra receivers? Can your RBs catch passes and/or block? Does your WR room complement each other and make a cohesive unit? How many skill players are ready to step in and make an impact when that inevitable injury happens? You get one set of weapons on a new NFL team, agnostic to contracts, scheme, or coaching — just which team's skill players give you the best shot to win a Super Bowl? These are your 2026 Skill Position Rankings for every team, from 1 to 32. Be sure to check out the whole NFL rankings series: Quarterbacks 2026 NFL Skill Position Rankings Tier Number Category Tier I MVP Starter Pack Tier II Loaded Deep at Every Spot Tier III Fantasy Football Island Tier IV One Star, No Weaknesses Tier V Saved By One Position Group Tier VI This is What Average Looks Like Tier VII AFC Contender Red Flags Tier VIII Young Talent That's Not There Yet Tier IX One Receiver Is Our Only Hope Tier X They're Definitely M.I.A. Betting Takeaways Tier I — MVP Starter Pack 1. Rams (Last Year: 8) Turns out having the best set of weapons in the league is a pretty good MVP starter pack. With the Rams , it's not just star power but also depth. Puka Nacua is the star, coming off a monster 129/1,715/10 season. He's an elite blocker too, the full package, and Davante Adams is about as great a red-zone threat as there is. The running game has also been great, with both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum ranking in the top 15 in PFF grade at their positions, making this a top-10 RB room. But it's the multifaceted TE room that really puts the Rams over the top. Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee are quality all-around threats, Davis Allen adds further depth, and sophomore Terrance Ferguson is a rare vertical threat X factor that's effectively WR3 on this team. Even if every team had a league-average QB, this is my No. 1 QB-agnostic offense in the NFL with these weapons, a great line, and the best playcalling in the league. No Code Needed Home Right Arrow NFL 2026 NFL Quarterback Rankings for Every Week 1 QB Brandon Anderson Staff Writer Download App Updated: Aug 19, 2026, 01:31 PM EDT Updated: Aug 19, 2026, 01:31 PM EDT 15 min read Credit: Reuters/Imagn. Pictured: Justin Herbert, Caleb Williams, Drake Maye, Josh Allen. No position in all of team sports is more important than quarterback. Quarterbacks touch the ball on every single play. An elite QB can drag an average roster deep into the playoffs, while a bad signal caller can doom an otherwise loaded roster. In my NFL Power Ratings, quarterbacks reign supreme — by a huge margin. I count QB as worth over 40% of the entire offensive unit ranking and almost 25% of the overall roster rank. They're just that important. Consider former MVP Josh Allen. With Allen healthy, the Bills rank in the top five offensively and top 10 overall in my system, bona fide Super Bowl contenders. But replace Allen with a league-average starter, and the Bills drop to around 18th on offense, a fringe playoff contender. Give Buffalo the worst QB in the league and it drops to bottom 10, largely irrelevant and out of the playoff picture altogether. That's why QBs get their own column, and it's why we'll check in on these rankings again all throughout season. Unlike many recent seasons, there's not a ton of turnover, with just six NFL teams starting an Opening Day quarterback in 2026 that did not start last season — and most of those six started a chunk of last season anyway. That means many familiar names from last year's column , but plenty of new ranks. So what QB would you want right now for one season on a new NFL team, agnostic to contract, surrounding talent, and scheme? That's the question we'll answer today at the league's most important position. These are my 2026 NFL Quarterback Rankings , from 1 to 32. 2026 NFL Quarterback Rankings Tier Number Category Tier I The Best of the Best Tier II AFC North Bites Back Tier III Great Regardless of Surroundings Tier IV The Litmus Tests Tier V The Upside Swings Tier VI Win With, But Not Because Of Tier VII No. 1 Pick Wildcards Tier VIII We Just Don't Know Yet Tier IX Unfortunately, We Probably Do Know Tier X Might As Well Be You or Me at QB Betting Takeaways Tier I — The Best of the Best 1. Josh Allen (Last Year: 2) 2. Patrick Mahomes (Last Year: 1) I've written this column for years, and Patrick Mahomes has ranked No. 1 for seven straight Opening Days — until this one. I noted last year that Josh Allen should probably be No. 1 but that Mahomes felt invincible until proven otherwise. Well, consider it proven after a 6-11 Chiefs season and an offseason surgery to repair a torn ACL. The truth is that there really isn't a good case against Allen at the top anymore. The physical tools are obvious — both as a passer and as a runner — and he's largely cut down the mistakes and been mostly great in the playoffs. Don't believe me? Allen may be 8-7 in the playoffs, but he's responsible for 38 touchdowns and just six interceptions in those games. He ranks first all time in playoff yards and touchdowns per game, as well as TD-to-turnover ratio. Allen regressed in sack avoidance last season, and he ended with a clunker in the loss against Denver. But he also finished top three in MVP voting for a fifth time in six seasons, and it would surprise no one to see him add to his tally this fall. But it's not like Mahomes took a tumble. He's down just one spot, and still in this top tier. There's real reason to be concerned, though. Mahomes is coming off the first major injury of his career, after finding a lot of his value last season as a runner. He's also on a three-year downswing of serious drop-off to around fringe top-10 in go-to QB metrics like Expected Points Added (EPA), Completion Percentage Over Expected (CPOE), and Success Rate (SR) after more or less leading those stats for the rest of his career. Mahomes had 20 Turnover Worthy Plays in 14 games, with most quality QBs closer to one per game, and he had his worst season ever throwing his trademark deep ball. Consider that Mahomes lost eight games last season — even with the knee injury ending things prematurely — after losing only 23 the entire rest of his career! That's twice as many losses as Mahomes has in the playoffs ever, and that's why he still ranks this high. For his career, Mahomes is still 17-4 in the playoffs with 5,814 yards, 46 TDs, and 10 interceptions — basically a full MVP season in the games that matter most. It's fair to have some concerns, but until those playoff numbers drop, he's going to be just fine. Even during this three-year downswing, Mahomes is still averaging a 10.3-win season with zero run game, bad receivers, and a fading offensive line, plus a 6-1 record in the playoffs with a ring. That'll do. Going up against Jacksonville’s third- and fourth-string defensive backups, Wilson should give New Orleans an edge when it comes to late-game execution. No Code Needed Home Right Arrow NFL Titans vs 49ers Predictions, Spread Pick, Odds Tonight Michael Crosson Download App Updated: Aug 13, 2026, 06:23 PM EDT Updated: Aug 13, 2026, 06:23 PM EDT 5 min read Credit: Aug 4, 2026; Nashville, TN, USA; Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh talks with the media during training camp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images The Tennessee Titans and San Francisco 49ers will face off in Week 1 of the NFL preseason tonight. Kickoff is set for 9:00 p.m. ET from Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif. The game will broadcast live on NFL Network. The Titans are 6.5-point favorites over the 49ers on the spread (Titans -6.5), with the over/under set at 39.5 (52¢ over/ 50¢ under). Tennessee is priced as a 69-cent favorite to win outright, while San Francisco is listed at 32 cents to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Titans vs 49ers predictions for Thursday, August 13. Titans vs 49ers Predictions, Picks Titans vs 49ers pick: 49ers +6.5 My Titans vs 49ers prediction is San Francisco to cover the spread via our Polymarket promo code . Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Titans vs 49ers Odds Titans vs 49ers Preview Titans Preview: Don't Buy the Narrative The Tennessee Titans originally opened as 2- or 2.5-point favorites in this matchup, depending on the shop, but the line has steadily climbed in their favor. All the exterior narratives currently scream to back Tennessee. New head coach Robert Saleh is eager to make a strong first impression and has announced that all four quarterbacks on the roster will see some action in Thursday's preseason opener. The intention to play starters in some capacity has undeniably factored into the line movement — we now see the Titans favored by 3.5 at Polymarket , and that number can now be found up to 4.5 at some places. However, evaluating preseason football requires context. The Titans’ quarterback room certainly features recognizable names, with former No. 1 overall pick Cam Ward comfortably sitting at the top of the depth chart with a pretty safe job, backed up by Mitchell Trubisky, Will Levis, and Hendon Hooker. While players like Trubisky and Levis boast plenty of actual NFL game experience, expectations should be tempered. They will be taking snaps alongside a bunch of backups on a squad that went 3-14 last season. Furthermore, when starters play in preseason games, it is typically only for a few scripted drives at less than maximum effort. If Ward or any of the starting offense played more than a single quarter, it would be surprising, meaning the bulk of what is essentially a televised practice will fall on the shoulders of secondary units struggling to find an offensive rhythm. 49ers Preview: Injuries Aplenty On the other side, the infamous electrical substation that looms over the 49ers ’ practice facility seems to have already found its midseason form, as several key San Francisco starters already find themselves on the injury report. Key pieces, including Mike Evans , Ricky Pearsall , Christian Kirk , Nick Bosa , and George Kittle , are either recovering from old injuries or dealing with new ones. This growing injury list has undoubtedly contributed to the spread creeping up to the 3.5/4.5 range. Head coach Kyle Shanahan, who famously plays things close to the vest regarding game plans, offered a characteristically vague update stating, “There won’t be many starters playing.” Given the current health of the roster, it is safe to take him at his word. San Francisco’s quarterback rotation also supports a conservative exhibition strategy. Best-case scenario: Mac Jones gets the starting nod and manages the offense for a chunk of the game. Jones was more than competent last season, going 5-3 as a starter while completing 69.6% of his passes for 195 yards per game with 13 touchdowns and six interceptions . Frankly, Jones might be too valuable — either as Brock Purdy ’s backup or as a future trade asset — to risk in the preseason. We might get him for a brief showcase to court a trade suitor, but don't hold your breath. If Shanahan opts to sideline his top two signal-callers, the remaining snaps will be left to a battle between 2025 seventh-round pick Kurtis Rourke and undrafted Nebraska journeyman Adrian Martinez. While that pairing might not sound inspiring on paper, Shanahan's system famously elevates whichever quarterback executes it best, regardless of draft pedigree. Brock Purdy was the 262nd pick in the draft. Shanahan also guided Jimmy Garoppolo to a Super Bowl! The Niners hand-picked Rourke late in the draft, and Shanahan clearly sees potential in Martinez. He can't seem to get rid of this guy, which makes me believe this duo should be able to keep things competitive in a preseason environment at the very least. Titans vs 49ers Prediction, Spread Analysis This matchup is a textbook trigger for the Bet Labs system titled Fade Line Movement, Early Preseason. This historical angle dictates that during the first two weeks of the exhibition schedule, anytime a favorite sees the opening spread move 1.5 points or more in their direction, the value shifts to the underdog. The fundamental theory here is that moving a line more than a full point based on one team's starters playing a few drives — or the opposing team's starters resting — is an overreaction. When the opening line of 2 or 2.5 was originally set, analysts were already operating under the assumption that the 49ers’ starters were not going to be on the field for most of the game. The same applies to the Titans. Don't expect to see more than a few series from Cam Ward and the Tennessee starters. Bumping the spread through the key number of 3 based on the Niners' recent injury vibes and Saleh’s declaration to play his quarterbacks isn't an accurate valuation of the actual game dynamics. No Code Needed Home Right Arrow NFL Pahokee, Florida Produces NFL Players at 47 Times the National Rate Ben Mendelowitz Research Analyst Download App Updated: Aug 12, 2026, 07:17 AM EDT Updated: Aug 12, 2026, 07:17 AM EDT 4 min read Credit: 2K3EC54 Inglewood, CA, USA, January 2022: The flag with the NFL logo waving in the wind. NFL is a professional American football league Pahokee sits on the southern edge of Lake Okeechobee, population 6,071, and has sent 21 players to the NFL. That works out to 345.9 players per 100,000 residents, Pahokee's own city-level rate. That is more than 47 times the 7.4-per-100,000 national average, calculated across the population of all 50 states and Washington DC. No other US city or town with at least 5,000 residents comes close to Pahokee's rate. Action Network analyzed data on every player to appear in an NFL game, cross-referencing hometowns against Pro Football Reference's birthplace database, then adjusted for city population to find where the league's talent is genuinely concentrated rather than just where the most people live. Cities and towns under 5,000 residents, and cities outside the US, were excluded from the ranking to avoid a handful of players in a tiny population inflating the rate. That leaves 3,297 qualifying US cities and towns. Key findings: Pahokee, Florida tops every US city or town with at least 5,000 residents, at 345.9 NFL players per 100,000 population. The city has produced Anquan Boldin, Fred Taylor and Janoris Jenkins, among others. Washington DC leads all 50 states plus DC at 30.0 players per 100,000, driven almost entirely by the district itself (208 of its 209 players trace back to Washington DC proper). Mississippi is the top-producing state, at 21.6 players per 100,000, nearly 3 times the national rate of 7.4. Chicago produces more NFL players in raw numbers than any other city, 496 total, but its population of 2.66 million puts its per-capita rate well outside the top tier. Nine of the 10 highest per-capita cities have fewer than 15,000 residents, showing NFL production concentrates disproportionately in small towns rather than major metros. Which Cities and Towns Produce the Most NFL Players Per Capita? Pahokee's case is well documented. Two rival high schools roughly 10 miles apart, Pahokee and Glades Central (in neighboring Belle Glade), have combined to send more than 60 players to the NFL over four decades, largely through a bruising annual rivalry known as the Muck Bowl. Anquan Boldin played in three Pro Bowls and won a Super Bowl with Baltimore in 2013. Fred Taylor rushed for over 11,000 yards across 13 NFL seasons. Both are Pahokee natives. Stone Mountain, Georgia ranks second at 212.8 per 100,000, with 13 players from a population of 6,109. Atlanta, Texas (not the Georgia metro) and Columbia, Mississippi are almost tied for third, at 160.6 and 160.5 respectively, both towns of roughly 6,000 people producing 9 to 10 NFL players apiece. Natchez, Mississippi is the only city in the top 10 with a population above 15,000, producing 22 players at a rate of 145.4 per 100,000. It is also the only top-10 entry to crack double digits in raw player count by a wide margin outside Pahokee. Please scroll to see the full data below: Small-town pipelines like Pahokee's tend to show up again once the next draft class starts getting priced on prediction markets. Action Network's best prediction markets reviews break down where those markets are sharpest heading into draft season, and anyone opening a position on Novig can grab the current Novig promo code first. Which States Produce the Most NFL Players Per Capita? Collating every city and town in the dataset by state tells a different story than the city-level ranking. Washington DC leads the country, but its sample leans almost entirely on the district itself rather than a spread of smaller towns. Among the 50 states, Mississippi is the clear leader at 21.6 players per 100,000 residents, despite ranking 35th in total US population. Louisiana is a close second at 20.8, and Alabama rounds out a Deep South cluster in third at 14.7. All three states produce NFL players at more than double the national rate of 7.4 per 100,000. Ohio is the highest-ranked state outside the South, in fifth place at 12.85 per 100,000, spreading its production across 240 different cities and towns, the widest base of any state in the top 10. Nebraska's sixth-place finish is driven by a smaller population rather than a deep talent base, at 226 total players. Methodology Action Network sourced every NFL player's birthplace from Pro Football Reference's birthplace database, covering every player to appear in a regular-season NFL game. Each birthplace was matched to its city or town population, then converted to a rate of NFL players per 100,000 residents to control for population size. Cities and towns with fewer than 5,000 residents were excluded from the city-level ranking to prevent towns with a handful of total players and a very small population skewing the per-capita rate. State-level rates were calculated by summing every player's hometown by state, then dividing by each state's 2026 population estimate from the US Census Bureau's Population Estimates Program. Washington DC was included in the state-level ranking as a distinct jurisdiction alongside all 50 states. The 5,000-resident floor removes the noisiest end of the dataset but does not fully eliminate small-sample volatility. Three cities in the city-level top 10, Atlanta TX, Bryn Mawr PA and Gilmer TX, have produced fewer than 10 total NFL players. At that sample size, one or two additional players would meaningfully shift both the rate and the ranking, so those entries should be read as smaller, noisier samples than city-level leaders like Pahokee (21 players) or Natchez (22 players). State-level rates do not carry this issue, since even the smallest state in the top 10, Nebraska, is built on 226 total players against a population of over 2 million. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions CINCINNATI -- There are a couple of reasons Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow isn't backing down from the championship chatter before the start of the new season. For starters, Burrow is hopeful that by talking about it enough, he can will a potential run to the Super Bowl into existence. The other reason? After two seasons of falling short after deep playoff runs, followed by three years of missing the postseason, enough is enough. Burrow is treating this season as a now-or-never year for Cincinnati. "You can keep pushing it down the road or you can talk about it now and say this is the year," Burrow said Thursday. "You know, I'm tired of saying, 'Next year, next year, next year.' This is it. "Your life is too short to keep pushing things down the road. I'm trying to instill some urgency and some intensity in everybody to go and be great every day and try to make it happen." That urgency has been a theme throughout the offseason and on Thursday following the team's joint practice against the Chicago Bears . While both first-team offenses had their fair share of good moments during team drills, Cincinnati closed the day with a clean victory. In the final two periods that mimicked the last 3:30 of a game, the Bengals' starters won both of them. Following a defensive stop, the offense moved the ball just enough to put kicker Evan McPherson in position for a field goal that won the period. In the second period, Cincinnati's defense dominated. First, newly acquired defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II picked off a ball he batted into the air. Then, defensive end Myles Murphy got two sacks, including one safety, before cornerback Jalen Davis intercepted Chicago's Caleb Williams as Williams remained under pressure a few yards away from his own goal line. It was exactly the type of showing the Bengals were hoping for when Cincinnati revamped the team after a 6-11 campaign last year. It was the first losing season since Burrow's rookie year in 2020 and a far cry from the team that lost in Super Bowl LVI in Jan. 2022 and lost in the AFC Championship Game a year later. In recent months, Burrow has spoken about his title aspirations, even drawing comparisons between this year's Bengals roster and the 2019 LSU team he led to an undefeated season and College Football Playoff title. That talk has been intentional. https://t.co/PAPATL0Ijj pic.twitter.com/IoByf9tQcK Ben Baby (@Ben_Baby) August 20, 2026 "I'm trying to put it out into the world," Burrow said. "I'm trying to manifest it. I'm trying to show our guys the urgency that I have and that I want us to have as an organization to go and make it happen." Since the end of last season, Cincinnati has operated as aggressively as it ever has. It signed linebacker Boye Mafe to a three-year, $60 million deal, and traded for Lawrence, which has already provided promising returns. After beating up on Cincinnati's offensive line throughout training camp, he caused havoc against the Bears. "He's an All-Pro guy," said Williams, adding that Lawrence is in the same category as Kansas City's Chris Jones . "He's a force to be reckoned with, and that's something that you go into a game week that you plan for him, that you plan to execute against him and doing things that aren't necessarily in his favor." Cincinnati's front office held up its end of the bargain when it came to producing a championship-level defense. Burrow said on Thursday that he believes the side of the ball that struggled so much over the past two seasons is good enough to push the Bengals back to the Super Bowl. However, an offense that is tinkering with a more varied attack is still trying to find its footing as the preseason winds down. Burrow acknowledged as much on Thursday. "We have to be more consistent on offense," Burrow said. "Our standard is so high, but it's so high because of what we've done and what we can do." Cincinnati still has three weeks until the season opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . That's when the Bengals will start to find out if it will finally be the year it all comes together -- or what might happen if it doesn't.

He joined ESPN in 2016 after covering the Eagles for Philadelphia Magazine's Birds 24/7, a site he helped create, since 2010. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions FOXBOROUGH -- Count Eagles running back Saquon Barkley among those who are happy the joint practices with the New England Patriots are now behind them. "I'm the wrong guy to ask because I hate joint practices, to be honest. I think one day is good," he said when asked about the benefits Thursday. "More times than not nothing good comes out of it. When you have the work it's good, but then you get the pushing, the shoving and someone says this about you and it's 'I don't know about that but you're this.' It's immature when you get to that level. I have to do a better job, too, because I'm a little troublemaker sometimes, but I was good this week." "Good" might be relative, as Barkley -- always known to mix it up with the defense during practice -- appeared to be at the center of at least one scrum Thursday. During a separate sequence, Philadelphia tackle Lane Johnson and New England linebacker K.J. Britt were grabbing each other by the face mask. To Barkley's point, there were several skirmishes between the Patriots and Eagles on the day, mostly between the Eagles' offense and the Patriots' defense. "That's bound to happen after Day 2," Barkley said. "Obviously football is a physical game within itself and it's just a little extra pushing and shoving. We've also got to do a better job of not allowing that to have a factor in our practice." The general consensus was that the joint practices were beneficial overall for the Eagles, who are installing a new offense under coordinator Sean Mannion. The new wide zone running scheme appeared effective, with Barkley and company breaking off several long runs, while the passing game showed it still is in the midst of the learning curve, as evidenced by Jalen Hurts' five interceptions over two days. Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio appeared to get plenty out of it, too, singing a much different tune than Barkley. "I love doing these things. I think these things are great," he said. "I wish we would do another one. It's great to go against a new team, new schemes, new players. You learn things. You're going to get unscouted looks and plays and see how people react. These things are tremendous and can't get enough of it."

records.new_body: 2026 Cleveland Browns training camp: Latest intel, updates - ESPN What we're hearing and seeing at Browns training camp: Watson delivers a must-see throw in practice vs. Bills --> Skip to main content Skip to navigation What we're hearing and seeing at Browns training camp: Watson delivers a must-see throw in practice vs. Bills Cleveland Browns 1h Daniel Oyefusi Cowboys: Jerry Jones shares camp thoughts as team leaves Oxnard Friday 57m Todd Archer Seahawks: CB Diggs talks for first time since signing 57m Brady Henderson Patriots: Maye pleased after two practices with Eagles 57m Mike Reiss Giants: Jaxson Dart's best performance of the summer? 57m Jordan Raanan Fantasy football rankings: Eric Karabell's RB tiers 13h Eric Karabell Fantasy football rankings: Eric Karabell's WR tiers 13h Eric Karabell Solak: Why Ben Johnson's Bears offense is much more than just Caleb Williams Chicago Bears 2d Ben Solak Hallmark, hot dogs and touchdowns: The Colston Loveland story Chicago Bears 2d Courtney Cronin NFL Future Power Rankings: We stacked all 32 teams based on expectations for 2027 to 2029 Kansas City Chiefs 4d Louis Riddick, +3 More NFL preseason on NFL Network, ESPN: How to watch, schedule 20d ESPN play Jordan Rodgers adamant Shedeur Sanders should be starting in preseason for Browns (0:50) Daniel Oyefusi Aug 20, 2026, 06:24 PM ET Close Daniel Oyefusi covers the Cleveland Browns for ESPN. Prior to ESPN, he covered the Miami Dolphins for the Miami Herald, as well as the Baltimore Ravens for The Baltimore Sun. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Browns reporter Daniel Oyefusi has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room. What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Browns camp. The biggest question for Cleveland remains who will be the starting QB? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53? Catch up on all the updates, including the Browns' top camp performer and biggest lingering question. Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams Latest Browns stories Shedeur Sanders not feeling pressure about Browns' QB decision Deshaun Watson returns with 'awesome' first half for Browns What are the Browns looking for in their QB competition? Jerry Jeudy clarifies viral video, says he talked to Browns QBs AJ Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation Thursday, Aug. 20 After a spirited joint practice with the Buffalo Bills on Thursday, Browns coach Todd Monken said he doesn't anticipate seeing the team's older starters play in Saturday's preseason game. Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson split first-team reps in the practice. Watson delivered one of his best throws of camp early in practice, when he found rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion downfield in between a pair of Bills defenders. Watson, though, had a poor stretch in red zone drills, sailing a pass to a wide-open Harold Fannin Jr . and then throwing an interception to defensive back Jordan Hancock a couple of plays later. One of Sanders' best moments came during a third-down session. On one play, Sanders used his cadence to draw the Bills defense offside and threw a downfield pass to wide receiver Isaiah Bond , who drew a defensive pass interference penalty. On the next play, Sanders found wideout Malachi Corley downfield for a big gain in the middle of the field. Sanders led Cleveland's only two-minute drill in practice and drove the offense the length of the field, but he was "sacked" on the penultimate play, and then his last-second pass to rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston in the end zone was broken up by corner Maxwell Hairston . "It didn't look like we were out of place. It looked like we belonged," Monken said after the practice. Watson to Conception, part 2 https://t.co/dc36Pebs90 pic.twitter.com/NDIqmKSuS1 Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) August 20, 2026 More observations: On the second play of a two-minute drill, the Browns defense allowed a 50-yard touchdown pass from Josh Allen to Dalton Kincaid on an apparent coverage bust. Running back Quinshon Judkins missed his second day of practice with what Monken called a "nagging" injury. Defensive end Alex Wright left practice on a cart after sustaining an apparent injury in defensive line-offensive line 1-on-1s. Defensive tackle Travis Bell left practice early with a member of the medical staff. Monday, Aug. 17 Shedeur Sanders is slated to start at quarterback in the Browns' second preseason game against the Bills on Saturday, but he could be playing without Cleveland's starting offense. Coach Todd Monken said he and Bills coach Joe Brady agreed to hold out starters if their No. 1 units get enough work in during joint practices on Thursday. "Would I like to have a decision today? Of course," Monken said. "Would I like a decision by next Monday? Of course. I'd love to have that decision. And we'll see. We've got a lot of football this week. We've already had a lot of football. We've got four days of practice and a game. That all adds into any decision with the roster and who the starters are. "Some are further along than others, right? We already know. That's part of it. And I'm OK. By the time we get to next week, that'd be great. We can start planning that way, have some practices, and here we go." More observations: Michael Coats Jr . and Nate Evans practiced after leaving the preseason opener with injuries. Zak Zinter , Myles Bryant , and Elijah Chatman returned to practice after missing multiple sessions, as well as the preseason opener. Thirteen players did not practice: Joe Royer , Cedric Tillman , D'Angelo Ross , Michael Burton , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall Jr ., Parker Brailsford , Jack Conley , Jack Stoll , Alex Wright (new), Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Maliek Collins . Monken said the Browns are being "overly cautious" with Schwesinger, who hasn't practiced since July 31. The team is hopeful he will return to practice next week. The Browns signed tight end Jermaine Terry II and waived tight end Brenden Bates with an injury designation. Who has been the Browns' top performer so far at camp? WR Denzel Boston . The No. 39 overall pick is trending to be Cleveland's No. 1 receiver sooner rather than later. Boston has dazzled with plenty of highlights, using his 6-foot-4, 215-pound frame to make contested catches almost daily. He's also made himself a friendly target for quarterbacks as a smooth route runner. Boston recently got promoted to the No. 1 offense as Cleveland's boundary receiver. What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? Who will be the Browns' starting quarterback? Deshaun Watson will start the preseason opener; Shedeur Sanders will start the second preseason game. The exhibition matches will allow Todd Monken to evaluate the quarterbacks in a bevy of game-like situations. The first-year head coach is placing an importance on pre-snap operation and playmaking ability. Wednesday, Aug. 12 The Browns are hoping quarterback Deshaun Watson 's return to health will mean a return to the Pro Bowl form he displayed with the Texans, but Watson said Wednesday that "my game has definitely changed." "I'm different, man," Watson said before practice. "I think ever since I've been here early on, bringing up Houston was cool, but I'm 30 now. I had some injuries and things like that. So, my game has definitely changed. But the mentality in how I play and how I approach it doesn't." Watson was one of the NFL's top dual-threat passers in Houston, but suspension and injuries have limited him to just 19 games since Cleveland traded for him in March 2022. "I think you have to be who you are because if you try to be something you're not, you're not going to play at the highest level of your skill set," coach Todd Monken said. "So it's just the way it is with him; he's going to have to play or utilize his athleticism in order to play at the top of his skill set. ... But one of the superpowers is his athleticism. I mean, that always has been. So you can't take that away or you've basically taken away a part of what made him special." More observations: In a lighter practice ahead of the team's preseason opener against the Bears, Watson and Shedeur Sanders led successful two-minute drills to cap the session. Both quarterbacks connected on deep passes during their possession. Sanders had a deep completion to wide receiver Isaiah Bond , who made a diving catch. Watson lofted a pass to receiver Luke Floriea along the offense's sideline. Teven Jenkins and Tyre Phillips split snaps at right guard with the No. 1 offense. Cornerback Denzel Ward and offensive tackle Izavion Miller returned to practice. Cornerback Tyron Herring left practice with a member of the team's medical staff during individual drills. Fifteen players did not practice: Joe Royer , Cedric Tillman (new absence), D'Angelo Ross , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall, Parker Brailsford , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Elgton Jenkins , Dae'Quan Wright , Jack Stoll , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis . Veteran edge rusher Tyus Bowser had a tryout with the Browns on Wednesday, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. Tuesday, Aug. 11 Four days before their preseason opener against the Chicago Bears on Saturday, the Browns listed " Deshaun Watson OR Shedeur Sanders " at starting quarterback in their first unofficial depth chart. Coach Todd Monken has yet to announce which quarterback will start in Chicago, but spoke about the value the preseason adds for evaluating the two passers. "It does, in terms of getting the ball out, got to learn to get the ball out. Got to learn how to slide," Monken said. "You're not going to be able to just run around. I do want playmaking ability, so there is a balance there between playmaking ability and taking some sacks. You're going to have to live with that to an extent. "The other part is stacking plays, where it matters, because they got the scoreboard on in terms of points you put on the board. In terms of the flow of the game, that's a big part of it. We're going to be on the road. The ebbs and flows of positive plays and negative plays, overcoming that. I think there's a part of the quarterback's body language, how they are around the team. Do I sense, 'Hey, that's over. I've moved on to the next play.' So there's a number of things you get to evaluate once you get to the closest we have in terms of games, which is preseason." With rookie Spencer Fano securing a starting role at left tackle, Monken said the only starting position on the offensive line up in the air is right guard. Teven Jenkins and KT Leveston have been rotating at the spot. "I think Teven has the advantage there from experience," Monken said. Deshaun Watson to Isaiah Bond for the TD in 11-on-11 pic.twitter.com/FmuZcCXD2K Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 11, 2026 More observations: Special teams coordinator Byron Storer said the team is "definitely taking a hard look at" punters Wes Pahl and Nik Constantinou , but "It's Corey [Bojorquez]'s job to lose." Monken said he is "hopeful" that defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr . will return to practice "soon." Hall hasn't practiced since Aug. 3. On the second-team offensive line, the Browns moved Dawand Jones from left tackle to right tackle and rookie Austin Barber from right tackle to left tackle. Cornerback Damarri Mathis left practice on the back of a cart after he sustained an injury in coverage during a 1-on-1 drill. The team later placed Mathis on injured reserve. Defensive tackle Travis Bell left practice early with a member of the team's medical staff. Fifteen players did not practice Tuesday: Joe Royer , D'Angelo Ross , Denzel Ward (new absence), Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall Jr ., Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Jack Stoll , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Maliek Collins . The Browns claimed tight end Dae'Quan Wright off waivers from the Eagles, per the NFL transaction wire. The Browns had three tight ends in for a tryout today, per the NFL transaction wire: Sal Cannella , Matt Lauter and Jermaine Terry II . Monday, Aug. 10 Coach Todd Monken explained the change in the quarterback rotation last Saturday. Though Monken said before the practice that Shedeur Sanders would get a "majority" of first-team reps, he said he was later informed that Sanders had received more padded practices with the starters than Watson in the week. So Monken changed the order of reps. Sanders practiced with the starting offense Monday, while Watson led the No. 2 offense. "As long as we're still sharing reps, it's a competition," Monken said. Monken also said he has not decided which quarterback will start the preseason opener in Chicago on Saturday, but he intends to start Watson in one of the first two preseason games and Sanders in the other. "I'd like to get our starters out there for the first series together [in the preseason opener]," Monken said. Sharp low red zone session for Shedeur Sanders. Finds Harold Fannin and then Jerry Jeudy here pic.twitter.com/okVcJgJ23h Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 10, 2026 More observations: Both Watson and Sanders threw short touchdowns during red zone 11-on-11 team drills, but it was overall a mistake-filled practice for the offense. Monken ended a two-minute drill for the No. 1 offense after three consecutive pre-snap penalties. The head coach then called it a day after back-to-back pre-snap infractions for the No. 2 offense. Monken made two notable non-quarterback personnel changes, as rookie left tackle Spencer Fano and rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston practiced with the first-team offense. Fano had been alternating days at starting left tackle with Dawand Jones . Monken said Fano's performance Saturday, in which he went head-to-head with defensive end Jared Verse and even engaged in a post-play scuffle, "solidified" the decision to give the first-round pick more first-team reps. Right tackle Tytus Howard , rookie linebacker Justin Jefferson and cornerback Damarri Mathis returned to practice. Fourteen players did not practice: tight ends Joe Royer (personal) and Jack Stoll ; cornerbacks Myles Bryant and D'Angelo Ross ; fullback Michael Burton ; linebacker Carson Schwesinger ; defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr ., Elijah Chatman , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis and Maliek Collins ; and offensive linemen Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller and Zak Zinter . Saturday, Aug. 8 The Browns made a major change to the quarterback rotation in their 10th practice. Despite Shedeur Sanders being scheduled to lead the No. 1 offense in his alternating reps with Watson, it was Watson who took every starting rep in team drills. Sanders split the remaining reps with Dillon Gabriel . Before practice, coach Todd Monken indicated that there might be a 7-on-7 session in which Watson threw to the team's top pass-catchers but added that "Shedeur will take the majority of the 1 reps today." The Browns are off Sunday, and Monken said the coaching staff would use that time to discuss which quarterback will start the preseason opener against the Bears next Saturday in Chicago. More observations: Watson had another productive practice to cap a bounce-back week for him. His highlight throws included a deep completion to wide receiver Isaiah Bond in 7-on-7 after he got a step ahead of cornerback Tre Avery , then a short touchdown pass to rookie wideout Denzel Boston on a back-shoulder fade in 11-on-11, beating corner Tyron Herring . Right tackle Tytus Howard left practice early with a member of the team's medical staff. Rookie Austin Barber took Howard's spot with the starting offense in team drills. Elgton Jenkins and Teven Jenkins returned to team drills after being limited to individual drills Friday. Fifteen players did not practice: Justin Jefferson (new absence), Joe Royer , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Damarri Mathis , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall Jr ., Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Maliek Collins and Kendrick Green . Friday, Aug. 7 The Browns had a lighter practice indoors and in helmets on Friday, as they are set to practice in pads for more than two hours on Saturday. It was still an eventful session, with all the quarterbacks pushing the ball downfield in team drills. Deshaun Watson looked his most comfortable attempting deep passes in camp so far. He connected with wide receiver Isaiah Bond for a long gain in 11-on-11s and also found wideout Jerry Jeudy for a 40-yard touchdown in 7-on-7s. Toward the end of practice during a two-minute drill, Watson evaded the pass rush and rolled out to his left before throwing a pass into the end zone that Bond leapt up and caught. Browns running end-of-game 2-min drill. It's fourth down, offense down 4. Deshaun Watson buys time and throws it up to Isaiah Bond, who goes up for the leaping catch in the back of the end zone. pic.twitter.com/dvISvpp2v9 Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 7, 2026 More observations: While Watson had some accurate downfield passes, he was also intercepted by cornerback Denzel Ward on an errant pass that went over the head of Bond; it's Watson's eighth interception in nine practices. The Browns signed offensive lineman Jack Conley and cornerback Jeadyn Lukus , claimed defensive tackle Patrick Jenkins , waived wide receiver Jamari Thrash (injury designation) and linebacker, and placed guard Kendrick Green on injured reserve. Rookie safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren recorded his first interception of camp, picking off Shedeur Sanders after he overthrew tight end Jack Stoll in 11-on-11s. Safety Donovan McMillon intercepted Dillon Gabriel in 11-on-11s on an underthrown deep ball to rookie wide receiver Kole Wilson . Linebacker Winston Reid forced a fumble on running back Raheim Sanders and recovered the ball to end the two-minute drill led by Sanders. Elgton Jenkins , Mason Graham and Teven Jenkins returned to practice, but both Jenkinses were limited to individual drills. Thirteen players did not practice: Joe Royer , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Damarri Mathis , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall Jr ., Parker Brailsford , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Zak Zinter , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Maliek Collins . Thursday, Aug. 6 The Browns' eighth day of practice concluded the installation of coach Todd Monken's offense. Going forward, Monken said practices would focus more on situational football, "premier plays," and work against defensive looks that Cleveland will see from opponents this season. "What we're trying to do is stack as many good plays as we can within what we're asking them to do on a given day," Monken said. "I'd much prefer stacking really good days, but as the head coach, if the offense is stacking really good days, it probably means the defense wasn't stacking a very good day. So, within every practice there's usually give and take, some ebb and flow of practice -- some things you all don't see, and some things that at the moment we don't see until we see it on tape. So it's really about how many plays in a row can we stack?" Good response from Sanders, finds KC Concepcion in the end zone two plays later https://t.co/sKtgEHzHsp pic.twitter.com/bWq7GCkePx Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 6, 2026 More observations: Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders both threw an interception in team drills. Cornerback Tyson Campbell intercepted Watson in 7-on-7 drills, while cornerback Myles Harden intercepted Sanders in red zone 11-on-11 drills. Safety Grant Delpit broke up a pass intended for rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston , which led to the pick. Two plays after his interception, Sanders threw the lone touchdown in team drills when he found rookie receiver KC Concepcion in the end zone after he located an opening in Cleveland's zone defense. Guard Zak Zinter left practice on a cart. Sixteen players did not practice Thursday: Joe Royer , Myles Bryant , Michael Burton , Damarri Mathis , Carson Schwesinger , Mike Hall Jr. , Parker Brailsford , Kendrick Green , Izavion Miller , Elijah Chatman , Elgton Jenkins , Teven Jenkins , Sam Kamara , Kalia Davis , Mason Graham , Maliek Collins . Wednesday, Aug. 5 Quarterback Deshaun Watson had a slow start to training camp but had his best day to date on Wednesday. After two consecutive practices in pads, the Browns practiced in shoulder pads and helmets and ran extensive red zone and goal line 7-on-7 drills. Watson excelled, throwing multiple touchdowns, but he also looked more in sync and confident pushing the ball downfield in other team drills. "I think to say who's ahead is a little extreme," Browns coach Todd Monken said before practice. "But we evaluate every day where our roster is, who's where. We try not to knee-jerk react on the one day; that's hard to do. We want every day to go as smooth as it can, and it doesn't, so you have to fight that part of it. We also have to fight; we're in install. We see what you see, and we see a little more in-depth because of the film. But the reality is we're always talking about personnel and the roster; the quarterbacks just happen to be part of that." More observations: Sixteen players did not practice Wednesday: tight end Joe Royer (personal), cornerback Myles Bryant and Damarri Mathis , fullback Michael Burton , linebacker Carson Schwesinger , defensive tackles Mike Hall Jr ., Kalia Davis , Mason Graham , Maliek Collins (PUP), Sam Kamara and Elijah Chatman ; centers Parker Brailsford and Elgton Jenkins ; offensive tackle Izavion Miller , guard Teven Jenkins and wide receiver Jamari Thrash . Tuesday, Aug. 4 Quarterback Shedeur Sanders , leading the No. 1 offense in Cleveland's quarterback competition today, led a two-minute drill that ended in a field goal. It marked the second straight day Sanders led a successful two-minute drill to end practice. "I've been highly impressed over the last four months that I've been around him with how far he's come as a player, and he's only going to continue to get better," Browns coach Todd Monken said. "There's a lot to take in when you're installing. We got through the spring, then we were gone for six weeks, and then you start back up again in a new system. I think you'll continue to see his operation and mechanics improve, and I think that's the biggest part right now is in and out of the huddle, getting to the line of scrimmage, eliminating that anxiety, his anxiety and my anxiety." Best throw of the day so far in what has been a slow practice for the offense. Shedeur Sanders to Luke Floriea on third down in 7-on-7. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- A.J. Brown and Jalen Hurts caught up for a few minutes after practice Thursday -- a notable development after the Patriots receiver revealed Wednesday that the former teammates had not spoken since he was traded to New England by the Eagles in June. Brown and Hurts greeted each other warmly on the visitors practice field and smiled as they spoke out of earshot of reporters before shaking hands and going their separate ways. The two have a long history together, dating back to when Hurts hosted Brown on a recruiting trip when he was at Alabama. They would work out together in the offseason and grew so tight that Hurts became godfather to Brown's daughter, Jersee. They teamed up for four fruitful seasons in Philadelphia that included back-to-back 1,400-plus receiving seasons for Brown and a Super Bowl championship after the 2024 season. Brown, however, expressed his desire for a change of scenery with the Eagles front office following a frustration-filled 2024 season, general manager Howie Roseman conveyed at the time. According to sources, Hurts was a factor in the receiver's frustrations, based in part on Brown not being targeted as much as he felt he should be against zone coverage. Brown let his unhappiness with his role in the offense be known on social media and in interviews during a 2025 season in which he posted 1,003 receiving yards -- his lowest totals in four seasons with the Eagles, and eventually got his wish to be traded. "Honestly guys, none of that stuff even matters, man. You all should want to report something positive. You know asking the question is going to turn negative," Brown said Wednesday when reporters asked follow-up questions about Hurts. "So let's not get into that. Let's keep everything positive. It's love my way." "I've got a lot of love for him and always have," Hurts said Wednesday, echoing Brown's sentiments.

Prior to ESPN, McFadden was a Denver Broncos beat reporter for the Denver Post. McFadden also wrote about the Baltimore Ravens and University of Maryland athletics for The Baltimore Sun. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions HENDERSON, Nev. -- Quarterback Fernando Mendoza is a football nerd, but in a good way. Just ask his former high school coach, Dave Dunn. As a 15-year-old quarterback at Christopher Columbus High School in Miami, Mendoza would skip eating lunch with his classmates in the cafeteria and take his food to Dunn's office, where he would have a notebook and pen in hand to go over the practice plan. Their routine meetings continued throughout Mendoza's time at Christopher Columbus. Even in the offseason, Mendoza would go over what defenses are doing and come up with ideas for the Explorers to implement into their game plan. "How many 15-year-old kids are wired that way?" Dunn told ESPN. Mendoza's meticulous preparation and dedication to his craft propelled him from being a three-star recruit in high school to becoming a Heisman Trophy winner and national champion at Indiana in 2025. It is with these traits that the Las Vegas Raiders hope Mendoza can develop into the face of the franchise and help the organization achieve sustained success whenever the 2026 NFL draft's No. 1 pick is called to be the starting quarterback. For now, Mendoza will look to use his studious techniques for Thursday's preseason game against the Houston Texans ( 8 p.m. ET, ESPN ). "[At quarterback], the expectation is to be the most prepared guy in the building," Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said. "Out of the young quarterbacks that I have been around, I think he has the upper hand on them in that area." Dunn, who has been at Christopher Columbus since 2019 and even coached Mendoza's brother Alberto, said Fernando doesn't like to leave any stone unturned. In Dunn's experience with Mendoza, nothing rarely caught the South Florida native off guard. The coach attributed that to Mendoza studying and mentally preparing himself so that he could put the team in the best position to win games. Dunn recalled a moment during a regional final game in which Mendoza didn't see anyone open so he had to improvise and scramble for a touchdown on the first drive. Mendoza came back to the sideline, breaking down the play, step-by-step. "Every once in a while, somebody's going to throw something at you you've never seen before," Dunn said. "... [Mendoza] knew nothing was open, and he knew where the pressure was coming from. He goes, 'All right, I knew I had to move to my left. I had the X receiver as a possibility. Saw that he wasn't going to get open [and] my only option was to scramble.'" Dunn admired Mendoza's attention to detail and studious habits. Whenever he saw Mendoza in his office or in team meetings with a notebook, Dunn loved it even if he thought it was out of the norm for younger players. Mendoza was even preparing for Kubiak's offensive scheme before he heard his name called in April's draft. Last year in college, he watched a lot of NFL football on Sundays and film breakdowns of how Kubiak utilized the Seattle Seahawks ' offense. Since Mendoza has been a Raider, his notebook is still one of his biggest assets. During Raiders OTAs, quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan said Mendoza wrote out every pass play, detailing the progression and his footwork. Mendoza even gave his own critique of when he fell short or when he felt he did well. It was one of the examples Sullivan used to describe Mendoza's tireless work ethic and old-school approach. "[Mendoza] didn't have the neatest handwriting, but I appreciated him doing that. I said, 'Maybe you could type this next time,'" Sullivan said. "But he went through that process, and he's someone that I think a lot of his confidence comes from the preparation and the type of time and effort that he puts in." Mendoza understands he is behind the curve. Since the start of training camp, Mendoza has mostly played with the second-team offense, while Kirk Cousins has played solely with the starters. Last week, Mendoza watched Cousins orchestrate a scoring drive at the beginning of the Raiders' 27-14 preseason loss to the Arizona Cardinals . And he still saw a significant gap between the 15-year veteran signal-caller and himself. Still, Mendoza's performance was good enough for Kubiak to call him an "ascending player." He threw for 97 yards and a touchdown, showcasing that progress has been made. Mendoza, however, is a perfectionist, so he harped on his jitters during his first drive, the misthrows and misreads. Mendoza repeatedly mentioned what needs fine-tuning. "Like you see Kirk has this time [and] anticipation. ... That's an area I've got to grow in," Mendoza said. Mendoza has been putting in extra work outside of the team's training camp practices. He occasionally spends time with the centers on the roster to strengthen his comfort level with playing under center. He has spent late nights in the indoor practice field, going through the team's offensive script with some of his teammates. And following his preseason debut, Mendoza said he immediately began watching the film of his performance. Mendoza continues to be an avid listener, soaking in the advice he receives from Cousins, his coaches and minority owner and NFL legend Tom Brady. "You have to do everything that you possibly can to get that mental edge over your opponent, and that's what he's doing," Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor said. "He still has a long way to go, but having Kirk as a mentor to him, Tom [Brady] as well, is really going to help his game grow." Fullback Connor Heyward said: "He wants to earn everything, which is that much more special. ... When you have a quarterback like that, you know the future is very bright." Mendoza's short-term memory has also been essential for his development. He tries not to dwell on the mistakes, such as the interception he threw in the red zone to Texans safety Jalen Pitre during the Raiders' joint practice in Houston on Tuesday. Instead, he views those moments as learning experiences and maintains an optimistic mindset. "It would be letting my teammates down if I let that burden me throughout the next couple of series, because I wouldn't be able to play on time and they wouldn't be able to rely on me," Mendoza said. "Tranquilo, which means 'calm' in Spanish. I say 'tranquilo' and move forward. You know, it's all good." Dunn said it has been "surreal" to see Mendoza's rise over time. When Mendoza was an unheralded high school recruit with just one Power 5 offer from Cal, Dunn knew all Mendoza needed was a chance, and his former star player would shine. Cal gave Mendoza an opportunity from 2022 to 2024, and then the Hoosiers did in 2025. When the Raiders eventually hand him the keys to the offense, Dunn knows Mendoza will be ready because of the work he puts in. "He is a lifelong learner when it comes to football," Dunn said.
