records.new_body: Denver Broncos 2026 preview: Bo Nix, Jaylen Waddle lead loaded AFC contender All NFL - current Fantasy College NFL Draft DFS Betting Denver Broncos 2026 preview: Bo Nix, Jaylen Waddle lead loaded AFC contender By Gordon McGuinness Posted Aug 11, 2026 9:00 am EDT Denver Broncos Jaylen Waddle adds another dimension: Waddle has earned PFF receiving grades above 80.0 in three of the past four seasons and gives Denver a speed complement to Courtland Sutton. Denver returns an elite foundation: The Broncos bring back all five key starters from PFF’s top-ranked offensive line and a defense featuring Nik Bonitto, Zach Allen and Pat Surtain II. Last Chance! The PFF Early Bird Sale Ends Aug. 17 : Save 33% and get PFF+ for just $79.99, our lowest price of the year. through . --> Explore PFF Fantasy Tools EARLY BIRD SALE: SAVE 33% — the lowest price of the year (opens in new tab) The Denver Broncos enjoyed a remarkable 2025 season, finishing 14-3 to win the AFC West and secure the No. 1 seed in the conference. They defeated the Buffalo Bills at home in the divisional round but lost quarterback Bo Nix to injury in the process, then fell 10-7 to the New England Patriots in the AFC Championship Game. With Nix healthy again, Denver has every reason to believe it can contend for the AFC's top spot once more and potentially go a step further in 2026. Here's our 2026 preview of the Denver Broncos . Key Free Agency/Trade Additions Position Player 2025 PFF Grade WR Jaylen Waddle 84.0 S Tycen Anderson N/A For the most part, it was a quiet offseason for the Broncos, but they made one major splash by adding wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. The sixth overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft is coming off another strong season and has earned PFF receiving grades above 80.0 in three of the past four years. Waddle's ability to win with speed makes him an excellent complement to Courtland Sutton , who caught 17 contested targets across the regular season and playoffs in 2025. Together, they give Denver two receivers who can win in very different ways. 2026 NFL Draft Class Position Player 2025 PFF Grade DI Tyler Onyedim 71.9 HB Jonah Coleman 82.1 OT Kage Casey 80.0 TE Justin Joly 77.9 S Miles Scott 77.0 TE Dallen Bentley 76.9 LB Red Murdock 91.1 Without a first- or second-round draft pick, it is difficult to find an immediate-impact player in the draft, and it won’t be a surprise to see limited contributions from the Broncos’ rookies in 2026. There’s still plenty to like about this class, though. Running back Jonah Coleman earned PFF grades above 80.0 in all four of his college seasons across stints at Arizona and Washington. He forced 174 missed tackles on 551 carries, with 4.1 of his 5.5 yards-per-carry average coming after contact. Tight end Justin Joly caught at least 40 passes in each of the past three seasons and averaged at least 1.75 yards per route run in each of the past four. He is excellent at the catch point, dropping just 5.7% of his catchable targets while producing a 66.0% contested-catch rate. Reasons for optimism The Broncos finished the 2025 season with PFF’s top-ranked offensive line and return their five best players up front in 2026. Left guard Ben Powers was the lowest-graded starter on the offensive line last year, and his 64.0 PFF grade still ranked 15th among left guards. Meanwhile, right guard Quinn Meinerz was the highest-graded guard in football, while Garett Bolles ranked fourth among left tackles. They also have a tremendous defense, with rookie cornerback Jahdae Barron the only player on that side of the ball to earn a PFF grade below 60.0 while playing 300 or more snaps. The defense was highlighted by the pass-rushing ability of edge defender Nik Bonitto and interior defender Zach Allen , who combined for 164 pressures across the regular season and playoffs, as well as cornerback Pat Surtain II , who allowed just 37 receptions into his coverage over that same span. The QB Annual Is Live Every qualifying quarterback. Every metric that matters. PFF grades, passing splits, EPA per dropback, clutch performance, interception luck and more — all in one interactive guide built on the same data trusted by all 32 NFL teams. Read the QB Annual (opens in new tab) Get PFF+ (opens in new tab) Reason for pessimism The Broncos simply don’t have many weaknesses on either side of the ball. If you were being picky, you could argue that an offensive line as good as theirs would benefit from having a truly elite running back behind it. What will likely define their season, though, is how big of a step forward Bo Nix can take in his third year. He has already improved his PFF passing grade from 73.8 as a rookie to 76.1 in Year 2, while his big-time throw rate climbed from 3.7% to 5.0%. Another jump in 2026 could be what takes an already talented Broncos roster to the next level. Breakout Candidate Rookie running back RJ Harvey had a solid debut season, earning a 69.6 PFF rushing grade across 165 carries while showcasing his big-play ability with runs of 38, 40 and 50 yards. He also contributed in the passing game, with his 1.40 yards per route run ranking 11th among the 43 running backs with at least 30 carries. With J.K. Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman sharing the backfield, Harvey is unlikely to take on a true workhorse role. However, he has the talent to emerge as Denver’s best running back in his second NFL season. Key roster battles With the Broncos having used a first-round pick on cornerback Jahdae Barron, it would be disappointing if he weren’t playing a significant role by the end of Year 2. He obviously isn’t going to take snaps away from Pat Surtain II, leaving his clearest paths onto the field ahead of Riley Moss on the outside or Ja’Quan McMillan in the slot. Neither player will be easy to displace. McMillan earned a 78.9 PFF coverage grade last season, while Moss led the team with 15 pass breakups. Both are set to become free agents after the season, so Barron may simply have to bide his time, but his role will be worth monitoring throughout the summer. Get access to PFF's fantasy rankings, projections and analysis before the offer ends, and make sure you have everything you need before you're on the clock. Last updated: Tuesday, August 11 1. RB Jeremiyah Love , Arizona Cardinals Love was selected third overall in April, the highest draft position for a running back since Saquon Barkley . Every running back taken within the first 20 picks over the past five seasons finished as a top-12 rookie. Love’s 79.2 PFF receiving grade ranks second among the top 20 running backs in the 2025 draft class, adding another dimension to an already high-upside profile. The landing spot in Arizona is a mild concern given the existing backfield competition and a PFF run-blocking grade that ranked fourth-lowest in the NFL last season, but the draft capital alone should secure him enough volume to be a borderline RB1 in redrafts and the top option in dynasty rookie drafts. 2. QB Fernando Mendoza , Las Vegas Raiders Mendoza was the No. 1 overall pick and the best pure passer in his class, but several factors keep him below the typical top selection in fantasy. He landed with a Raiders team that graded near the bottom of the league on offense, offers little of the rushing upside that fuels most recent first-round quarterbacks and ranks in the back third of recent first-rounders in PFF passing grade. The Raiders also appear set to sit him behind Kirk Cousins to start, so he may not play much, if at all, this season. He is worth waiting on in dynasty rookie drafts and is a redraft option only in superflex. 3. WR Carnell Tate , Tennessee Titans Tate was a surprise fourth overall pick in April, but the draft capital alone makes him the top dynasty wide receiver and the first rookie wideout off the board in redrafts. Recent top-10 selections like Ja'Marr Chase , Malik Nabers , Jaylen Waddle and Garrett Wilson all became immediate fantasy contributors. Tate's target share could mirror the 29.8% Nabers generated in New York given Tennessee ‘s similar receiver setup with Wan'Dale Robinson in the slot under Brian Daboll. The main variable is Cam Ward ‘s development as a passer, but Tate has the role and the situation to be a fantasy starter from Day 1. records.new_body: Carolina Panthers 2026 preview: Bryce Young enters pivotal year after NFC South title All NFL - current Fantasy College NFL Draft DFS Betting Carolina Panthers 2026 preview: Bryce Young enters pivotal year after NFC South title By Gordon McGuinness Posted Aug 10, 2026 6:15 am EDT Carolina Panthers Bryce Young faces a pivotal season: Young has earned a PFF grade above 70.0 in consecutive years, but Carolina will likely need to see more before committing to him beyond his fifth-year option in 2027. Carolina upgraded its defense: Devin Lloyd arrives after earning an 87.9 PFF grade in 2025, while Jaelan Phillips generated 76 pressures across the regular season and playoffs. The PFF Early Bird Sale Is Here : Save 33% and get PFF+ for just $79.99, our lowest price of the year. through . --> Explore PFF Fantasy Tools EARLY BIRD SALE: SAVE 33% — the lowest price of the year (opens in new tab) The Carolina Panthers lost their final two games of the 2025 regular season but still won the NFC South on a tiebreaker, returning to the playoffs for the first time since 2017. Their season ended with a home loss to the Los Angeles Rams in the wild-card round, but reaching the postseason was still an encouraging step forward for a team in the midst of a rebuild. Carolina was aggressive in free agency as it looked to build on that progress, but the team's ceiling in 2026 will likely be determined by the play of quarterback Bryce Young . Here's our 2026 preview of the Carolina Panthers . Key Free Agency/Trade Additions Position Player 2025 PFF Grade WR John Metchie 57.6 OT Rasheed Walker 63.0 C Luke Fortner 66.5 OT Stone Forsythe 55.4 QB Kenny Pickett 48.4 HB AJ Dillon 54.7 LB Devin Lloyd 87.9 EDGE Jaelan Phillips 74.2 Linebacker Devin Lloyd has steadily improved over his first four NFL seasons and is coming off a career year in 2025. His 87.9 PFF grade ranked third among all linebackers, with Lloyd pairing strong work against the run with significant improvement in coverage. He also provides value as a blitzer, generating 28 pressures on 103 pass-rushing snaps, the third-most pressures among off-ball linebackers. The signing of Jaelan Phillips carries some risk given his injury history, but his pass-rushing production returned to 2022 levels during his time with the Miami Dolphins and Philadelphia Eagles last season. His 76 total pressures across the regular season and playoffs ranked ninth among edge defenders, while his 44 pressures from Week 10 through the end of the season following his trade to Philadelphia ranked seventh at the position. 2026 NFL Draft Class Position Player 2025 PFF Grade OT Monroe Freeling 72.3 DI Lee Hunter 80.4 WR Chris Brazzell II 79.4 CB Will Lee III 66.5 C Sam Hecht 80.8 S Zakee Wheatley 85.9 LB Jackson Kuwatch 82.1 Defensive tackle Lee Hunter is a stout run defender with the potential to anchor the middle of Carolina's defensive line for years to come. After spending three seasons at UCF, Hunter earned a career-high 83.6 PFF run-defense grade in his lone season at Texas Tech. He also showed some ability as a pass rusher, earning a 72.1 PFF pass-rush grade in 2025, but his ability to hold up against the run is likely to be his calling card at the NFL level. Center Sam Hecht falling to the fifth round was a surprise given his reliability in college. He allowed just seven pressures on 392 pass-blocking snaps last season and did not surrender a sack across 850 pass-blocking snaps in his college career. He also earned a career-high 78.3 PFF run-blocking grade in 2025. While Luke Fortner enters the season as the likely starter, Hecht has a realistic path to becoming Carolina's starting center in the near future. Reasons for optimism Wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan made an immediate impact in his first NFL season, leading all rookie wide receivers in receiving grade (79.2) and trailing only Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III with an average of 1.85 yards per route run. McMillan quickly established himself as Bryce Young's favorite target, with his 126 targets across the regular season and playoffs twice as many as any other player on the Panthers' roster. The QB Annual Is Live Every qualifying quarterback. Every metric that matters. PFF grades, passing splits, EPA per dropback, clutch performance, interception luck and more — all in one interactive guide built on the same data trusted by all 32 NFL teams. Read the QB Annual (opens in new tab) Get PFF+ (opens in new tab) Reason for pessimism The Panthers are currently without both starting offensive tackles. Left tackle Ikem Ekwonu suffered a ruptured patellar tendon in the wild-card loss to the Rams, while right tackle Taylor Moton is sidelined with blood clots. It remains unclear when either will return in 2026, but both appear likely to miss at least the start of the season. That makes the additions of Rasheed Walker and Monroe Freeling through free agency and the draft even more important. Walker earned a 69.3 PFF pass-blocking grade in 2025, while Freeling was one of college football's top pass protectors, allowing just two pressures on 469 pass-blocking snaps. Still, losing both starting tackles is a significant concern, and for all of Freeling's potential, he has yet to play an NFL snap. There is also the question of how far Bryce Young can take this team. The 2023 No. 1 overall pick is coming off his second consecutive season with a PFF grade above 70.0, but he has shown the potential to become a top-tier quarterback only in flashes. His 4.5% big-time throw rate in 2025 ranked tied for 19th among the 45 quarterbacks with at least 100 dropbacks. That level of production is manageable while Young remains on his rookie contract, but the Panthers will likely need to see more before committing to him beyond his fifth-year option in 2027. Breakout Candidate The Panthers have already demonstrated their belief in former undrafted free agent Jalen Coker, signing him to a three-year, $34 million extension this offseason. Through his first two NFL seasons, Coker has earned PFF receiving grades above 70.0 and averaged at least 1.60 yards per route run in both years. With Tetairoa McMillan established as the primary target, Carolina does not need Coker to lead the passing game. Instead, 2026 presents an opportunity for him to earn more recognition as a versatile secondary option who can make plays both from the slot and out wide. Key roster battles The Panthers' decision to spend a third-round pick on wide receiver Chris Brazzell II appeared to put added pressure on former first-round pick Xavier Legette. Through two NFL seasons, Legette has been outproduced by Jalen Coker, who went undrafted in the same class, and Brazzell was set to provide another challenger for playing time. An early training camp injury is expected to cost Brazzell his rookie season, however, shifting the focus to whether John Metchie can push Legette for a starting role. Metchie has shown occasional flashes through his first three NFL seasons, but his career average of 1.03 yards per route run suggests he presents a less significant threat to Legette's role than Brazzell might have. Wide receiver depth is a concern: Drake London remains the clear No. 1 option, but Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus each posted PFF receiving grades below 60.0 in 2025. The PFF Early Bird Sale Is Here : Save 33% and get PFF+ for just $79.99, our lowest price of the year. through . --> Explore PFF Fantasy Tools EARLY BIRD SALE: SAVE 33% — the lowest price of the year (opens in new tab) After a difficult start to the 2025 season left them at 4-9 through 13 games, the Atlanta Falcons won their final four contests to finish tied for the best record in the NFC South, ultimately placing third on tiebreakers. Atlanta responded with sweeping changes, hiring Kevin Stefanski as its new head coach and adding Tua Tagovailoa to create competition at quarterback. Here is our 2026 preview for the Atlanta Falcons . Key Free Agency/Trade Additions Position Player 2025 PFF Grade WR Jahan Dotson 54.1 WR Olamide Zaccheaus 55.7 OT Wanya Morris 57.1 OT Jawaan Taylor 53.3 TE Austin Hooper 65.3 QB Tua Tagovailoa 62.1 QB Trevor Siemian N/A RB Brian Robinson 66.7 DI Chris Williams 58.7 DI Maason Smith 49.1 DI Da’Shawn Hand 59.3 EDGE Samson Ebukam 64.1 EDGE Azeez Ojulari 62.5 LB Christian Harris 54.8 S Sidney Brown 60.0 P Jake Bailey 75.1 K Nick Folk 91.3 Outside of Tua Tagovailoa at quarterback, the signing of right tackle Jawaan Taylor could have the biggest impact on Atlanta’s offense. Kaleb McGary retired after missing the entire 2025 season due to injury, leaving a significant hole along the offensive line. McGary earned a 73.8 PFF overall grade in 2024 and was always a stronger run blocker than pass protector, but Taylor provides a solid replacement after earning PFF pass-blocking grades of 69.5 and 67.3 over the past two seasons. Nick Folk will turn 42 during the 2026 season, but his performance has continued to improve. He has set career highs in PFF field goal grade in each of the past two seasons, including a 91.3 mark in 2025 that ranked seventh in the NFL. Folk missed just one kick all season and was perfect from inside 50 yards. 2026 NFL Draft Class Position Player 2025 PFF Grade CB Avieon Terrell 83.5 WR Zachariah Branch 82.0 LB Kendal Daniels 77.4 DI Anterio Thompson 76.0 LB Harold Perkins 62.4 OT Ethan Onianwa 58.2 Cornerback Avieon Terrell’s draft stock tumbled after a rough workout that included a 4.64-second 40-yard dash, leading to him still being available when the Falcons came on the clock in the second round. His college production paints a more encouraging picture, as Terrell earned PFF coverage grades above 75.0 in all three seasons and never allowed 400 or more receiving yards in coverage in a single year. Wide receiver Zachariah Branch was productive in his final season at Georgia , averaging 2.57 yards per route run and forcing 20 missed tackles on 81 receptions. His average depth of target was just 3.6 yards, though, with 51 of his targets coming behind the line of scrimmage. Branch still produced when given opportunities downfield, catching all five of his targets 20 or more yards downfield, making his usage in the NFL fascinating to watch given his college target profile. Reasons for optimism Bijan Robinson remains one of the best running backs in football and is coming off a season in which he forced 86 missed tackles — 19 more than any other player at the position during the 2025 regular season. He also became a bigger factor in the passing game, averaging 1.88 yards per route run. The QB Annual Is Live Every qualifying quarterback. Every metric that matters. PFF grades, passing splits, EPA per dropback, clutch performance, interception luck and more — all in one interactive guide built on the same data trusted by all 32 NFL teams. Read the QB Annual (opens in new tab) Get PFF+ (opens in new tab) Reason for pessimism The Falcons signed wide receiver Drake London to a long-term extension this offseason, with the former first-round pick out of USC having earned a PFF receiving grade above 85.0 in three of his first four NFL seasons. Despite missing time in 2025, London still earned an 89.9 PFF receiving grade, racked up 919 receiving yards and averaged 2.34 yards per route run. The concern is that Atlanta doesn’t have much else to get excited about at the position. Free-agent additions Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus both earned PFF receiving grades below 60.0 and averaged fewer than 1.00 yards per route run in 2025. They do have Kyle Pitts at tight end and Bijan Robinson at running back, who combined for 213 targets last year, but don’t be shocked to see rookie third-round draft pick Zachariah Brand finish fourth on this team in targets. Breakout Candidate Left guard Matthew Bergeron enters the final season of his rookie contract with an opportunity to earn a significant payday with a strong 2026 campaign. He has already played more than 3,000 snaps in his career and has earned PFF overall grades above 70.0 in back-to-back seasons. Bergeron has consistently graded better as a run blocker than in pass protection, but he has also earned PFF pass-blocking grades above 65.0 in each of the past two seasons. He allowed 28 pressures across 519 pass-blocking snaps in 2025. Key roster battles Quarterback Michael Penix Jr. regressed in his second NFL season, with his PFF overall grade dropping from 87.9 across 230 snaps as a rookie to 59.3 across 553 snaps before a season-ending knee injury in 2025. There are no guarantees he will return in time for the start of the regular season, giving Tua Tagovailoa the early edge in the quarterback competition. Tagovailoa also regressed in 2025, with his 62.1 PFF overall grade marking a career low. If Atlanta can get the 2023 version of Tagovailoa, who led the NFL with an 88.6 PFF passing grade and tied for seventh with a 5.8% big-time throw rate, Penix may not see the field in his third NFL season. Given what both quarterbacks have shown recently, though, it’s very possible that each starts multiple games in 2026. records.new_body: PFF Safety Rankings: The top 32 players ahead of the 2026 NFL season All NFL - current Fantasy College NFL Draft DFS Betting PFF Safety Rankings: The top 32 players ahead of the 2026 NFL season By Bradley Locker Posted Aug 7, 2026 6:15 am EDT Kyle Hamilton comes in No. 1: The Ravens star has been the league's highest-graded player at the position since his debut four years ago. The Rams wield three great players: Kamren Kinchens and Kamren Curl both sit inside the top 12, while Quentin Lake is also an underappreciated asset. The PFF Early Bird Sale Is Here : Save 33% and get PFF+ for just $79.99, our lowest price of the year. After cycling through every position on the field, PFF’s individual player rankings have now reached the final defensive spot: Safety. Game-changing safeties make their presence felt in a variety of ways, from ball-hawking coverage to surging run-defense to physically imposing tackles. The players near the top of the list below integrate all three, often from versatile alignments. 1. Kyle Hamilton , Baltimore Ravens Since Hamilton was picked 14 th overall in 2022, all he’s done is star in Baltimore. His 92.6 overall PFF grade is the league’s highest at the position, producing at least an 86.3 grade in all four years. Whether playing in center field, the box or slot, Hamilton has dominated no matter the assignment with his incredible instincts, closing speed and length. 2. Derwin James , Los Angeles Chargers James became the highest-paid safety in league history this offseason, and for good reason. He’s earned at least a 77.5 overall PFF grade in seven of his eight pro seasons, a remarkable feat given the position’s inconsistency and changing responsibilities. James has fully bounced back from a poor 2023, posting the fifth-best overall grade among his counterparts over the last two seasons. The four-time All-Pro is readily stamping his legacy as one of the best of the era. 3. Xavier McKinney , Green Bay Packers Paying safeties big money doesn’t always work out, but the Packers are sure happy they did so with McKinney. Since 2023, his 90.9 overall PFF grade trails just Hamilton, with his 94.9 PFF coverage grade the best in the league. McKinney actually added a new dimension to his game last season with a career-best 82.9 PFF run-defense grade, missing only 3.5% of his tackle attempts on the ground — the second-lowest figure in 2025. 4. Minkah Fitzpatrick , New York Jets After a dominant stretch in Pittsburgh that trailed off, Fitzpatrick returned to Miami and produced a much-needed rebound season. Fitzpatrick’s 81.9 overall PFF grade was the fifth-highest among qualifiers, and he was one of four safeties with a 78.0-plus PFF coverage and run-defense mark. Now on the Jets, the 29-year-old chess piece will look to keep pace on a defense with improved talent. 5. Brian Branch , Detroit Lions Branch falling to the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft still makes little sense, especially with how he’s fared as a pro. Since debuting, Branch has been the second-most valuable safety by PFF Wins Above Replacement , netting no worse than a 77.6 overall PFF grade every campaign. Although an Achilles tear cut his 2025 season short, Branch was dominant with 82.6-plus marks in run-defense, tackling and pass-rushing. The star will help lift a Lions defense aiming to get back to full strength. 6. Antoine Winfield Jr. , Tampa Bay Buccaneers Following an underwhelming 2024 campaign, Winfield responded nicely with a 74.4 overall PFF grade last season. His 4.2% missed tackle rate was the second-lowest among qualified safeties, and his 74.3 PFF coverage grade placed in the 92 nd percentile. The second-most valuable safety by WAR since he was drafted in 2020, Winfield remains a weapon for Todd Bowles in Tampa Bay. 7. Jalen Pitre , Houston Texans Pitre has continued to develop over his four years in Houston, and he reached his zenith in 2025 with an 83.6 overall PFF grade — ranking third among qualified safeties. Pitre has operated best in the slot, where his 68.9 passer rating allowed was the third-best among safeties with at least 100 such coverage snaps. He also regularly brings a presence in the run game with 79.5-plus PFF run-defense grades in each of the last two years. The future is bright for the hard-hitting 27-year-old on arguably the sport’s best defense. 8. Kevin Byard , New England Patriots Even as he nears age 33, Byard has remained a very strong player at a position where many crater with age. Byard has earned at least a 72.8 overall PFF grade in every year since 2021, an especially impressive achievement considering that’s come with three separate teams. Originally known for his coverage prowess, Byard has grown substantially in run defense, tying Branch for the best PFF run-defense grade since 2023 (91.2). The fourth-most valuable safety by WAR since 2020, Byard now reunites with head coach Mike Vrabel in New England as he looks to form a lockdown secondary possessing tons of other talent. 9. Jessie Bates III , Atlanta Falcons Bates has enjoyed a remarkable career, laying claim to three 80.0-plus-graded seasons since 2020 to place as the fifth-most valuable safety in the last six seasons. The only reason for concern is that his grade fell from 80.2 in 2024 to 64.5 in 2025, his lowest since 2019. Bates was a bit uncharacteristic in coverage with a career-worst 100.6 passer rating allowed, but a positive was his personal-best 6.6% missed tackle rate. Bates still carries a reputation as one of the sport’s best ballhawks with 29 career interceptions, but he’ll need to get back on track in 2026. 10. Kamren Kinchens , Los Angeles Rams Despite being a third-round pick in 2024, Kinchens has blossomed into one of the better players at his position. Over the last two years, his 79.4 overall PFF grade places seventh, and his 81.9 PFF coverage grade was the fourth-best among qualifiers in 2025. The third-year pro has All-Pro potential as he helps spearhead an improved Los Angeles secondary. 11. Bryan Cook , Cincinnati Bengals After three mediocre seasons in Kansas City, Cook broke out in earnest last year with an 83.3 overall PFF grade. His 83.0 PFF coverage grade was the third-highest at the position, and he also slotted 12 th in PFF run-defense grade (79.7) while missing only 5.7% of his tackle attempts. Now on the Bengals, Cook looks to revamp a Cincinnati defense that desperately seeks more playmaking in the second and third levels. 12. Kamren Curl , Los Angeles Rams Curl also flourished during the Rams’ spectacular 2025 season, posting a 77.8 overall PFF grade — his second 77.5-plus grade in the last four years. Curl’s 87.9 PFF run-defense grade was the second-best among safeties, and his 8.3% missed tackle rate was well above average. After signing an extension in Los Angeles, Curl will remain part of one of the NFL’s best secondaries next to his running mate Kinchens. 13. Antonio Johnson , Jacksonville Jaguars Johnson did a total about-face in 2025, going from one of the NFL’s worst to best safeties by overall PFF grade. Indeed, his 86.6 overall PFF grade was the highest among anyone at the position with 700 or more snaps. Johnson was particularly dynamic in coverage, amassing an 87.6 PFF coverage mark and allowing only a 53.4 passer rating on targets in his direction. The key for Johnson will be consistency as he enters his fourth season in pursuit of a lucrative extension. 14. Nick Emmanwori , Seattle Seahawks Although Emmanwori wasn’t a regular contributor for Seattle until Week 5, he burst onto the scene almost as fast as his 40-yard dash time. From that point until the Super Bowl, his 73.5 overall PFF grade was the 10 th -best among qualified safeties, including sitting seventh in PFF coverage grade (73.9). There’s no denying Emmanwori’s game-bending potential for the defending champs given his freakish skills as a hybrid defender, but slightly more consistency could help given that Emmanwori fell below a 61.0 overall grade in eight of his 17 rookie contests. 15. Talanoa Hufanga , Denver Broncos After being constrained by injuries the prior two seasons, Hufanga enjoyed a fruitful first campaign in Denver with a 70.9 overall PFF grade over a career-high 1,225 snaps. The second-team All-Pro was greatly impactful in coverage with a 24% forced incompletion rate — tied for second among safeties — and his 76.3 PFF run-defense grade sat in the 71 st percentile. The 14 th -most valuable safety by WAR since 2022, Hufanga is a quality player who just has to stay on the field more. 16. Kerby Joseph , Detroit Lions Joseph’s 2024 campaign was an unforgettable one, reaching a 90.7 overall PFF grade while combining for 21 interceptions and pass deflections. However, he couldn’t replicate that last season, playing to a 59.5 overall mark across only six games due to a lingering knee injury. If Joseph can stay healthy in 2026, he very well might shoot right back up this list and rekindle an elite duo with Branch in Detroit. 17. Julian Love , Seattle Seahawks Love has elevated himself in Seattle, placing fifth in overall PFF grade (86.5) over his three years with the Seahawks. Coverage has been a specific forte with 77.4-plus marks in each of those three campaigns. Love’s ranking is most explained by his substandard work against the run in 2025 (0.9% run stop rate) and playing only 634 total snaps due to a hamstring injury, but he’s a very valuable piece for the reigning champs and could be much higher in 2026 if he remains on the field this season. 18. Jaylinn Hawkins , Baltimore Ravens Hawkins turned in an outstanding season in 2025, placing 12 th among qualifiers on a career-high 74.9 overall PFF grade. The former Patriot was balanced, becoming one of six at the position with a 74.5-plus grade in both coverage and run defense. After heading to Baltimore this offseason, the 28-year-old is poised to create a high-upside trio with Hamilton and second-year talent Malaki Starks . 19. Coby Bryant , Chicago Bears Over the last two seasons, Bryant has played 1,948 snaps, an impressive number — especially given his 74.6 overall PFF grade during that duration. Although Bryant has never exceeded a 72.8 single-season mark, he’s been solid in both coverage and run defense, sitting in at least the 62 nd percentile in each since 2024. The new Chicago Bear will need to clean up his tackling a bit given his 18.7% miss rate tied for fifth-highest among qualifiers last season. 20. Jalen Thompson , Dallas Cowboys In each of the last five years, Thompson has played at least 938 snaps with no lower than a 65.0 overall PFF grade, a worthy measure of his consistent play. While Thompson didn’t produce anything more than a 69.2 grade in either coverage or run defense last year, he’s missed only 12 tackles since 2024 and has displayed aptitude in both aforementioned categories in 2023 and 2024. The longtime Cardinal is now in Dallas and looks to turn around one of the league’s worst defenses working next to rookie phenom Caleb Downs. 21. Evan Williams , Green Bay Packers Williams has continued to look like a steal since the Packers took him in the fourth round in 2024. Over his two pro seasons, Williams has churned out a 73.9 overall PFF grade, good for 16 th among qualifiers. He was especially fearless against the run in 2025 with an 85.6 PFF run-defense grade and 4.8% run stop rate. The next step is getting more measured in coverage after allowing 71.8% of his targets to be hauled in and forcing only one incompletion. 22. Justin Reid , New Orleans Saints Reid enjoyed a dynamite 2024 season with the Chiefs, earning a 78.2 overall PFF grade with 76.5-plus grades in all three major grading categories. His first year in New Orleans wasn’t quite on par, with his overall PFF grade falling to a 66.7. The main culprits were worse coverage and a higher missed tackle rate, although his run defense was still effective at a 77.0 mark. The Saints are relying on Reid to show his prior self this season, especially in one of the league’s youngest secondaries. 23. Jalen Ramsey , Pittsburgh Steelers After being traded to the Steelers last summer, Ramsey’s first season was eventful, including moving from cornerback to safety midseason. From Week 9 onward, Ramsey’s 60.0 overall PFF grade slotted 46 th out of 65 qualified safeties, although his 6.3% missed tackle rate and 75.9 PFF run-defense grade were above average. With Patrick Graham installing a new defensive system in 2026, Ramsey is expected to operate more in the slot, which could mirror more of his peak version with the Rams in 2021-22. The 31-year-old is a decorated player, not far removed from a great season and someone who still possesses strong instincts and downhill ability, but his skill in coverage is a bit of a concern. 24. Alohi Gilman , Kansas City Chiefs Playing with both the Chargers and Ravens last year, Gilman produced a solid 70.3 overall PFF grade, headlined by a 72.0 PFF coverage mark. Since 2023, Gilman also ranks 16 th among safeties in PFF WAR, although his grades over the last two years haven’t matched his elite 86.1 mark in 2023. Now in Kansas City, Gilman will bring his pass-first approach to a defense aiming to replace Cook and multiple key members of its defensive backfield. 25. Brandon Jones , Denver Broncos Jones was quietly phenomenal in both 2023 and 2024 with 75.4-plus overall PFF grades, but that number slipped to a 64.3 last season. Jones’ coverage was the primary issue, with his PFF coverage grade declining to a 60.6 due to breaking up fewer passes and allowing over three more yards per reception on average. The 28-year-old could be due for a bounce-back season in a Denver secondary that returns its tremendous core. 26. Xavier Watts , Atlanta Falcons Watts quickly turned into an impressive player as a rookie, securing a 72.2 overall PFF grade while operating on 1,093 snaps. The coverage maestro from Notre Dame kept it up as a pro with a 72.7 grade in that category, including snagging five interceptions and tying for 11 th with a 17% forced incompletion rate. If Watts can pair better run-defense work with his efforts in coverage, he’ll rise this list in no time. 27. Craig Woodson , New England Patriots A fellow mid-round pick last April, Woodson similarly made his mark for New England off the bat. His 72.2 overall PFF grade tied Watts, although it was more heavily skewed by his positional-best 89.7 PFF run-defense grade. If Woodson takes strides in coverage — where his underlying metrics show promise — then he and Byard should form a premier tandem for the Patriots in 2026. 28. Ronnie Hickman Jr. , Cleveland Brown s Hickman has played just 1,827 snaps over his three-year career, but he’s looked good when on the field with a 75.7 overall PFF grade. Likewise, Hickman’s 78.7 PFF coverage grade is the ninth-best among qualifiers since 2023. Hickman’s status for 2026 and beyond is somewhat up in the air as he enters a contract season — and with the Browns nabbing second-round safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren — but the 24-year-old is a promising player who can unlock another level by getting more consistent against the run. 29. Camryn Bynum , Indiana polis Colts One of the league’s most dazzling celebration artists, Bynum has reason to keep dancing. He’s earned at least a 70.0 overall PFF grade in two of the past three campaigns, and he’s remained durable by appearing on no fewer than 1,056 snaps in each of the last four seasons. Bynum’s 6% missed tackle rate was the eighth-lowest in his first year with the Colts, and his 67.7 PFF coverage grade placed in the 83 rd percentile as well. 30. Quentin Lake , Los Angeles Rams Lake can get overshadowed on a team full of stars, but he’s actually been responsible for the fourth-most WAR of any safety since 2023. Lake’s 83.6 PFF run-defense grade places 13 th at the position over the last three years, but his 62.7 PFF coverage grade hasn’t been as stout. Also holding Lake back is the fact that he’s never exceeded a 71.7 overall single-season grade, but the former sixth-round pick remains a plus contributor in the slot for Sean McVay’s defense. 31. Calen Bullock , Houston Texans Bullock has quickly anointed himself as a starter in Houston, appearing on 2,188 snaps over his two-year career. He showed nice development in his second season with an 85.6 PFF run-defense grade and by cutting his missed tackle rate in more than half, although his overall PFF grade was just a 69.4. While Bullock’s 50% catch rate and 35.4 snaps per reception were among the league’s best for safeties, his 14.8 yards per reception was the seventh-worst among qualifiers, and he only ranked in the 67 th percentile in PFF coverage grade at free safety. If Bullock can avoid more big plays on a limited target share, he’ll grow even further. 32. Budda Baker , Arizona Cardinals An eight-time Pro Bowler, Baker is a well-respected player — but one whose advanced statistics paint a more cloudy picture. Baker has sat below a 65.0 overall PFF grade in two of the past three seasons, and his coverage was especially liable last year. Indeed, Baker’s 35.7 PFF coverage grade was the third-lowest among qualifiers, giving up a 119.6 passer rating when targeted. Also worrisome for Baker was a career-high 17% missed tackle rate. The 30-year-old is still a formidable run defender, but his coverage acumen may not project well for the close of his career. records.new_body: College Football: Top 10 quarterback rooms heading into the 2026 season All NFL Fantasy College - current NFL Draft DFS Betting College Football: Top 10 quarterback rooms heading into the 2026 season By Max Chadwick Posted Aug 7, 2026 6:00 am EDT Oregon has the best quarterback room in the country: Dante Moore is a top-three quarterback in the nation, while Dylan Raiola is the best backup in college football. Ohio State comes in second: Julian Sayin is back after being a Heisman finalist, and Tavien St. Clair was a top-five recruit in the 2025 class. The PFF Early Bird Sale Is Here : Save 33% and get PFF+ for just $79.99, our lowest price of the year. We’re a few weeks away from the 2026 college football season. With that, it’s time to rank the 10 best position units. First up is quarterback rooms. While having a good starting quarterback is critical, teams must possess capable backups in case the starter goes down with an injury or is struggling. Below is a list of PFF’s top-10 quarterback rooms in college football. 1. Oregon Dante Moore returned to Oregon despite being a projected top-three pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. He enters his redshirt junior year as our No. 2 quarterback in the country after tossing 30 big-time throws in 2025, the most in the FBS. Behind Moore is Dylan Raiola, a former five-star recruit who started the last two years at Nebraska . He’s likely a top-40 quarterback in America right now and is expected to become Oregon ’s starter in 2027. 2. Ohio State The Buckeyes’ quarterback room is home to the best signal-caller in the sport in Julian Sayin. He completed 77% of his passes in 2025, the third-highest rate in college football history. Behind Sayin is redshirt freshman Tavien St. Clair, the No. 4 overall recruit from the 2025 class and a quarterback who would start for many Power Four schools right now. 3. Ole Miss Trinidad Chambliss was a revelation for Ole Miss last season, posting the fourth-most big-time throws in the entire FBS (29). He enters 2026 as the No. 4 quarterback in college football. Chambliss needed to win an injunction against the NCAA this offseason in order to receive another year of eligibility. While the Rebels were waiting for that verdict, they formed a contingency plan by bringing in Auburn transfer Deuce Knight. The former five-star recruit was stellar in his lone start as a true freshman, tallying six total touchdowns against Mercer . 4. Texas Arch Manning enters the 2026 season as the favorite to be the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft and our No. 3 quarterback in the sport. His 87.3 PFF grade in 2025 was a top-15 mark in the nation. Behind Manning is redshirt freshman Karle Lacey Jr., a former top-20 quarterback recruit, and MJ Morris, a player who made starts for two separate Power Four schools in Maryland and NC State . The Longhorns also added a five-star true freshman in Dia Bell, who won Elite 11 MVP in 2025. 5. LSU The Tigers’ placement in the top five of this list is thanks to three incoming transfers. The headliner is Sam Leavitt ( Arizona State ), who’s our No. 8 quarterback in America. His 87.8 PFF grade since 2024 is seventh among returning Power Four quarterbacks. Redshirt freshman Husan Longstreet comes in via USC and was a five-star recruit in the 2025 class. Landen Clark also transferred in from Elon and posted an impressive 84.2 PFF grade as a redshirt freshman last year. through . --> Read more Read more College Football: The top 10 returning quarterbacks for the 2026 season By Max Chadwick (opens in new tab) → 6. Notre Dame CJ Carr enters his redshirt sophomore season as the betting favorite to win the Heisman Trophy and our No. 5 quarterback in the nation. His 6.5% big-time throw rate last year was sixth in the Power Four. He’s the main reason why the Fighting Irish are on this list. Backup Blake Hebert was a three-star recruit, as was freshman Noah Grubbs. Teddy Jarrard enters his freshman campaign as a former four-star recruit. 7. Miami (FL) Miami will be starting a transfer at quarterback for the third year in a row. Darian Mensah ( Duke ) will try to fill the big shoes left behind by Cam Ward and Carson Beck , but he’s more than capable of doing so. Mensah led the Power Four last year with 3,951 passing yards and enters 2026 as our No. 6 quarterback in the nation. The Hurricanes also have a couple of former four-star recruits in their room in redshirt freshman Luke Nickel and true freshman Dereon Coleman. 8. USC Jayden Maiava is entering his second full season as USC ’s starting quarterback and is our No. 7 signal-caller in the country. He was fifth in the FBS last year in passing yards (3,711) and the only one in the top five to play fewer than 14 games. Maiava’s 86.2 PFF grade was also 10th in the Power Four. Behind him are Sam Huard, a five-star recruit in 2021, and Jonas Williams, the No. 8 quarterback recruit in the 2026 class. 9. California Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele is coming off a stellar freshman campaign and is already a top-10 quarterback in the sport. His 28 big-time throws last year were fifth in the Power Four. Backing him up is Colorado State transfer Jackson Brousseau, who started eight games for the Rams last season. 10. Georgia Gunner Stockton is a top-15 quarterback in America and was highly efficient last year while leading the Bulldogs to an SEC championship. His 81.2% adjusted completion rate was second only to Sayin in the Power Four. Georgia has three former four-star recruits behind Stockton in redshirt sophomore Ryan Puglisi, redshirt freshman Ryan Montgomery and true freshman Bryson Beaver. records.new_body: PFF Cornerback Rankings: The top 32 players entering the 2026 NFL season All NFL - current Fantasy College NFL Draft DFS Betting PFF Cornerback Rankings: The top 32 players entering the 2026 NFL season By Dalton Wasserman Posted Aug 7, 2026 5:45 am EDT Devon Witherspoon leads the way: The reigning champion was the league's highest-graded corner, in part due to his versatile talent. The Patriots have a terrific trio: Christian Gonzalez , Carlton Davis III and Marcus Jones all sit in the top 20 of the rankings. The PFF Early Bird Sale Is Here : Save 33% and get PFF+ for just $79.99, our lowest price of the year. PFF's offseason NFL positional rankings continue with cornerbacks. Between lockdown players on the outside and disruptive options on the interior, the position is ripe with tons of young talent. 1. Devon Witherspoon , Seattle Seahawks Witherspoon finished 2025 as the NFL’s highest-graded cornerback. He played a career-high 461 snaps on the outside, but remains a versatile piece who can man the slot when needed. He recorded one interception, eight pass breakups and 13 pressures, including a sack in the Super Bowl last season. All of that production, combined with the fact that he’s an elite run defender, makes Witherspoon one of the most valuable players in the NFL. 2. Sauce Gardner , Indianapolis Colts Gardner traversed through a wild 2025 season in which he dealt with injuries and was traded from New York to Indianapolis. His play when on the field was still quite admirable. Gardner’s 75.6 PFF coverage grade tied for 15th among qualified cornerbacks. He also earned a career-high 84.5 PFF run-defense grade that ranked fourth among that same group. A fully healthy Gardner could change the complexion of the entire Colts defense. 3. Pat Surtain II , Denver Broncos Surtain didn’t quite reach the heights of his Defensive Player of the Year-winning 2024 campaign last season, but he still played very well while accruing at least 1,000 snaps for the fourth straight year. His 73.3 PFF grade ranked 22nd among all qualified cornerbacks. He also tallied 10 pass breakups and hauled in one interception. Surtain will continue to be the headliner for one of the league’s elite secondaries. 4. Trent McDuffie , Los Angeles Rams The Rams paid a hefty price to acquire McDuffie, and a dive into the metrics makes it easy to see why. Since he was drafted in 2022, McDuffie’s 90.2 PFF coverage grade ranks second in the NFL behind fellow 2022 draftee Sauce Gardner . Last season, he earned a 74.7 coverage grade that ranked 18th among qualified cornerbacks while tallying one interception and four pass breakups. 5. Cooper DeJean , Philadelphia Eagles DeJean became an extremely valuable piece of Philadelphia’s defense the moment he stepped on the field for them in 2024. Since he was drafted, DeJean’s 87.1 PFF grade trails only Devon Witherspoon for the best in the NFL. In 2025, he reeled in two interceptions while tying for second in the NFL with 14 pass breakups, postseason included. DeJean should continue to lock down the slot this season for the Eagles. 6. Quinyon Mitchell , Philadelphia Eagles Mitchell has quickly become one of the NFL’s best corners during his first two seasons. His 84.5 PFF grade since the start of 2024 ranks third in the NFL behind Witherspoon and teammate DeJean. While racking up two interceptions and eight pass breakups last season, Mitchell allowed a 54.4 passer rating as the primary coverage defender, which was the second-lowest mark among qualified cornerbacks. 7. Derek Stingley Jr. , Houston Texans Stingley experienced a bit of a volatile 2025 campaign in coverage last season, but his elite ball skills still allowed him to tally four interceptions and nine pass breakups. His 73.5 PFF coverage grade ranked 23rd among all qualified cornerbacks. Over the past three years, Stingley slots second among qualified cornerbacks with a 90.3 coverage grade. He and Kamari Lassiter make a good case to be labeled the NFL’s best cornerback duo. 8. Christian Gonzalez , New England Patriots Gonzalez has become one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL. Among qualified corners last year, including the postseason, Gonzalez ranked 12th in coverage grade, fourth in pass breakups and fourth in passer rating allowed as the primary coverage defender. He also missed just one tackle in 18 games last season. Still just 24 years old, Gonzalez should be the headliner in New England’s secondary for years to come. 9. Kamari Lassiter , Houston Texans Lassiter was immediately made a starter after being selected in the second round of the 2024 draft, and he’s done nothing but play at a high level since. Over the past two seasons, he’s earned an 82.1 PFF grade that ranks seventh among all qualified cornerbacks. He recorded four interceptions and 14 pass breakups last season while making major positive strides in run defense. Lassiter is quietly becoming one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL. 10. Mike Jackson , Carolina Panthers In a matter of just two seasons, Jackson has gone from an afterthought in Seattle to being arguably the Panthers’ best defensive player. Last season, he earned an 85.8 PFF coverage grade that led all cornerback who played at least 300 coverage snaps. Postseason included, he paced Carolina with five interceptions and 11 pass breakups last season. 11. Jamel Dean , Pittsburgh Steelers After seven successful seasons in Tampa Bay, Dean will take his talents to Pittsburgh on the heels of an excellent 2025 campaign. He produced a career-high 80.6 PFF grade while tallying three interceptions, one pass breakup and two forced fumbles. Dean also allowed a passer rating of 47.7 into his coverage, which was the lowest mark among qualified cornerbacks in the NFL. 12. Christian Benford , Buffalo Bills Benford endured a turbulent 2025 in which he played to a career-low 53.9 PFF coverage grade. Across the two prior seasons, he recorded an 87.1 coverage grade that was the fourth-best mark among qualified cornerbacks, so there is reason to think he can bounce back. On the bright side, Benford tied for the NFL lead among cornerbacks with a 90.1 PFF run-defense grade last season. 13. Ja’Quan McMillian , Denver Broncos McMillian was the highest-graded primary slot cornerback in the NFL last season. His 80.8 PFF grade ranked fourth among all qualified cornerbacks. Including the postseason, he accrued three interceptions, three pass breakups, two forced fumbles and four sacks. His versatility allows Denver to execute a variety of schemes at a very high level. 14. Jaylon Johnson , Chicago Bears Johnson was limited to just nine games, including the postseason, in 2025 due to injury. He wasn’t quite right all season as he earned a mediocre 60.3 PFF coverage grade, his lowest since 2021. However, Johnson was the highest-graded cornerback in the NFL in 2023 and turned in a fine season in 2024. He’s a prime bounce-back candidate in Chicago’s secondary this season. 15. Jaylen Watson , Los Angeles Rams Watson joins ex-Chiefs teammate Trent McDuffie in Los Angeles this season on the heels of his highest-graded campaign to date. His 74.1 PFF grade ranked 18th among qualified cornerbacks in 2025. While he did pick off two passes and break up three others, it was Watson’s work in the run game that really stood out. Watson’s 83.5 PFF run-defense grade ranked sixth among all qualified cornerbacks. 16. Carlton Davis III , New England Patriots Davis ranked 19th among qualifiers with a 74.0 PFF grade last season, and he was a major reason for New England’s success down the stretch in the playoffs. From Week 11 through the Super Bowl, his 87.3 PFF grade placed third in the NFL as he collected two interceptions and a league-leading 10 pass breakups. Davis, Gonzalez and Marcus Jones enter 2026 as one of the NFL’s premier cornerback trios. 17. DJ Turner II , Cincinnati Bengals Turner produced a breakout season in 2025 that saw him rank seventh among qualified cornerbacks with a 78.1 PFF coverage grade. His ball skills were on display, as he racked up 13 pass breakups, tied for second-most in the NFL during the regular season. While his run defense lags a bit behind, Turner’s coverage prowess is now a core component of Cincinnati’s defensive success. 18. Joey Porter Jr. , Pittsburgh Steelers Porter earned a career-high 76.6 PFF coverage grade last season that ranked 13th among all qualified cornerbacks. Including the playoffs, he tallied 13 pass breakups, which tied for the fourth-highest total in the NFL. Porter also allowed just a 55.9 passer rating as the primary coverage defender, third-lowest among qualified cornerbacks behind new teammate Dean and Mitchell. 19. Marcus Jones , New England Patriots Jones continues to get better with each passing season. In 2025, he compiled a career-high 74.2 PFF coverage grade that ranked 20th among qualified cornerbacks. Jones also stuffed the stat sheet with four interceptions, seven pass breakups, three sacks and a forced fumble. He’ll continue to be a mainstay as New England’s slot cornerback and primary punt returner this season. 20. Denzel Ward , Cleveland Brown s Ward’s production saw a bit of a dropoff in 2025 after he led the NFL with 17 pass breakups in 2024. He collected just one interception and four pass breakups last season, but Ward has an excellent track record that could foreshadow a bounceback. He has long been up to the task of covering the NFL’s top wide receivers. 21. Jourdan Lewis , Jacksonville Jaguars Lewis has been one of the NFL’s more productive slot cornerbacks over the past two seasons in particular. Since the start of 2024, his 78.7 PFF coverage grade ranks 12th among cornerbacks who have played at least 400 coverage snaps. During that time, he’s amassed three interceptions, nine pass breakups and 44 total stops. A return to full health and an even more defined role in the slot should allow Lewis to have another productive season. 22. Isaiah Rodgers , Minnesota Vikings Rodgers finally got a starting opportunity in 2025 and took full advantage of it. His 74.1 PFF coverage grade ranked 21st among qualified cornerbacks. He’s now earned at least a 70.0 coverage grade in all five seasons that he’s played in his career. The highlight of Rodgers’ 2025 season came in Week 3 against the Cincinnati Bengals , when he scored two defensive touchdowns and earned the first 99.9 game grade in PFF history. 23. D.J. Reed , Detroit Lions Reed recorded a career-low 61.3 PFF coverage grade in his first season in Detroit, but that’s tilted downward a bit due to two tough games against the Packers and Rams. Prior to 2025, Reed had secured at least a 70.0 coverage grade in six straight campaigns. Considering the Lions’ lack of cornerback depth, a bounceback from Reed could be vital to their postseason aspirations. 24. Charvarius Ward , Indianapolis Colts Ward was limited to just seven appearances in 2025 due to concussion issues, but he was quite productive when he was on the field. His 77.4 PFF coverage grade ranked ninth among qualified cornerbacks last season, and he broke up seven passes in those seven games. Assuming he is fully healthy this season, Ward and Gardner could form one of the NFL’s best cornerback duos. 25. A.J. Terrell , Atlanta Falcons Terrell struggled a bit more than usual in coverage in 2025, but still showed flashes of playmaking ability. During the regular season, he led Atlanta and tied for eighth in the NFL with 10 pass breakups. He was also one of just 12 cornerbacks who forced multiple fumbles. Yet Terrell tied for the regular-season lead with 12 penalties, so he could be in line for a rebound if he can cut that total down. 26. Eric Stokes , Las Vegas Raiders Stokes turned in a career-high 75.0 PFF grade last season that ranked second among qualified Raiders defenders behind Maxx Crosby . His 75.2 PFF coverage grade slotted 17th among qualified cornerbacks. While he didn’t reel in any interceptions, Stokes did not allow more than 50 yards in any individual game last season, which says a lot considering the lack of production from the rest of Las Vegas’ defense. 27. Garrett Williams , Arizona Cardinals Williams endured a tough 2025 that was marred by injuries and ultimately curtailed due to a torn Achilles. Assuming he can return to full strength, Williams showed in 2024 that he can be one of the best slot cornerbacks in the NFL. That year, he ranked fourth among qualified cornerbacks with an 83.7 PFF coverage grade while picking off two passes and breaking up six others. That level of production would be a huge boon for a Cardinals secondary that carries major cornerback uncertainty. 28. Jaycee Horn , Carolina Panthers Horn comprises one half of perhaps the NFL’s most underrated cornerback duo in Carolina. While the past two seasons haven’t been consistently great from a grading perspective, Horn still shows off his playmaking ability in spurts, as evidenced by his five interceptions last season. He’s also played over 1,000 snaps in two consecutive years, which is encouraging given the durability issues earlier in his career. 29. Rasul Douglas , Washington Commanders After enduring some struggles in Buffalo in 2024, the veteran Douglas returned to proper form in Miami in 2025, ranking 26th among qualified cornerbacks with a 72.6 PFF coverage grade. He hauled in two interceptions while tying a career-high with nine pass breakups. The soon-to-be 31-year-old is a nice reinforcement to a very young Washington cornerback unit. 30. Tarheeb Still , Los Angeles Chargers Still’s consistency and versatility have been valuable additions to the Chargers’ defense during his first two seasons in the NFL. Since the start of 2024, his 75.3 PFF coverage grade ranks 17th among cornerbacks who have played at least 400 coverage snaps. During that time, Still has lined up outside on 985 snaps and in the slot on 532 snaps. If he can improve his tackling a bit in 2026, Still could find himself even higher on this list at season’s end. 31. Kool-Aid McKinstry , New Orleans Saints McKinstry has begun to establish himself as a reliable player in New Orleans’ secondary. His 71.4 PFF coverage grade ranked 29th among qualified cornerbacks last season. Likewise, McKinstry’s 12 pass breakups were the sixth-most in the NFL during the regular season, and he led the Saints with three interceptions. Another positive step in McKinstry’s development could turn the Saints’ secondary into one of the league’s better units. 32. Keisean Nixon , Green Bay Packers Nixon finished 2025 ranked 15th in PFF WAR among cornerbacks. A key component in that is that he tied for second among all cornerbacks with 13 pass breakups during the regular season. The biggest drawback in Nixon’s game right now is that he commits too many penalties. Including the postseason, he tied for the NFL lead with 13 of them. On a down-to-down basis, though, Nixon has become the Packers ’ best cornerback. records.new_body: 2026 NFL Hall of Fame Game Recap: Immediate fantasy football takeaways from Panthers vs. Cardinals All NFL Fantasy - current College NFL Draft DFS Betting 2026 NFL Hall of Fame Game Recap: Immediate fantasy football takeaways from Panthers vs. Cardinals By Nathan Jahnke Posted Aug 6, 2026 9:41 pm EDT Bam Knight starts for the Arizona Cardinals : Knight was a focal point of the Arizona offense, and the broadcast made it clear he has a shot at the third running back spot on the depth chart. Ja’Tavion Sanders plays for the Carolina Panthers : The receiving tight end played despite an injury early in the week and other important players resting for Carolina. The PFF Early Bird Sale Is Here : Save 33% and get PFF+ for just $79.99, our lowest price of the year. PFF's fantasy football recap focuses on player usage and stats, breaking down all the vital information you need to gain an edge in 2026. And with fantasy draft season approaching, there’s no better time to get access to the full suite of PFF tools and data. The PFF Early Bird Sale is back, giving new subscribers the opportunity to save 33% on an annual PFF+ subscription and pay just $79.99 (regularly $119.99). PFF+ gives you everything you need to draft smarter and stay ahead all season, including exclusive player grades, Premium Stats, fantasy tools, betting dashboards and expert analysis built on the same data trusted by NFL teams. Carolina Panthers @ Arizona Cardinals Ja’Tavion Sanders starts for the Panthers : Once a popular fantasy sleeper pick, Sanders no longer appears to be a lock to make the Panthers roster. Last season, Sanders split time with Tommy Tremble when both were healthy. He played 77% of the Panthers’ third-down snaps but only 35.5% of their early-down snaps in 11 personnel and 31.4% in 12 personnel, with Mitchell Evans playing ahead of him in those situations. More concerningly, Sanders fell to third on the Panthers’ unofficial depth chart behind Evans despite playing more than him last season. Tremble was among the starters held out of this game, while Evans did not play after being carted off the field during practice last week, though his injury does not appear to be serious. Sanders also suffered an ankle injury Tuesday, but players who suffer even minor injuries during training camp are typically held out of the following preseason game. Despite that, Sanders played every snap on the opening drive. Veterans James Mitchell and Feleipe Franks took over to start the second drive, with Sanders returning for just one play. Sanders did not play after that drive, while several other players who started the game remained on the field. Sanders could still make the roster and carve out a role as a third-down specialist, but his usage suggests he is unlikely to play as much as he did last season. He is already only a consensus top-45 fantasy tight end for 2026, and even that ranking may prove too optimistic. The Carolina Panthers adjust without Chris Brazzell II : The Panthers’ third-round pick underwent surgery on his torn LCL a week ago, ruling him out for the season. Carolina’s top two wide receiver spots are locked in with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , both of whom sat out tonight. Brazzell was expected to compete with Xavier Legette for the No. 3 receiver role, but his injury makes Legette the clear favorite for the job. Legette also suffered an injury in practice earlier this week and did not play, though head coach Dave Canales said he would have been held out regardless because the starters were not playing. That put the spotlight on Carolina’s backups, as there could be a significant opportunity for another receiver if one of the top three misses time this season. Hunter Renfrow ranked fourth among the Panthers’ wide receivers in routes and targets last season but was not re-signed. Brycen Tremayne , Jimmy Horn Jr. and David Moore were next on the team in routes run, while John Metchie III joined Carolina in free agency after finishing the 2025 season as a starter for the New York Jets . The Panthers had a clear usage pattern in 11 personnel, with Moore at X, Tremayne at Z and Metchie in the slot. Metchie has a good chance to make the roster and would be the most likely beneficiary if Coker misses time. Moore could also have a path to increased playing time if Carolina wants to use McMillan more frequently in the slot or if McMillan suffers an injury. Horn appears to be the odd man out of the group. He not only failed to play with the top receivers available for this game, but he also wasn’t initially part of the next group, with Metchie continuing to work from the slot alongside different combinations of outside receivers. Horn also wasn’t among the Panthers’ primary kick returners early in the game. Unless Carolina keeps seven wide receivers or injuries create another opening, Horn appears unlikely to make the 53-man roster. Bam Knight starts for Arizona and has a chance to make the roster: Knight is currently fifth on the depth chart, but he has a chance to be named RB3 on the depth chart. Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier were among the key Cardinals who did not play. James Conner isn’t on the PUP list, but he has held himself out of team drills, which contributed to his absence from this game. Trey Benson was also held out after dealing with knee discomfort earlier in the week. That left Knight as the starter. He played all 15 snaps on the Cardinals’ opening drive and continued to see action later in the first half. Both the pregame show and game broadcast mentioned Knight as a candidate for the No. 3 running back job. That role typically requires special-teams contributions, and while Knight has limited regular-season experience there, he has still logged more professional special-teams snaps than Conner or Benson. Knight did little in this game to either help or hurt his chances of making the roster. Playing deep into the second quarter typically isn’t an encouraging sign, but the Cardinals had only two other healthy running backs available, including Evan Hull , who had been with the team for just three days. Arizona’s running back depth will be worth monitoring, particularly because Conner or Benson could become trade candidates if another team needs help at the position before the season. Miscellaneous Notes Arizona rested several key players for this game, including quarterbacks Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew , running backs Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier , wide receivers Michael Wilson , Marvin Harrison Jr. and Kendrick Bourne , and tight end Trey McBride . Head coach Mike LaFleur spent the past three seasons as the Los Angeles Rams ’ offensive coordinator, where the team had a policy of resting its starters throughout the preseason. The Cardinals may have held out so many players because this was the Hall of Fame Game, but LaFleur’s history suggests we may not see some of them until the regular season. Jalen Brooks and Simi Fehoko were the main wide receivers, with Xavier Weaver joining them in three-receiver sets. It’s unlikely all three make the roster, given that four wide receivers sat out and fifth-round rookie Reggie Virgil is likely to make the roster. While James Conner isn’t on the PUP list, he has held himself out of team drills, which contributed to his absence from this game. Cardinals running back Trey Benson was dealing with knee discomfort earlier in the week, which kept him out of tonight’s game. Third-year tight end Tip Reiman remains on the PUP list with an ankle injury. Carolina running back Jonathon Brooks did not play in this game. It’s unclear whether the Panthers view him similarly to the other key starters who were rested or were simply being cautious with his return after he missed all of last season. Tight end Ja’Tavion Sanders suffered an ankle injury on Tuesday. He notably fell to third on the Panthers unofficial depth chart behind Mitchell Evans . Evans was carted off the field during practice last week , but the injury doesn’t appear to be serious. Other Carolina players who rested for this game included quarterback Bryce Young , running back Chuba Hubbard and tight end Tommy Tremble . Continuity is the offseason strategy: Jacksonville made few major additions after winning the AFC South and closing the regular season on an eight-game winning streak. Their season ended with a home wild-card loss to the Buffalo Bills , but the way they finished the regular season provides plenty of optimism heading into 2026, particularly after Trevor Lawrence ‘s strong play down the stretch. Here's our 2026 preview of the Jacksonville Jaguars . Key Free Agency/Trade Additions Position Player 2025 PFF Grade HB Chris Rodriguez Jr. 73.4 DI Ruke Orhorhoro 37.3 CB Dane Jackson N/A G Trystan Colon 47.5 HB Ameer Abdullah 70.5 The Jaguars' approach to the offseason suggests they have confidence in the roster they assembled in 2025, as they did not add a projected starter and instead focused on improving their depth. Ruke Orhorhoro is one of the more intriguing additions as a reclamation project after a disappointing second season with the Falcons . He generated 30 pressures on 390 pass-rushing snaps but struggled badly against the run, with his 30.1 PFF run-defense grade tied for the third lowest among qualifying interior defenders. Still, he will not turn 25 until the middle of the season, leaving room for further development. Running back Chris Rodriguez Jr. could have the biggest impact among Jacksonville's free-agent additions. Across his three NFL seasons, 3.6 of his 4.6 career yards per carry have come after contact, highlighting his ability to create yards on his own. With Travis Etienne Jr. no longer on the roster and Bhayshul Tuten carrying the ball just 87 times as a rookie, Rodriguez has a realistic path to carving out a meaningful role in the Jaguars' backfield. 2026 NFL Draft Class Position Player 2025 PFF Grade TE Nate Boerkircher 74.6 DI Albert Regis 72.2 G Emmanuel Pregnon 87.0 S Jalen Huskey 83.6 LB Wesley Williams 71.9 TE Tanner Koziol 78.9 WR Josh Cameron 72.4 WR CJ Williams 76.5 EDGE Zach Durfee 77.4 LB Parker Hughes 74.7 The Jaguars drew plenty of criticism for selecting tight end Nate Boerkircher in the second round, given where he ranked on many consensus draft boards. However, the tight end position came off the board earlier than many expected throughout the draft. Boerkircher earned a 72.2 PFF run-blocking grade in his final season at Texas A M and dropped just two passes during his college career, though he never topped 24 targets in a season. Guard Emmanuel Pregnon is coming off the best season of his college career, posting an 86.3 PFF run-blocking grade and an 88.1 PFF pass-blocking grade while allowing just five pressures on 471 pass-blocking snaps. He will turn 25 during his rookie season, which likely contributed to his slide in the draft, but don't be surprised if he earns a starting role at some point over the next few seasons. Reasons for optimism Trevor Lawrence is coming off the best season of his NFL career, setting career highs with an 83.7 PFF overall grade and an 80.5 PFF passing grade. His overall mark ranked seventh among quarterbacks, but from Week 13 onward he was the highest-graded passer in the league with a 92.6 PFF grade. During that stretch, Lawrence posted a 7.7% big-time throw rate, tied for the third highest in the NFL, while his 1.5% turnover-worthy play rate ranked fourth lowest. Lawrence's late-season surge coincided with the arrival of Jakobi Meyers at the trade deadline, giving Jacksonville a much stronger receiving corps. Meyers, Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. earned PFF receiving grades of 73.2, 85.1 and 66.6, respectively. Their presence also allows second-year player Travis Hunter to spend more time at cornerback, where he was more effective as a rookie, earning a 73.2 PFF grade compared to a 62.2 mark at wide receiver. Center Robert Hainsey earned a PFF pass-blocking grade below 60.0 and ranked 34th among the 40 centers who played at least 300 snaps, while right guard Patrick Mekari also finished below the 60.0 mark, ranking 67th out of 81 qualifying guards. Jacksonville is in much better shape at both tackle spots, but the interior of the offensive line projects as one of the weaker units in the NFL entering 2026. Breakout Candidate Parker Washington thrived in an expanded role after Travis Hunter's injury, though his breakout season was somewhat overshadowed by the arrival of Jakobi Meyers at the trade deadline. Washington averaged 2.19 yards per route run in 2025, 0.61 more than any other Jaguars pass-catcher. He also caught fire down the stretch, recording 507 receiving yards over Jacksonville's final five games, including the playoffs—more than double any of his teammates during that span. Key roster battles Given Patrick Mekari ‘s struggles at right guard, it is fair to wonder whether Wyatt Millum can force his way into the starting conversation before the season begins. The 89th overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft made the transition from tackle in college to guard in the NFL and showed encouraging flashes as a rookie, earning a 75.0 PFF grade across 111 snaps. While 34 of those snaps came as an extra tight end, one of the more intriguing storylines this preseason will be whether Millum gets an opportunity to work with the first-team offense at guard. Notably, 37 of his 42 preseason snaps as a rookie came at tackle. records.new_body: Indianapolis Colts 2026 preview: Sauce Gardner, Laiatu Latu give Indianapolis a promising defensive foundation All NFL - current Fantasy College NFL Draft DFS Betting Indianapolis Colts 2026 preview: Sauce Gardner, Laiatu Latu give Indianapolis a promising defensive foundation By Gordon McGuinness Posted Aug 6, 2026 11:31 am EDT Indianapolis Colts Daniel Jones is under the microscope: The Colts are betting the veteran quarterback can provide the consistency needed to end a two-year playoff drought. Josh Downs is positioned for a breakout: Michael Pittman's departure opens the door for the fourth-year receiver to take on a significantly larger role. The PFF Early Bird Sale Is Here : Save 33% and get PFF+ for just $79.99, our lowest price of the year. through . --> Explore PFF Fantasy Tools EARLY BIRD SALE: SAVE 33% — the lowest price of the year (opens in new tab) The Colts raced out to an 8-2 start in 2025, but a seven-game losing streak to close the season left them at 8-9 for the second consecutive year. They made a blockbuster move during the season by acquiring cornerback Sauce Gardner, then doubled down this offseason by committing to Daniel Jones at quarterback as they look to challenge the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars, who finished first and second in the AFC South last season. Here's our 2026 preview of the Indianapolis Colts . Key Free Agency/Trade Additions Position Player 2025 PFF Grade WR Nick Westbrook-Ikhine 51.5 EDGE Arden Key 63.7 DI Colby Wooden 50.7 EDGE Micheal Clemons 59.9 LB Akeem Davis-Gaither 49.9 S Juanyeh Thomas 60.0 CB Cam Taylor-Britt 57.6 The Colts traded away wide receiver Michael Pittman this offseason but made little investment in replacing him. Nick Westbrook-Ikhine, who signed a one-year deal, was their only offensive free-agent addition outside of quarterback Easton Stick, who projects as a potential third-string option. Westbrook-Ikhine's best season came in 2024, when he totaled 497 receiving yards and averaged 1.14 yards per route run, tied for 86th among qualifying wide receivers. Arden Key appears set to start opposite Laiatu Latu on the edge, and after a slow start to his career, he has developed into a reliable contributor. Following three straight seasons with PFF grades below 60.0 to open his career, Key has posted grades above that mark in each of the past five seasons. 2026 NFL Draft Class Position Player 2025 PFF Grade LB CJ Allen 75.8 S A.J. Haulcy 86.6 G Jalen Farmer 69.8 LB Bryce Boettcher 77.6 EDGE George Gumbs Jr. 66.0 EDGE Caden Curry 90.6 HB Seth McGowan 70.1 WR Deion Burks 64.1 Despite not owning a first-round pick, the Colts appear to have landed a pair of immediate starters on the defensive side of the ball. Second-round pick CJ Allen earned PFF grades above 70.0 in each of his final two college seasons. His biggest strength is defending the run, as evidenced by an 88.6 PFF run-defense grade in his final season, though he earned just a 55.5 PFF coverage grade. How he develops in coverage will be one of the key storylines to monitor as he transitions to the NFL. Safety A.J. Haulcy followed up a strong 2024 season at Houston with an even better campaign at LSU in 2025. His 88.6 PFF coverage grade ranked tied for eighth among all safeties in the 2026 draft class, giving the Colts another rookie with the potential to contribute right away. Reasons for optimism Laiatu Latu took a significant step forward in his second NFL season, improving across multiple key metrics. His PFF grade jumped from 72.1 as a rookie to 84.1 in Year 2, while his run-defense grade increased by nine points and his pass-rush grade improved by 4.9. His pressure rate also climbed from 10.1% to 14.0%, and 20 of his pressures resulted in sacks or quarterback hits, up from 13 the previous season. If Latu takes another step forward in 2026, he could establish himself among the league's next tier of edge defenders just below the NFL's elite. The QB Annual Is Live Every qualifying quarterback. Read the QB Annual (opens in new tab) Get PFF+ (opens in new tab) Reason for pessimism The Colts' commitment to Daniel Jones is relatively low risk, with his contract tying him to the team for only the next two seasons. Even so, it is fair to question whether he is the long-term answer at quarterback. Jones opened 2025 strongly, ranking 10th among quarterbacks with an 80.3 PFF grade through Week 8, but he fell to 32nd from Week 9 onward. Over the full season, his 3.1% big-time throw rate ranked 34th among the 45 quarterbacks with at least 100 dropbacks, while his 3.9% turnover-worthy play rate was tied for the 13th highest. Jones' career body of work offers little reason to expect a dramatic turnaround. Across seven NFL seasons, he has produced a higher big-time throw rate than turnover-worthy play rate just once, and his career 2.9% big-time throw rate would have ranked only 36th among those 45 qualifying quarterbacks in 2025. Breakout Candidate Michael Pittman ‘s departure should create more opportunities for Josh Downs in a contract year. The 2023 third-round pick has recorded at least 500 receiving yards in each of his first three NFL seasons while dropping just 4.3% of his catchable targets over that span. In 2024, Downs averaged 2.20 yards per route run and saw 102 targets. With a clear path to the No. 2 receiver role in Indianapolis' offense, he has a strong chance to return to that level of production in 2026. Key roster battles With Josh Downs expected to take on a larger role following Michael Pittman's departure, the No. 3 receiver job is also up for grabs. Nick Westbrook-Ikhine is the favorite entering training camp, but after posting PFF receiving grades below 65.0 in each of the past four seasons, he is far from a lock to hold onto the role. Seventh-round pick Deion Burks dropped just four of the 93 catchable targets he saw at Oklahoma, though he never averaged more than 1.60 yards per route run in a season. Ashton Dulin has flashed in limited opportunities and has dropped only two passes in his NFL career, but he has never been targeted more than 24 times in a season. The opportunity is there for someone to seize the No. 3 receiver role. If none of the contenders separates from the pack, however, it could leave the Colts with a meaningful weakness in their receiving corps.
