Titans 19, 49ers 13 The Titans used their starters for a quarter and a half in the first preseason game. There were some positives and negatives from Cam Ward's performance, so let's begin with the good moments he had against the 49ers. His opening drive went 96 yards for a touchdown, capped off by a Tony Pollard rushing score. Ward made a couple of nice throws on the drive to move his team down the field and put Pollard in position to score. However, the positives end there. Ward missed Wan'Dale Robinson on an easy throw on the initial possession, and on the second drive, Ward was whistled for a horrible intentional grounding penalty because he held the ball forever and seemed to lack any sort of awareness in the pocket. Ward later missed an open Carnell Tate on a throw that the announcers deemed a "layup." Ward also dealt with a lot of pressure, as Tennessee's offensive line couldn't block San Francisco's backups. Yes, the 49ers played their backups to begin this game, and yet Ward couldn't complete half of his passes. Tennessee's offense looked absolutely dreadful when factoring in that they were battling reserves in this contest. Here were Ward's targets: Elic Ayomanor: 1 Gunnar Helm: 1 Calvin Ridley: 1 Wan'Dale Robinson: 5 Tyjae Spears: 1 Carnell Tate: 2 (1 end zone) It's difficult to find a positive for a receiver in a game in which a quarterback completed fewer than half of his throws, but Wan'Dale Robinson definitely deserves to be mentioned as a positive coming out of this game. Robinson saw five targets from Cam Ward, and yet no other Tennessee receiver who started the game saw more than two targets. In fact, Robinson was only one of two starters who saw multiple targets in this game. Ward struggled in this contest, but he looked most comfortable throwing to Robinson, who should have a solid year from a PPR perspective. Titans rookie running back Nicolas Singleton had a couple of nice runs in this game, but he was destroyed in pass protection. He was plowed over by a defender, resulting in Will Levis taking a crushing sack. Singleton will need to improve in this regard to get on the field more often. The 49ers, as mentioned, played their backups in this game. However, there is one player who really stood out, and that was No. 33 overall pick De'Zhaun Stribling. He had a monster game, catching six passes. He made one reception that was a beautiful catch downfield near the sideline, where he somehow stayed in bounds. He made an even crazier play after that, converting a third down by keeping his toe in bounds and his heel off the ground, which would have put him out of bounds. The play was challenged, and the announcers even thought that he stepped out of bounds, but Stribling somehow remained in bounds because his heel never touched the ground. Stribling looked great in this game, and remember, he battled Tennessee's starters, so this result definitely should be factored in as a major positive for Stribling heading into the season. NFL Preseason Announcers: The play-by-play announcer confused a second-and-1 with a second-and-14 somehow. I've never heard an announcer be that off before. Follow me @walterfootball for updates. Chargers 27, Texans 7 Neither the Texans nor the Chargers played their starters in this game, but we got a good look at Trey Lance, who was on the field for a half. Lance began the game well with some nice completions to KeAndre Lambert-Smith, but he missed Lambert-Smith for a touchdown on the initial possession. Lance then had a series of potential dropped interceptions. Two were clear dropped interceptions, while the third saw a defensive back get one hand on a potential pick. In between, Lance also threw way behind one of his targets. Lance showed some potential on a possession near the end of the first half when he fired a laser to rookie receiver Brenen Thompson. However, later on the possession, Lance heaved an interception deep in Houston territory when the defensive back read his eyes easily. This was not an encouraging performance for Lance, who was battling Houston's backups. He continued to show some upside, but there's way too much downside with him, so he's looking like a mere career backup at this point. It must be noted that two particular Chargers played in this game. Those were Kimani Vidal and Oronde Gadsden II. There's been some talk that Vidal might take some touches away from Omarion Hampton, but given that he played in this game with the other backups, that's unlikely to happen. Also, Gadsden playing is interesting considering that he was a big factor in the Chargers' offense last year. The Chargers signed David Njoku, so it sounds like he is going to be the primary tight end, whereas Gadsden has been practicing on special teams. Gadsden is certainly one to avoid at his ADP considering the situation. There's not much to say about the Texans, who played Davis Mills a bit and then Graham Mertz the rest of the way. However, rookie tight end Marlin Klein made a huge play with a 31-yard downfield reception, where the announcers claimed that not even Dalton Schultz could make that sort of play. Klein also drew an interference flag. The announcers raved about Klein's potential in this offense, though as a rookie, he is probably going to be a little bit limited until 2027. Follow me @walterfootball for updates. Patriots 13, Colts 13 Both the Patriots and the Colts sat their starters in this game, so there's not much to discuss. However, the Colts played a couple of young quarterbacks worth mentioning, so let's delve into them. Anthony Richardson played the entire first half and had some struggles to begin the game. He missed on an early throw, a short, routine pass that should have been completed easily. He then had a pass way off the mark that was bobbled and dropped into the hands of a Patriots defender. Richardson, however, had some nice rushes. The coaches designed running plays for him, and he took advantage, even scoring an apparent touchdown on one play, though replay showed that he was barely out of bounds before he crossed the goal line. The Colts then fumbled on the next play, so they couldn't score on the drive. Richardson also fumbled later in the game on a scramble where a defender popped the ball out of his hands. The good news for Richardson is that Riley Leonard wasn't any better. Leonard really struggled in this game. He had an underthrown duck that was intercepted. He also tossed some balls into the ground and had passes batted at the line of scrimmage. NFL Preseason Announcers: For many years, Patriots broadcasts have featured a segment from the employees at Bob's Discount Furniture. This is the first time in memory that they didn't get opinions from the furniture salesmen. Let's pour one out for those guys, who put in some hard work over the years. Follow me @walterfootball for updates. Bengals 16, Lions 14 The Bengals not only played their starters in this game, but they had Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase out on the field for two whole drives to begin this contest. They did this last year during the preseason as well because they wanted to stop performing so poorly to begin the year. However, this did not work that well. They beat the Browns in Week 1 last year, but were outgained by about 200 yards and were lucky that Cleveland made some unforced errors that prevented them from winning the game. The Bengals looked as slow as ever, as they scored just three points against Detroit's backups in two possessions. Burrow took a bad sack on one of the drives where he held the ball forever, and then the other possession stalled before a long field goal was made by Evan McPherson. To be fair, there were heavy rain conditions in this game that made moving the ball very difficult. However, the opponent was so bad that the Bengals should have scored a touchdown on at least one of their drives. Ja'Marr Chase: 1 Mike Gesicki: 1 Andrei Iosivas: 1 Samaje Perine: 1 Drew Sample: 1 There's nothing worth noting about the Lions, who played their deep backups the entire evening. NFL Preseason Announcers: The announcers had some weird moments in this game. One of them shouted, "They're keeping the offense on the field!" when it was third down. They also called Burrow "one of the all-time greats," which is a bit presumptive. I love Burrow, and he could get there one day, but to declare him as such now is ridiculous. Follow me @walterfootball for updates. Steelers 28, Packers 9 The Packers decided that they needed to play their starters for some reason. They can't be too happy with the result, as the first-team unit wasn't able to score a touchdown against Pittsburgh's backup defensive unit. "No Cookie" Jordan Love missed an easy throw right away, but rebounded with a nice connection to Jayden Reed. His one drive was unimpressive overall, but it was a very small sample size. Here were Love's targets: Marshawn Lloyd: 1 Jayden Reed: 2 Christian Watson: 1 Josh Wylie: 1 Jayden Reed will be more involved this year because he's now playing in two-receiver formations, which he had never done prior to this season. It's no coincidence that Reed was the only starter with multiple targets in the preseason opener. Josh Jacobs was one of the few starters who rested. Marshawn Lloyd started instead. He had a nice 5-yard run on his first opportunity, but didn't do much else after that. With Jacobs possibly facing suspension, Lloyd must be rostered. The Steelers didn't play any of their starters. Mason Rudolph was the first quarterback on the field. He then gave way to Will Howard. Third-round rookie Drew Allar then took over a bit in the second half. He immediately completed a 74-yard pass to Kaden Wetjen, though that was mostly WetJen, as Allar connected on a slant to the fourth-round rookie that was in the air for 10 yards. Wetjen then blazed by every Green Bay defender and was tackled at the 1-yard line. Allar missed an easy throw in the red zone after that, but then ran for a touchdown on the next lay. Allar's next drive featured some quality strikes. He eventually rolled left and found Wetjen for a touchdown. The next possession saw Allar drew an interference flag on a deep throw, setting up another score. Allar had a great game overall. He threw off his back foot on a couple of occasions, but wasn't penalized for it. The Steelers should feel encouraged, but let's remember that Allar's biggest flaw entering the NFL was what's between his ears. He battled a vanilla defense that didn't challenge him, so things will be much different versus complex defense. Still, this was a positive outcome for him. Germie Bernard had a nice debut as well. He caught all but one of his targets, and that lone exception appeared to be a touchdown, but a defender pushed him out of bounds while he was in the air. Follow me @walterfootball for updates. Panthers 33, Cardinals 30 Neither the Cardinals nor the Panthers played their starters in this game. Even Jeremiyah Love sat out despite being a rookie. That meant that all eyes were on third-round rookie quarterback Carson Beck, who was starting for Arizona. Beck didn't put together a scoring drive on his first possession, although he scrambled for a first down on the initial third down of the game. On his next third down, Beck threw an accurate ball, but the pass was dropped thanks to rookie cornerback Will Lee breaking up the play. Beck, however, rebounded on the next possession with a 35-yard pass when receiver Jalen Brooks beat Lee. Beck then zinged a pass to Brooks for a gain of about 20 yards, and then had a nice throw to running back Corey Kiner, who was tackled inches shy of the goal line, setting up Kiner's touchdown run on the ensuing play. Beck wasn't done after that. He had a great deep pass to Brooks, hitting him in stride for a 49-yard connection. He then showed great touch on a fade pass to Simi Fehoko for a touchdown. Beck played one drive in the third quarter, where he had a deep throw that looked like it would be completed for a 30-yard gain, but his receiver dropped it. Beck finished the night on that possession, and he showed some great ability. However, it should be noted that he was playing against a vanilla Carolina defense that didn't give him any complicated looks, which is where Beck would probably struggle in real-game action. Still, Arizona should be optimistic about his performance in his debut appearance. Kenny Pickett started for the Panthers in this game, but didn't play very much. He drew a deep pass interference penalty to receiver Bryson Tremayne on his first possession, but then threw well short on third-and-9. Pickett just dinked and dunked while he was on the field and didn't really show anything of note. Undrafted rookie Haynes King played most of the game for the Panthers. King is known for his mobility, and he showed off his scrambling ability on numerous occasions. However, he was a surprise as a passer. He showed nice touch on a touchdown pass on an early drive and then made some very accurate throws right before halftime. However, King made a huge mistake at the end of the drive when he missed a wide-open receiver in the end zone. This was a classic example of King's poor mechanics, which he desperately needs to improve. King, however, rebounded at the end of the third quarter when he converted a third-and-15 with a 16-yard completion. On the final drive, King fired an accurate ball on third-and-10 for an 11-yard completion. He then made a great scramble to move into the red zone. On the final play of regulation, King scrambled and barely reached the ball over the goal line to score the decisive touchdown. King showed some very good passing ability in this game, surprising Chris Collinsworth, the color commentator on the broadcast. He's still a work in progress and really needs to improve his mechanics, but he showed some potential in his NFL preseason debut. Chicago Bears (11-6) at 2. Detroit Lions (12-5) This might be the best two-seven matchup in NFL history, given that both teams involved are legitimate Super Bowl contenders. Both have dynamic offenses, and Ben Johnson's presence could give Chicago a leg up in this battle. However, the ultimate difference could prove to be Chicago's poor pass rush. Jared Goff will be kept clean all game, while Caleb Williams will see some pressure from Aidan Hutchinson. Lions 27, Bears 24 6. San Francisco 49ers (13-4) at 3. Philadelphia Eagles (11-6) This is a rematch of last year's wild card-round game. The Eagles entered the contest as the favorite, but ultimately lost to an injury-ravaged 49ers team. Most of the blame went on A.J. Brown, who dropped three passes in the defeat. Brown is no longer on the team, but then again, it's unlikely that the 49ers will be so bogged down by injuries. San Francisco is the better team and will win this game as a result. 49ers 23, Eagles 19 5. Seattle Seahawks (13-4) at 4. New Orleans Saints (9-8) This is another playoff rematch, but the original took place long ago, back when the Pete Carroll era initially began in Seattle. The Seahawks hosted the heavily favored Saints, but were able to triumph on the back of Marshawn Lynch and his legendary "Beast Quake" touchdown run. Sixteen years later, could there finally be a reversal? Perhaps it'll be Travis Etienne whose run registers on the Richter scale, with the upstart Saints vanquishing the reigning Super Bowl champions. Saints 41, Seahawks 36 7. New England Patriots (10-7) at 2. Cincinnati Bengals (13-4) This is another great two-seven game, although the Patriots are probably the weakest of the four teams involved in these two contests. That may sound odd, given that the Patriots were recently in the Super Bowl, but their record last year was enhanced by a very easy schedule, and their playoff wins were a byproduct of opposing offenses being absolutely dreadful. That is not the case with the Bengals, who will be able to take advantage of New England's defensive deficiencies. Bengals 38, Patriots 27 6. Denver Broncos (10-7) at 3. Los Angeles Chargers (12-5) Will Justin Herbert finally win a playoff game? This is the matchup for him to accomplish that feat, given that he's owned the Broncos when he and his team have been mostly healthy. The Broncos' strength, their pass rush, will be neutralized by the Chargers' two elite tackles. Herbert won't have a problem scoring, while Bo Nix won't be able to keep up. Chargers 31, Broncos 23 5. Baltimore Ravens (11-6) at 4. Jacksonville Jaguars (12-5) The Ravens would be one of the top Super Bowl contenders if they didn't have glaring issues with the interior of their offensive line. The Jaguars have talent on their defensive front, so they should be able to take advantage of this liability. Their athletic edge players, meanwhile, will be able to contain Lamar Jackson for the most part. Trevor Lawrence will advance to the second round this time. Jaguars 26, Ravens 20 2026 NFL Playoff Predictions - Divisional Round 6. San Francisco 49ers (13-4) at 1. Los Angeles Rams (15-2) The 49ers and Rams opened their seasons in Australia, and now will one go home following the third battle between these teams. The Rams have owned the 49ers of late, taking four of the previous five meetings, and the one loss was in overtime when Los Angeles looked unprepared to play. While the 49ers have one of the very few tackles who can neutralize Myles Garrett, their defense won't be able to hold up against Matthew Stafford and company. Rams 34, 49ers 24 4. New Orleans Saints (9-8) at 2. Detroit Lions (12-5) When the Seahawks upset the Saints, they battled an NFC North team in the second round as double-digit underdogs. Many thought they'd have a chance against the Bears, but it was an ugly, lopsided affair. The Saints won't stand much of a chance against this Detroit behemoth. Lions 35, Saints 24 4. Jacksonville Jaguars (12-5) at 1. Buffalo Bills (13-4) The Bills and Jaguars met in the opening round of the playoffs last year in what was a showdown between the top two teams in the AFC. The Bills prevailed at the very end in a thriller. The difference in this matchup is that these teams will be battling in Buffalo's frigid environment. This is obviously not ideal for a team from Florida. The Bills should be able to vanquish the Jaguars again. Bills 27, Jaguars 23 3. Los Angeles Chargers (12-5) at 2. Cincinnati Bengals (13-4) Here's another playoff matchup between a warm-weather team playing in the freezing cold. The Chargers are a great team with Super Bowl aspirations, but they better achieve home-field advantage, or they could get caught playing in Cincinnati or Buffalo. The Chargers would have a chance if Jesse Minter were still coaching their defense, but their new coordinator may not be able to figure out how to contain Joe Burrow and the rest of Cincinnati's offense. And if this ends up being a reenactment of the Freezer Bowl, where the Bengals defeated the Chargers 27-7 in minus-55 weather, forget about it. Bengals 34, Chargers 21 2026 NFL Playoff Predictions - Championship Sunday 2. Detroit Lions (12-5) at 1. Los Angeles Rams (15-2) This is Jared Goff's chance to get the ultimate revenge. His team discarded him in favor of Matthew Stafford, but he can now end the Rams' chances of winning a Super Bowl before this Los Angeles team breaks up and goes with Ty Simpson in the post-Sean McVay era. As mentioned in the previous round, the 49ers have one of the few players who can handle Myles Garrett. The Lions have one as well with Penei Sewell. The Rams are the best team in the NFL, but they have their flaws. They had struggles in short yardage last year, and their special teams unit was an abomination. The Lions are better in both areas, so they could upset the Rams. Lions 27, Rams 24 2. Cincinnati Bengals (13-4) at 1. Buffalo Bills (13-4) This is yet another playoff rematch. The Bengals went into Buffalo a few years ago and dismantled the Bills. For whatever reason, Josh Allen hasn't been able to get over the hump in the playoffs. Perhaps that will change this year, but of the two quarterbacks in this matchup, Joe Burrow has been way more clutch. Burrow happens to possess two terrific receivers who can take advantage of Buffalo's secondary. It's also unclear if the Bills will be able to stop the run after they were so poor against it last season. Bengals 34, Bills 31 2026 NFL Playoff Predictions - Super Bowl LXI at Los Angeles Detroit Lions (12-5) vs. Cincinnati Bengals (13-4) It's the Year of the Cat! The Lions and Bengals both failed to qualify for the playoffs last year, but there's reason to believe that they'll both have a good chance to make a deep run in this upcoming postseason. That's what recent history suggests, anyway. The two participants in the Super Bowl last year, the Patriots and Seahawks, both played against every team in the NFC South during the regular season. The two teams from the previous Super Bowl, the Eagles and Chiefs, both played against every team in the NFC South as well. It should come as no surprise that these teams had so much success, given that they were able to rack up easy wins and earn a high playoff seed as a result. Both the NFC North and the AFC North battle the NFC South this year. The Lions, Bears, Vikings, Packers, Bengals, Ravens, Steelers, and Browns (yeah, right) all qualify as potential Super Bowl participants, based on this criteria. And of those eight teams, the Bengals and Lions both arguably rate as being the best. If this is the Year of the Cat, who then will prevail? Both are great teams and can certainly win, but there's a major difference between the two quarterbacks. Both are extremely talented, former No. 1 picks. However, Jared Goff struggled in his only Super Bowl and even forgot his own snap count on one play. Burrow, conversely, was terrific in his sole Super Bowl, albeit in a loss. He's been extremely clutch in the playoffs, and there's no reason to think that will change. Reader, DT Shelby Harris, DT Leki Fotu, DT Sam Roberts, OLB Khalid Kareem, ILB Tremaine Edmunds, CB Greg Newsome, S Elijah Campbell, S Jason Pinnock, P Jordan Stout. Early Draft Picks: OLB Arvell Reese, G Francis Mauigoa, CB Colton Hood. Giants Rookie Forecast Offseason Losses: QB Russell Wilson, WR Wan'Dale Robinson, TE Daniel Bellinger, G Greg Van Roten, G Aaron Stinnie, C Austin Schlottman, DT Dexter Lawrence, DT Rakeem Nunez-Roches, DT D.J. Davidson, ILB Bobby Okereke, CB Cordale Flott, S Dane Belton, K Graham Gano. 2026 New York Giants Offense: It didn't take very long for the Giants to turn to first-round rookie quarterback Jaxson Dart last year. Russell Wilson started the first three games, but was benched during the Week 3 loss versus the Chiefs. Dart stepped in and then won his first start against the Chargers. Dart had some very bright moments in his initial season, but there were some dark ones as well, particularly those involving his injuries. Dart was reckless and was checked for a grand total of five potential concussions in just 10 games. He was diagnosed with only one concussion, but given how flimsy NFL doctors can be, there's a chance that Dart was concussed on two or three occasions. Dart is exciting, but asking him to play it safe would diminish his upside. Thus, the Giants needed to protect him as well as possible and give him plenty of weapons. They certainly failed in the latter objective, but they at least tried to bolster his blocking. They re-signed Jermaine Eluemunor, a solid right tackle who serves as a quality bookend for terrific left tackle Andrew Thomas. The Giants then drafted another tackle, Francis Mauigoa, with the No. 10 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Mauigoa is a talented tackle, but will be asked to play out of position at guard. This was a confusing selection because the Giants could have just drafted the superior guard, Vega Ioane, with that pick. Perhaps Mauigoa will pan out as the team's new right guard, but he doesn't project well in that role. There's concern with the other two starting offensive linemen as well. Center John Michael Schmitz is a recent second-round pick, but hasn't played up to that level yet. Perhaps he'll be a late bloomer and eventually get there. Left guard Jon Runyan struggled mightily last year. The Giants brought in Daniel Faalele, one of several former Ravens who followed John Harbaugh to New York, to compete for snaps. As for the receivers, the Giants have a huge problem at the position this year. Malik Nabers is a mega talent, but is coming off a torn ACL that had more complications than usual. There is growing speculation that Nabers may not be available until October, which means that Dart will have to rely on a group of pedestrian veterans as his downfield targets. Darius Slayton is the incumbent, while the likes of Darnell Mooney, Calvin Austin, JuJu Smith-Schuster, and Odell Beckham were signed. Beckham used to be the best of the bunch, but he's no longer a viable starter due to age and injuries. Mooney is coming off a dreadful 2025 campaign, but was dealing with an injury all year. It's possible that he could recover and serve as a fine No. 2 option once Nabers returns. There's also third-round rookie Malachi Fields, who has some potential. Given the state of the receiver corps, Dart will be looking toward his tight ends often. Theo Johnson is an athletic player who developed some chemistry with Dart last year. The Giants, intending to use multi-tight end formations, also signed Isaiah Likely, another former Raven. The extremely athletic Likely had some huge games in Baltimore while serving second fiddle to Mark Andrews. He'll be the primary tight end in New York, meaning he could have his best season yet. The Giants could also have a great season from Cam Skattebo. The renowned Arizona State product took over as the starter around the same time as Dart last year, and he was terrific as both a runner and a receiver out of the backfield. He suffered a devastating ankle injury in the second matchup against the Eagles, but it's sounding like he'll be ready by Week 1. If not, Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary will once again split the workload in a mediocre rotation. 2026 New York Giants Defense: It was discussed earlier that the Giants' second opening-round selection, Francis Mauigoa, will be playing out of position, and yet New York could have drafted a better player at that position. Amazingly, the same thing could be said of the Giants' initial first-round pick. It was reported that New York loved Jordyn Tyson, but couldn't resist Arvell Reese when he fell to them at No. 5. Reese was projected by many to be a dynamic edge rusher, but New York has plenty of those with Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, and Kayvon Thibodeaux all stationed at outside linebacker. Reese will be asked to play inside, which may not be a natural fit for him. But even if it is, the Giants could have chosen a better inside linebacker by selecting Sonny Styles. Nevertheless, Reese will be one of the two inside linebackers, joining Tremaine Edmunds, who was signed over from Chicago. Edmunds is a very athletic player, but has often struggled in coverage. Edmunds, at the very least, will thrive in run support. Reese, conversely, will be learning the position and could struggle before blossoming later. It must be noted, however, that many hybrid linebackers, even those chosen in the top 10, have busted at an alarming rate. As for the trio of edge rushers mentioned earlier, Burns is the best of the bunch. This was clear when he racked up 16.5 sacks in 2025. Carter has loads of potential as a top-five pick from the 2025 NFL Draft, but he managed just four sacks last year. He also came under scrutiny for openly challenging his quarterback's political beliefs when such matters could have been handled internally. There was some speculation that Thibodeaux (2.5 sacks) could be traded, but in the wake of the antics, it could be Carter who is dealt. One prominent Giant who was dealt this offseason is Dexter Lawrence. The mega-talented nose tackle is coming off a bit of a down year, but was projected to rebound. Lawrence was shipped off to the Bengals for the No. 10 overall pick, but the Giants were able to replace him with D.J. Reader. This is just a short-term solution, however, given that Reader turned 32 this offseason. Reader will be able to plug running lanes, and he'll be flanked by 2025 third-round pick Darius Alexander and another new addition, Shelby Harris. Alexander will need to make a big leap after struggling mightily as a rookie. Harris is a mediocre veteran who is even older than Reader; he turns 35 in August. New York also made some additions to the secondary, with two being particularly prominent. Greg Newsome II was signed over from the Jaguars. Newsome is a skilled cornerback who figures to start opposite Paulson Adebo, a mediocre player at the position. Dru Phillips will reprise his role as a fine slot corner. The other new Giant defensive back is another former Raven. Ar'Darius Washington barely played last year because he was returning from a devastating injury. He should be close to 100 percent now, and if that's the case, he'll be an enormous upgrade at safety. The Giants had mediocre play at the position last season with Jevon Holland and Tyler Nubin. Both will return for 2026, so New York will be hoping that one of them steps up. Nubin is young enough (25) to make a leap, while Holland is still in his prime and could rebound from a disappointing season. 2026 New York Giants Schedule and Intangibles: The Giants appear to have severe kicking issues. They'll be relying on someone named Ben Sauls or Dominic Zvada this year. Another former Raven will be punting for the Giants. Jordan Stout was second in net punting last year. The Giants have a tough fourth-place schedule. They have to go up against the Rams, Seahawks, 49ers, Texans, Jaguars, and Lions. 2026 New York Giants Rookies: Go here for the Giants Rookie Forecast , a page with predictions like which rookie will bust and which rookie will become a solid starter. 2026 New York Giants Positional Rankings (1-5 stars): Quarterbacks Offensive Line Secondary Running Backs Defensive Line Special Teams Receivers Linebackers Coaching 2026 New York Giants Analysis: The Giants will be much better this year with an upgraded coach and a quarterback who has professional experience. However, they still have some major weaknesses, and their fourth-place schedule is unforgiving. Still, it's not impossible that the Giants will be able to qualify for the playoffs, provided that Jaxson Dart remains healthy. Projection: 8-9 (Tied 3rd in NFC East) 2025 Projection: 4-13. 2025 Actual Result: 4-13. 2024 Projection: 4-13. 2024 Actual Result: 3-14. 2023 Projection: 9-8. 2023 Actual Result: 6-11. 2022 Projection: 5-12. 2022 Actual Result: 9-7-1. 2021 Projection: 7-10. 2021 Actual Result: 4-13. 2020 Projection: 11-5. 2020 Actual Result: 6-10. 2019 Projection: 5-11. 2019 Actual Result: 4-12. 2018 Projection: 6-10. 2018 Actual Result: 5-11. 2017 Projection: 7-9. 2017 Actual Result: 3-13. = 2016 Projection: 7-9. 2016 Actual Result: 11-5. NFL Draft Team Grade: C Grade Goals Entering the 2026 NFL Draft: The Giants need to spend several of their picks to help Jaxson Dart. Adding talent on the offensive line and to the receiver group would make a lot of sense, though New York is smitten Jeremiyah Love. The Giants also need to focus on improving their defensive line and secondary. 2026 NFL Draft Accomplishments: The Titans opted to pass on Arvell Reese in favor of a receiver. This was the right decision to help their young quarterback even though the edge rush was a huge need for them. The Giants were confronted with the same decision, but decided to do the opposite. They could have helped Dart by selecting Tyson, but they went with Reese instead even though they had far less of a need on the edge than Tennessee did. It's curious as to why the Giants made this decision when they had the opportunity to draft the better of the two receivers. One could say that New York helped Dart with their next top-10 selection, but that's not entirely true. The Giants spent the 10th-overall choice on Francis Mauigoa, who will have to play out of position until Jermaine Eluemunor leaves the team. A big issue, aside from the positional switch, is that Mauigoa has a back injury and may miss a chunk of his rookie season. This is obviously not ideal for Dart. Only one pick might aid Dart completely this year, and that was the third-rounder used on Malachi Fields. The Giants also made another great selection with Colton Hood on Day 2, so this haul wasn't a total disaster. The Giants were able to obtain some good players, but this draft class was a disappointment overall because the Giants failed to put Dart into the best possible situation to succeed. NFL Draft Individual Grades: 5. Arvell Reese, DE/OLB, Ohio State C- Grade I guess the Giants didn’t think Arvell Reese would be available, so they passed on Jordyn Tyson for him. Reese may be intriguing, but again, he has no set position and is just a one-year starter. Now, Tyson may not get to the Giants, so it’ll be difficult to find some help for Jaxson Dart. This pick has a ton of upside, but there’s a low floor as well, especially when considering that edge rush was not a need whatsoever. 10. Francis Mauigoa, OT, Miami D Grade What in the world are the Giants doing? They initially drafted a developmental player over an explosive receiver to potentially be an edge rusher, which they don’t need, and now they drafted a tackle, which they also don’t need, and yet that tackle may not be able to play this year because of a back injury. New York had loads of potential entering the 2026 NFL Draft and squandered it. 37. Colton Hood, CB, Tennessee A Grade The Giants were sniped by the Texans and Chiefs for their picks. They were going to draft Kayden McDonald here and Mansoor Delane at No. 10. It all worked out, however, because Hood is a strong value at this spot, as someone who easily could have gone toward the end of Round 1. Cornerback is a huge need, so this selection should make New York feel better about the sniping. 74. Malachi Fields, WR, Notre Dame B Grade The Giants traded a 2027 pick for this, which is not something I like. However, the Giants needed to give Jaxson Dart a play-maker, and Malachi Fields is a big receiver who can be a red zone weapon. I had Fields in the second round, so I definitely like the value (without factoring the trade). 186. Bobby Jamison-Travis, NT, Auburn B Grade Bobby Jamison-Travis is stout against the run, but doesn’t offer anything as a pass rusher. With Dexter Lawrence gone, this pick can’t be a surprise. Jamison-Travis makes sense in Round 6. 192. J.C. Davis, OT, Illinois B+ Grade J.C. Davis is a vesatile tackle. The Giants need depth on the offensive line to help protect Jaxson Dart, so I like this pick, especially because I had Davis going about a dozen picks earlier. 193. Jack Kelly, LB, BYU A- Grade Jack Kelly is a tough linebacker who gives maximum effort. I love this pick, as Kelly is someone I pegged as a fourth-round pick. He could become a locker room leader for the Giants if he pans out. --Offseason Reports Lander-- Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Buffalo Bills Carolina Panthers Chicago Bears records.new_body: 2026 NFL Season Preview: Washington Redskins - WalterFootball Skip to content Home 2026 NFL Season Preview: Washington Redskins --Offseason Reports Lander-- Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Buffalo Bills Carolina Panthers Chicago Bears Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Dallas Cowboys Denver Broncos Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Kansas City Chiefs Los Angeles Chargers Los Angeles Rams Las Vegas Raiders Miami Dolphins Minnesota Vikings New England Patriots New Orleans Saints New York Giants New York Jets Philadelphia Eagles Pittsburgh Steelers Seattle Seahawks San Francisco 49ers Tampa Bay Buccaneers Tennessee Titans Washington Commanders Washington Redskins 2026 NFL Season Preview: Veteran Additions: RB Rachaad White, WR Dyami Brown, TE Chig Okonkwo, DT Tim Settle, DT Charles Omenihu, DT DJ Davidson, OLB Odafe Oweh, OLB K'Lavon Chaisson, ILB Leo Chenal, CB Rasul Douglas, CB Ahkello Witherspoon, CB Amik Robertson, S Nick Cross. Early Draft Picks: ILB Sonny Styles, WR Antonio Williams. Redskins Rookie Forecast Offseason Losses: RB Chris Rodriguez, RB Austin Ekeler, WR Deebo Samuel, WR Noah Brown, TE Zach Ertz, OT Trenton Scott, C Tyler Biadasz, DT Eddie Goldman, OLB Von Miller, OLB Jacob Martin, ILB Bobby Wagner, CB Jonathan Jones, CB Noah Igbinoghene. 2026 Washington Redskins Offense: Expectations were high for Jayden Daniels entering the NFL, and yet he exceeded all of them as a rookie. A year after C.J. Stroud broke records for an NFL rookie quarterback, Daniels surpassed some of them. With a bolstered supporting cast, Daniels was supposed to skyrocket to the moon in his second season, but crashed back down to Earth instead with a very disappointing 5-12 record. Injuries were the primary culprit for Daniels, who got hurt on multiple occasions last year and never seemed 100 percent for a full game outside of Week 1. Perhaps he'll have better injury luck in his third year, though the offensive line will obviously play a big factor in determining that. It'll definitely help if elite guard Sam Cosmi can remain on the field for more than nine games. Cosmi missed about half of 2025, but is healthy heading into this season. If he and Laremy Tunsil can stay off the injury report, Daniels will have two very high-end blockers in front of him. The rest of the offensive line has its issues. Right tackle Josh Conerly didn't perform very well in his rookie year, but he's a recent first-round pick with plenty of potential. There's a good chance he'll improve now that he's experienced. Conversely, there's not too much upside with center Nick Allegretti and left guard Chris Paul, both of whom struggled last season. The Redskins lost last year's center, Tyler Biadasz, but failed to replace him. This was an oversight by the front office. Washington's management failed to pair Daniels with an abundance of receiving talent as well. Terry McLaurin will return as the No. 1 receiver, and he figures to have a better and healthier 2026 campaign because he's not holding out this time. The Redskins also signed athletic tight end Chig Okonkwo away from the Titans to replace Zach Ertz. That was it, however, as Deebo Samuel departed and wasn't replaced either unless third-round rookie Antonio Williams is ready to contribute immediately. Unless the Redskins sign a veteran receiver, Daniels will be relying on the likes of Williams, Treylon Burks, and Dyami Brown, which is far from ideal. Daniels figures to target Rachaad White heavily as well. The Redskins had grand plans for Austin Ekeler in that regard last year, but he suffered a devastating injury in Week 2 and was lost for the season. White will fill that role perfectly. He won't do as much in the ground game, however, so the Redskins will be hoping that one of Jacory Croskey-Merritt or sixth-round rookie Kaytron Allen steps up. Croskey-Merritt was everyone's darling fantasy sleeper weeks prior to the 2025 season, but never lived up to the hype. Allen isn't very athletic, but he's a skilled runner. 2026 Washington Redskins Defense: The Redskins didn't do very much to improve their offense this offseason. This was because they spent so much energy bolstering the defense. It's difficult to blame them, given that they allowed the most yardage in the NFL last year. Washington is projected to have between six and eight new defensive starters in 2026. This includes first-round rookie Sonny Styles. Chosen in the top 10, Styles is an elite athlete with great college tape. The Redskins have had big problems defending the middle of the field for years, but Styles will have a huge impact in helping to improve this area. Styles figures to start next to another new addition, Leo Chenal. Signed away from the Chiefs, Chenal played well in both run support and coverage last season. There will be two new edge rushers as well. The Redskins struggled mightily to generate quarterback pressure last year, with no returning player logging more than 5.5 sacks. Dorance Armstrong, who had that figure, will be playing in a rotation with Odafe Oweh and K'Lavon Chaisson. Oweh and Chaisson both notched 7.5 sacks last season with the Chargers and Patriots, respectively. Oweh is the better of the two; he had 10 sacks in 2024 with Baltimore. Oweh and Chaisson aren't great players by any means, but they'll still be upgrades over what Washington possessed in 2025. The only guaranteed new starter on the defensive line is nose tackle Tim Settle, who was signed over from Houston. However, newly signed D.J. Davidson and Charles Omenihu will compete for playing time. Settle performed well in a heavy Houston rotation last year. He'll play next to Da'Ron Payne, a big defensive tackle who still thrives in both run support and the pass rush. Javon Kinlaw will also be in the mix, but he's a former first-round bust who has never played well in the NFL. As for the secondary, the Redskins figure to have at least one new starter at both cornerback and safety. The new corners are Amik Robertson and Rasul Douglas. Robertson performed well in Detroit. He'll be stationed in the slot, as Trey Amos and Mike Sainristil were projected to operate outside. Both are young players who struggled last year because they had no support from the pass rush. Amos is a second-round pick from the 2025 NFL Draft, while Sainristil had a strong rookie campaign, so there's definitely a chance that both players improve if the Redskins can generate more pressure this season. Washington signed Douglas, who thrived in Miami last year. He'll challenge one of the young corners for work. The new safety is former Colt Nick Cross, who is a stout in-the-box run defender. He's not great in coverage, but he's not completely lost in that regard either. He'll start next to Will Harris, who is coming off a down year because he missed eight games due to injury. 2026 Washington Redskins Schedule and Intangibles: The Redskins' rich fan base doesn't show up to games because they're too busy dining at fancy restaurants and passing bills that only enrich themselves and extract wealth from future generations. This would explain why the team is just 56-85 as a host the past 16 years. However, they were 7-2 at home with Jayden Daniels in his rookie year, so perhaps they will have a strong home-field advantage for once. Washington's new kicker is Jake Moody. Any 49er fan knows how putrid Moody can be, but Moody did well for Washington after taking over for Matt Gay in the middle of 2025. Moody went 10-of-11, hitting both tries from 50-plus. Tress Way was seventh in net punting in 2024 and sixth in 2025. He did well to pin the opposition inside the 20. The Redskins have a mixed schedule. They have tough non-divisional opponents like the Seahawks, Rams, 49ers, Jaguars, Texans, and Bengals. However, they also get the Colts, Titans, Falcons, and Cardinals. 2026 Washington Redskins Rookies: Go here for the Redskins Rookie Forecast , a page with predictions like which rookie will bust and which rookie will become a solid starter. 2026 Washington Redskins Positional Rankings (1-5 stars): Quarterbacks Offensive Line Secondary Running Backs Defensive Line Special Teams Receivers Linebackers Coaching 2026 Washington Redskins Analysis: The Redskins advanced to the NFC Championship two years ago, upsetting the No. 1 seed Lions in the process. They were dismantled by the Eagles, and they've played horribly since. They could bounce back in 2026 if Jayden Daniels remains healthy and the defense improves with all of the new additions. However, there could be more of the same in 2026, given Daniels' lacking durability and the holes that remain on the stop unit. Projection: 8-9 (Tied 3rd in NFC East) 2025 Projection: 12-5. 2025 Actual Result: 5-12. 2024 Projection: 7-10. 2024 Actual Result: 12-5. 2023 Projection: 5-12. 2023 Actual Result: 4-13. 2022 Projection: 6-11. 2022 Actual Result: 8-8-1. 2021 Projection: 10-7. 2021 Actual Result: 7-10. 2020 Projection: 4-12. 2020 Actual Result: 7-9. 2019 Projection: 4-12. 2019 Actual Result: 3-13. 2018 Projection: 10-6. 2018 Actual Result: 7-9. 2017 Projection: 8-8. 2017 Actual Result: 7-9. 2016 Projection: 9-7. 2016 Actual Result: 8-7-1. NFL Draft Team Grade: A Grade Goals Entering the 2026 NFL Draft: The Redskins have just two picks in the first four rounds, so they need to draft very carefully. They somehow have to both find Jayden Daniels another weapon and improve their horrible defense that has issues at every level. Good luck, Washington. 2026 NFL Draft Accomplishments: Washington didn't have much to work with, but it made the most of what it had. Of the four picks the Redskins had in the top 200, all of them scored in the "A" range. They drafted incredibly well, selecting either mega talents or great bargains. The Redskins planned on taking Carnell Tate, but because he was off the board, that allowed Washington to obtain the better player, as Sonny Styles figures to provide a much-needed colossal upgrade in the middle of the defense. Then, in the third round, Antonio Williams was obtained to provide Jayden Daniels with the upgrade he likely thought he was getting at No. 7. Washington continued to draft strongly after that, securing a third-round prospect in Joshua Josephs in Round 5, and a fourth-round prospect in Kaytron Allen in the sixth frame. Allen and sixth-round center Matt Gulbin will give Daniels more of a supporting system, while Josephs could bolster a weak pass rush. All of these elements were able to add up to a stellar draft class for Washington. NFL Draft Individual Grades: 7. Sonny Styles, LB, Ohio State A Grade Sonny Styles doesn’t provide positional value, but that’s out the window in this lackluster draft class. The Redskins are getting the best player on the board who fills a huge need for them. They should be able to cover the middle of the field for once, and Styles will be very useful against the Eagles’ offense. 71. Antonio Williams, WR, Clemson A- Grade I’ve had Antonio Williams in the second round in a bunch of my mock draft updates, so I obviously like that the Redskins were able to obtain him at this spot. Williams has play-making ability and runs good routes, so he should be able to develop into a solid No. 2 wideout for Washington. 147. Joshua Josephs, DE, Tennessee A Grade Joshua Josephs has the potential to be a designated pass rusher in the pros. I had him going at the end of the third round. Washington signed multiple defensive ends this free agency, but two of them were for one year, so Josephs will be a replacement in 2027. 187. Kaytron Allen, RB, Penn State A Grade Kaytron Allen is a physical runner who generates yards after contact. The Redskins don’t have much going on at running back, so Allen could see a decent number of carries as a rookie. Allen easily could have gone four rounds earlier. 209. Matt Gulbin, C, Michigan State B Grade Matt Gublin was a great blocker in school, but didn’t measure well athletically. He should be a fine backup in the NFL, and I thought he would go in this range, so this pick is fine. 223. Athan Kaliakmanis, QB, Rutgers B- Grade Athan Kaliakmanis over Garrett Nussmeier is wild. Kaliakmanis has plus intermediate accuracy and a quick release. He had a lot of buzz heading into the draft. He could be a developmental backup. --Offseason Reports Lander-- Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Buffalo Bills Carolina Panthers Chicago Bears Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns records.new_body: 2026 NFL Draft Grades: Dallas Cowboys - WalterFootball Skip to content Home 2026 NFL Draft Grades: Dallas Cowboys --Offseason Reports Lander-- Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Buffalo Bills Carolina Panthers Chicago Bears Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Dallas Cowboys Denver Broncos Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Kansas City Chiefs Los Angeles Chargers Los Angeles Rams Las Vegas Raiders Miami Dolphins Minnesota Vikings New England Patriots New Orleans Saints New York Giants New York Jets Philadelphia Eagles Pittsburgh Steelers Seattle Seahawks San Francisco 49ers Tampa Bay Buccaneers Tennessee Titans Washington Commanders Dallas Cowboys 2026 NFL Season Preview: Veteran Additions: QB Sam Howell, WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling, C Matt Hennessy, DT Otito Ogbonnia, DT Jonathan Bullard, OLB Rashan Gary, ILB Dee Winters, CB Cobie Durant, S Jalen Thompson, S P.J. Locke. Early Draft Picks: S Caleb Downs, DE Malachi Lawrence, ILB Jaishawn Barham, CB Devin Moore, DT L.T. Overton, OL Drew Shelton. Cowboys Rookie Forecast Offseason Losses: WR Jalen Tolbert, OT Hakeem Adeniji, G Brandon Jones, C Brock Hoffman, DE Jadeveon Clowney, DE Dante Fowler, DT Osa Odighizuwa, ILB Kenneth Murray, ILB Jack Sanborn, S Donovan Wilson. 2026 Dallas Cowboys Offense: Dak Prescott has proven that he can play at an All-Pro level when everything is perfect around him. That was largely the case last year. CeeDee Lamb missed three games, and the team's best offensive lineman was out for a single contest, but all else went according to plan. As a result, Prescott threw for 4,552 yards, 30 touchdowns, and only 10 interceptions. Things may not be so great for Prescott this time around because of George Pickens' status. Pickens gave Prescott the dynamic No. 2 receiver he had needed for a long time, but a contract dispute could cause Pickens to be displeased and quit on the team like he did toward the end of 2025. Prescott will still have great weapons to aid him, namely Lamb and tight end Jake Ferguson, but Pickens took the offense to another level last year when he tried hard, so he'll be missed if he's not available for any reason. If Pickens lets Dallas down, the team will be looking for more out of Ryan Flournoy, who had a magnificent game against the Lions late in 2025. Prescott also figures to be well protected again, which hasn't always been the case during his tenure in Dallas. The best offensive lineman mentioned earlier was Tyler Smith, one of the top guards in the NFL. He and Tyler Booker figure to form one of the top guard tandems in the NFL; Booker was a first-round pick last year who had a terrific rookie campaign. It's reasonable to expect Booker to improve his play now that he has experience. He and Smith will flank Cooper Beebe, another young lineman who thrived last year. Beebe, a third-round selection from the 2024 NFL Draft, has been a quality center thus far. He could also improve now that he has more experience." The tackle situation isn't as promising for the Cowboys. Tyler Guyton is a recent first-round pick, but he has struggled mightily thus far in his professional career. Right tackle Terence Steele has been better, but only by default. Despite the mediocre tackle play, Dallas was able to run the ball extremely well last year. Javonte Williams looked like an electric back for the Broncos during his rookie year, but wasn't the same following his ACL tear. That changed last year when he switched teams. Williams eclipsed 1,200 rushing yards, and with all three interior blockers returning, there's no reason to expect Williams to regress in 2026. 2026 Dallas Cowboys Defense: The Cowboys finished second in yardage gained last year, ranking only behind the Rams. Yet, Dallas won just seven games. The reason for this was the putrid defense, which surrendered the third-most yardage in the NFL. It's safe to say that Micah Parsons was missed. The Cowboys had some players who were able to generate some quarterback pressure last year from Jadeveon Clowney and Dante Fowler, but this wasn't a consistent phenomenon. They needed to obtain better pass rushers this season, and they did just that. They began by trading for Rashan Gary, who logged 7.5 sacks last year for the Packers. Gary has seemingly been around forever, but he's just 28, so he'll continue to play at a high level. He'll be in a three-man rotation with second-year Donovan Ezeiruaku and first-round rookie Malachi Lawrence. Ezeiruaku showed some major potential last year by registering 36 quarterback pressures despite playing about half the snaps. Lawrence, meanwhile, was a late riser who should be able to contribute in his initial season. The Cowboys received a huge boost from the defensive line at the trade deadline when they acquired Quinnen Williams. The former Jet was incredibly dominant on his new team, notching 32 quarterback pressures in only seven games with the Cowboys. Williams will start on the three-man defensive line with veteran Kenny Clark and newly signed Otito Ogbonnia. There's also fourth-round rookie LT Overton, who could compete for some snaps. Clark was decent last year, but he turns 31 in October, so he could decline a bit. Ogbonnia, conversely, was rather lackluster for the Chargers in 2025. Dallas also made changes to its secondary and linebacker corps. Three new players were added to the defensive backfield, including first-round rookie Caleb Downs. The Ohio State product is a dynamic talent and should be an instant upgrade for the Cowboys. He's a natural safety, but could play in the slot as well because Dallas has two starting-caliber safeties, including newly signed Jalen Thompson. The former Cardinal is coming off a solid season, and he will start next to Malik Hooker, who was decent in run support last year. The cornerbacks, meanwhile, received a boost in the wake of the Cobie Durant signing. Formerly of the Rams, Durant isn't a great player by any means, but he's certainly a big upgrade over the terrible players Dallas had at the position last year. He'll start opposite DaRon Bland, who is coming off an injury-ravaged campaign. Bland should be able to rebound in 2026. The new player in Dallas' linebacker group is Dee Winters. Signed over from the Rams, Winters is much like Durant. He's not very good at all, but he's still a lot better than what the Cowboys had at the position last season. He'll play next to DeMarvion Overshown, a very talented linebacker who has missed lots of recent action due to injury. 2026 Dallas Cowboys Schedule and Intangibles: Brandon Aubrey is arguably the best kicker in the NFL. He was 36-of-42 last year, hitting a ridiculous 11-of-17 from 50-plus. In the past two seasons, he's 25-of-34 from beyond 50. Bryan Anger is coming off a down year. He went from ranking second in net punting average to 13th, and he didn't place the ball inside the 20 very consistently. The Cowboys have a mixed non-divisional schedule. They have to take on the Ravens, Texans, 49ers, Seahawks, Rams and Jaguars. On the bright side, they also get the Buccaneers, Cardinals, Colts, and Titans. 2026 Dallas Cowboys Rookies: Go here for the Cowboys Rookie Forecast , a page with predictions like which rookie will bust and which rookie will become a solid starter. 2026 Dallas Cowboys Positional Rankings (1-5 stars): Quarterbacks Offensive Line Secondary Running Backs Defensive Line Special Teams Receivers Linebackers Coaching 2026 Dallas Cowboys Analysis: The Cowboys had one of the worst defenses in the NFL last year. This prevented them from reaching the playoffs despite owning the NFL's No. 2 offense. Dallas still has some holes on the defensive side of the ball, but it made some big improvements this offseason. As long as the Cowboys can maintain their offense close to the level they possessed in 2025, they'll be in postseason contention. In fact, a deep run into the playoffs can't be discounted. Projection: 9-8 (2nd in NFC East) 2025 Projection: 7-10. 2025 Actual Result: 7-9-1. 2024 Projection: 9-8. 2024 Actual Result: 7-10. 2023 Projection: 10-7. 2023 Actual Result: 12-5. 2022 Projection: 8-9. 2022 Actual Result: 12-5. 2021 Projection: 6-11. 2021 Actual Result: 12-5. 2020 Projection: 8-8. 2020 Actual Result: 6-10. 2019 Projection: 7-9. 2019 Actual Result: 8-8. 2018 Projection: 5-11. 2018 Actual Result: 10-6. 2017 Projection: 11-5. 2017 Actual Result: 9-7. 2016 Projection: 10-6. 2016 Actual Result: 13-3. NFL Draft Team Grade: A Grade Goals Entering the 2026 NFL Draft: The Cowboys have an explosive offense, but couldn't stop anyone last year. They added Rashan Gary to their defense, but still need one more superstar to make the appropriate improvement to give themselves a chance to make a playoff run in 2026. They'll need to consider moving up for an edge rusher or Sonny Styles and then use some other picks to add another potential defensive starter or two. 2026 NFL Draft Accomplishments: Dallas had six draft choices prior to Round 7, and five of those were spent on defense. This couldn't have been surprising to anyone, given how poor the Cowboys were defensively last year. But were the picks good? Well, the Cowboys landed the top safety in the draft at No. 11, and then followed that up with a very speedy edge rusher, whom they obtained after trading down three spots. The Cowboys landed another talented edge rusher in the third round and then acquired a ballhawking cornerback in the fourth frame. Caleb Downs, Malachi Lawrence, Jaishawn Barham, and Devin Moore all scored "B" or better individually. The Cowboys had to improve their defense, and that's exactly what they did. It wasn't a perfect draft, but Jerry Jones had a great weekend. NFL Draft Individual Grades: 11. Caleb Downs, S, Ohio State B Grade I don’t know why the Cowboys would move up to No. 11 when they had their choice of Caleb Downs and Rueben Bain. They just wasted two fifth-round picks, which isn’t the end of the world, but is still a poor use of resources. That spoils what would otherwise be an “A” pick because Downs is one of the top players in this class. The Cowboys desperately needed to find play-makers for their defense, and they certainly obtained one. 23. Malachi Lawrence, DE, Central Florida A- Grade I like that the Cowboys traded down three spots and were able to obtain a player they could have easily chosen at their natural selection. Malachi Lawrence is an explosive pass rusher who should be able to help Dallas get to the quarterback for a change. He’s a liability against the run, but Dallas needed a pass-rushing replacement for Micah Parsons. 92. Jaishawn Barham, DE/OLB, Michigan A Grade This is a great value pick for the Cowboys. I had Jaishawn Barham in the second round. He’s a linebacker who can generate a good pass rush. I wouldn’t be crazy about him dropping into coverage, however. 112. Drew Shelton, OT/G/C, Penn State A+ Grade The Cowboys needed to go defense, defense, defense, but they also needed depth on their offensive line. Drew Shelton is a perfect player for depth because he can play every single position. I thought Shelton could’ve gone much higher than Round 4 for that reason, so I love this selection. 114. Devin Moore, CB, Florida B+ Grade Devin Moore is a very tall cornerback with a knack for intercepting passes. This sounds great, but he has an extensive injury history. If he can get over it, the Cowboys could be getting a solid starter with this pick, but there’s definitely a major downside. 137. L.T. Overton, DE, Alabama A Grade LT Overton is a tough defender with good quickness and athleticism. I had him going in the third round, so the Cowboys are getting a steal and filling a position of need. It’s hard not to like this pick. 218. Anthony Smith, WR, East Carolina C Grade Anthony Smith is not someone I had in my top-400 prospects. The Cowboys probably would have been better off drafting players who can help their defense. --Offseason Reports Lander-- Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Buffalo Bills Carolina records.new_body: 2026 NFL Season Preview: Philadelphia Eagles - WalterFootball Skip to content Home 2026 NFL Season Preview: Philadelphia Eagles --Offseason Reports Lander-- Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Buffalo Bills Carolina Panthers Chicago Bears Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Dallas Cowboys Denver Broncos Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Kansas City Chiefs Los Angeles Chargers Los Angeles Rams Las Vegas Raiders Miami Dolphins Minnesota Vikings New England Patriots New Orleans Saints New York Giants New York Jets Philadelphia Eagles Pittsburgh Steelers Seattle Seahawks San Francisco 49ers Tampa Bay Buccaneers Tennessee Titans Washington Commanders Philadelphia Eagles 2026 NFL Season Preview: Veteran Additions: QB Andy Dalton, FB Carson Steele, WR Dontayvion Wicks, WR Marquise Brown, TE Johnny Mundt, OLB Jonathan Greenard, OLB A.J. Epenesa, OLB Arnold Ebiketie, CB Tariq Woolen. Early Draft Picks: WR Makai Lemon, TE Eli Stowers, OT Markel Bell. Eagles Rookie Forecast Offseason Losses: WR A.J. Brown, WR Jahan Dotson, TE Kylen Granson, G Brett Toth, DE Jaelan Phillips, DE Brandon Graham, OLB Josh Uche, OLB Azeez Ojulari, ILB Nakobe Dean, S Reed Blankenship. 2026 Philadelphia Eagles Offense: It's astonishing to think that some football analysts deemed the Jalen Hurts selection to be one of the worst draft picks of all time. Hurts, who was once benched in favor of Tua Tagovailoa at Alabama, became the MVP frontrunner during various points of the 2022 and 2023 NFL seasons. Hurts has piloted one of the most explosive offenses in the past couple of years, and he has been the key cog of the unstoppable fourth-down play, which is known as the Tush Push. The play has become so dominant that nearly two-thirds of the NFL wanted to ban it, but there weren't enough votes last offseason to do so. Hurts was not in MVP conversation in 2025 because he had a down passing year. He'll now be without his No. 1 target, A.J. Brown, but this could be a case of addition by subtraction because the two didn't get along very well. Brown even dogged it in the playoff loss to the 49ers with three horrible drops. DeVonta Smith will take over as the new main threat, and he should thrive in that role. Smith posted some excellent numbers when Brown was hurt during the 2023 season, so he's proven that he's capable of being the top threat. The Eagles signed some receivers to go with him - Dontayvion Wicks, Marquise Brown, Elijah Moore - but they'll be counting on Makai Lemon the most. The first-round pick is a talented player, but comes with some severe personality issues that nearly sunk his draft stock. If those persist, he will not be in the NFL for very long. The Eagles also used their second-round pick on an offensive player, choosing Eli Stowers. The young tight end set combine records with his elite athletic traits, and he'll be involved early with Dallas Goedert in two-tight end sets. Goedert has been highly productive when either Brown or Smith have been hurt, so he should have a big year, which could be his last in Philadelphia. With Brown gone, the Eagles may also use Saquon Barkley more as a receiver out of the backfield. Barkley is coming off a down year in the wake of his 2,000-yard campaign in 2024. Barkley is still young, so he could easily rebound with another stellar season, especially if the offensive line holds up well. The offensive line was a big issue last year. This was a surprise because Philadelphia arguably had the best blocking unit in the NFL in 2024, but that was far from the case this past season. Injuries played a role, as Lane Johnson missed eight games, including the home playoff loss to the 49ers. Landon Dickerson missed just two contests, but it was clear that he was not 100 percent. And then there was center Cam Jurgens, who was out for three games, but did not play well last year. There are some bright spots on the offensive line, however. If Johnson and Dickerson can remain healthy, they'll both perform at high levels, particularly the former, who is routinely ranked as the best right tackle in the NFL. Jordan Mailata, meanwhile, is one of the better blind-side protectors in the NFL. Right guard Tyler Steen was also a pleasant surprise as a first-year starter. 2026 Philadelphia Eagles Defense: The Eagles maintained a great offense when they won the Super Bowl in 2024, but their defense was also stellar. Philadelphia was impenetrable at times, completely clamping down on the Chiefs in the Super Bowl. They still maintained a great defensive unit this past season, but they allowed about 30 more yards per game compared to 2024. The pass rush wasn't as dominant this time. The Eagles still put plenty of pressure on opposing quarterbacks, but they were a bit weaker in that regard last year. Part of the reason was that the Eagles lost some key depth like Milton Williams and Josh Sweat, who signed with the Patriots and Cardinals, respectively, prior to 2025. Philadelphia took notice of this and traded for Jonathan Greenard in exchange for a pair of third-round picks. Greenard is a dynamic edge-rushing threat, and he'll form a dangerous trio of edge rushers with Nolan Smith and Jalyx Hunt. Smith was a bit of a disappointment last year, but Hunt managed to lead the team in sacks with 6.5. Philadelphia will continue to be strongest on the defensive line. The three-man group will be comprised of Jalen Carter, Jordan Davis, and Moro Ojomo. Carter and Davis are two of the better defensive linemen in the NFL, though Carter didn't play up to his standards last year. Ojomo, conversely, enjoyed a solid first year as a starter. If the Eagles can generate more quarterback pressure from Greenard and an improved Carter, it would obviously help a secondary that had some problems last season. They had no issues with Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean last year, as the duo served as one of the better cornerback tandems in the NFL. However, there was a problem opposite Mitchell. Adoree Jackson was used there, but he was atrocious at times. Tariq Woolen might be better by default, but he was benched last year in Seattle. While the Eagles added Woolen to their secondary, they lost Reed Blankenship. With the very skilled Blankenship gone, the Eagles will have to go with the duo of Andrew Mukuba and Marcus Epps at safety. Mukuba had a fine, but not great rookie year as a second-round selection. Epps, conversely, is a 30-year-old journeyman who struggled for the most part in 2026. Blankenship was one of two defenders the Eagles lost in the middle of their defense this offseason. The other was Nakobe Dean, who joined the Raiders. The talented linebacker was expendable, however, because Philadelphia has two dynamic players at the position. Zack Baun has developed into one of the better off-ball linebackers in the NFL. Jihaad Campbell, meanwhile, is a first-round pick from the 2025 NFL Draft. Campbell had a terrific rookie campaign in all facets, and he should continue to get better. 2026 Philadelphia Eagles Schedule and Intangibles: Jake Elliott made a name for himself when he drilled a 61-yard, game-winning kick against the Giants in 2017. He has regressed of late, however. He was just 20-of-27 in 2025. Braden Mann was 10th in net punting average in 2024 and 12th in that category in 2025. The Eagles have some tough games against the Bears, Rams, Jaguars, Seahawks, Texans, and 49ers. There are some easy games as well versus the Titans, Steelers, Cardinals, and Colts. 2026 Philadelphia Eagles Rookies: Go here for the Eagles Rookie Forecast , a page with predictions like which rookie will bust and which rookie will become a solid starter. 2026 Philadelphia Eagles Positional Rankings (1-5 stars): Quarterbacks Offensive Line Secondary Running Backs Defensive Line Special Teams Receivers Linebackers Coaching 2026 Philadelphia Eagles Analysis: The Eagles were the pick to win the Super Bowl on this Web site two years ago. That was not the case last season, but the Eagles could rebound if their offensive line improves. They have the offensive playmakers and the defense to contend, but the blocking was so much worse in 2025, and yet Philadelphia still won the division. The Eagles will be one of the favorites in the NFC if their offensive line woes are resolved. Projection: 11-6 (1st in NFC East) 2025 Projection: 14-3. 2025 Actual Result: 11-6. 2024 Projection: 13-4. 2024 Actual Result: 14-3. 2023 Projection: 13-4. 2023 Actual Result: 11-6. 2022 Projection: 12-5. 2022 Actual Result: 13-4. 2021 Projection: 4-13. 2021 Actual Result: 9-8. 2020 Projection: 9-7. 2020 Actual Result: 4-11-1. 2019 Projection: 12-4. 2019 Actual Result: 9-7. 2018 Projection: 13-3. 2018 Actual Result: 9-7. 2017 Projection: 12-4. 2017 Actual Result: 13-3. 2016 Projection: 5-11. 2016 Actual Result: 7-9. NFL Draft Team Grade: C Grade Goals Entering the 2026 NFL Draft: The Eagles need to concentrate on the offensive line and receiver corps. Lane Johnson is frequently injured and will retire soon, while A.J. Brown will likely be moved to the Patriots after June 1. Philadelphia also has a need at guard, and it wouldn't hurt if the team found an eventual replacement for Dallas Goedert. 2026 NFL Draft Accomplishments: Philadelphia drafted some talented players, but they may not all pan out like the team hopes. The primary example of this is Makai Lemon. If Lemon didn't have character concerns, he may have flirted with the top 10, but he had the worst combine interviews imaginable. If he behaves that way in the locker room, he's not going to be on an NFL roster for very long, no matter how good he is. There is precedent for this with Antonio Brown in his Raider and Buccaneer days, and I'd say Lemon would actually be worse for the locker room than Brown was if his behavior persists. Another example is Micah Morris. This is less serious because Morris was just a sixth-round pick, but he's another talented player who has issues. His problems are a lack of work ethic and poor conditioning. He could bust because of those reasons. Meanwhile, the Eagles wasted a fifth-round pick on Cole Payton, who doesn't have much starting experience and can't read defenses. It all sounds negative for the Eagles, but they made some positive draft picks as well. Eli Stowers figures to be a great threat over the middle of the field, while Markell Bell is talented enough to potentially replace Lane Johnson down the road despite being a third-round pick. He's raw, but can be developed. And speaking of raw, seventh-round defensive tackle Uar Bernard ran a 4.63 at 306 pounds. I'm sure he'll remind Philadelphia fans of a defensive version of Jordan Mailata. Despite some positives, I can't say I'm a fan of the Eagles' draft. There's high upside to it, but there's a very low floor with the Lemon, Morris, and Payton picks. NFL Draft Individual Grades: 20. Makai Lemon, WR, USC C Grade There are two sides to this pick. On one hand, the Eagles were able to land a dynamic weapon to help them deal with A.J. Brown’s departure. Lemon was good enough to go No. 13, so this value is great. On the other hand, Lemon had some seriously terrible and weird interviews at the combine. I don’t know if he’ll be welcome on an NFL team for the long term, so the Eagles may not even know how he conducted himself. This pick has great upside, but Lemon may not be around very long if he continues this behavior. 54. Eli Stowers, TE, Vanderbilt A Grade Dallas Goedert doesn’t have much time remaining in Philadelphia, so with A.J. Brown leaving, and Makai Lemon escorting himself out of the pros very soon, the Eagles needed pass-catchers to complement DeVonta Smith in the future. Eli Stowers is incredibly athletic and could have easily been chosen 10 or so picks earlier than this. 68. Markell Bell, OT, Miami B+ Grade The Eagles needed a tackle to succeed Lane Johnson. Markell Bell is a bit raw, but he’s made big strides every year at Miami, so he may continue to improve a lot and become a quality right tackle in the pros. This is a solid pick for the Eagles, who traded for Jonathan Greenard. I’ll have that grade posted once the third round concludes. 178. Cole Payton, QB, North Dakota State C- Grade Cole Payton needs work reading the field and developing a pocket presence, but he’s athletic and accurate. I can’t say I’m a fan of this pick, as there were better quarterbacks available. 207. Micah Morris, G, Georgia C+ Grade Micah Morris has good strength, quickness, and athleticism, but his work ethic and conditioning are poor. The Eagles have taken some major character concerns in this draft, so we’ll have to see if it works out for them. 244. Cole Wisniewski, S, Texas B Grade Cole Wisniewski is an instinctive safety, but needs to bulk up. He could be a fine backup and special teamer. I had him going 15 selections earlier, so the value is fine. 251. Uar Bernard, DT, Nigeria B+ Grade That’s right. Nigeria. Uar Bernard is one of the best pure athletes in this class. He’s 306 pounds, yet runs a 4.63. It’s unreal. He’s super raw, but could be developed into something special. 252. Keyshan James-Newby, DE/OLB, New Mexico B+ Grade Keyshawn James-Newby is undersized, but he’s explosive and has a high motor. I had him going in the sixth round, so the Eagles are getting good value with him, although he’s not nearly as exciting as the Nigerian prospect. --Offseason Reports Lander-- Arizona Cardinals Atlanta
