records.new_body: 2026 NFL Season Preview: New York Jets - WalterFootball Skip to content Home 2026 NFL Season Preview: New York Jets --Offseason Reports Lander-- Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Buffalo Bills Carolina Panthers Chicago Bears Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Dallas Cowboys Denver Broncos Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Kansas City Chiefs Los Angeles Chargers Los Angeles Rams Las Vegas Raiders Miami Dolphins Minnesota Vikings New England Patriots New Orleans Saints New York Giants New York Jets Philadelphia Eagles Pittsburgh Steelers Seattle Seahawks San Francisco 49ers Tampa Bay Buccaneers Tennessee Titans Washington Commanders New York Jets 2026 NFL Season Preview: Veteran Additions: QB Geno Smith, WR Tim Patrick, G Dylan Parham, DT David Onyemata, DT T'Vondre Sweat, OLB Joseph Ossai, OLB Kingsley Enagbare, ILB Demario Davis, CB Nahshon Wright, S Minkah Fitzpatrick, S Dane Belton. Draft Picks: OLB David Bailey, TE Kenyon Sadiq, WR Omar Cooper, CB D'Angelo Ponds, NT Darrell Jackson, QB Cade Klubnik. Jets Rookie Forecast Offseason Losses: QB Tyrod Taylor, TE Stone Smartt, TE Jelani Woods, G Alijah Vera-Tucker, G John Simpson, DT Jay Tufele, S Andre Cisco. 2026 New York Jets Offense: It's been a long time since the Jets have had any sort of stability at quarterback, but there is at least one ESPN analyst who believes that is about to change. This analyst called Geno Smith a "top-10 quarterback" prior to 2025. Smith was dreadful for the Raiders, but one poor year likely won't change that opinion. And sure, Smith compiled most of his positive yardage in garbage time when he was with the Seahawks, but the fact does remain that Smith is more stable than whatever the Jets had at quarterback last year, whether it was Justin Fields, Tyrod Taylor, or the anemic Brady Cook. To be fair to Smith, he had some of the worst blocking imaginable last year in Las Vegas. The Jets have a far superior offensive line compared to what the Raiders maintained, as two recent first-round picks will once again start at tackle. Olu Fashano has been a quality blind-side protector, but the better of the two tackles thus far is Armand Membou. Despite being a rookie last year, Membou was excellent on the right side. He has all the athleticism in the world for an offensive lineman, and the sky is the limit for him. Another Jets lineman with high potential was Alijah Vera-Tucker, but he spent too much time on the injury report. He's no longer on the roster, so the Jets will move forward with the trio of Josh Myers, Joe Tippmann, and the newly signed Dylan Parham in the interior. Tippmann is the best of the three, while Parham was the lone bright spot on the Raiders' front last year in the wake of Kolton Miller's injury. The glaring weakness is center Josh Myers, who should just be a backup. Smith didn't have much at his disposal as far as pass-catchers were concerned last year, aside from Brock Bowers, who also dealt with injuries. Once Jakobi Meyers was dealt, Smith had nothing to work with downfield in Las Vegas, but things will be radically different with his new team. Garrett Wilson is an incredibly talented, young receiver, while Adonai Mitchell has plenty of potential as someone who can make big plays down the field. The Jets also used one of their three first-round picks on Omar Cooper, who will be a big upgrade in the slot. The second of the Jets' opening-round selections was used on Kenyon Sadiq, a terrific tight end prospect. The Jets already had the very athletic Mason Taylor at the position, so they'll be able to utilize multi-tight end formations with Sadiq and Taylor creating havoc for opposing defenses. Smith's best weapon, aside from Wilson, is Breece Hall, who signed a big contract this offseason. Hall has a checkered injury history, but he's an incredibly gifted running back who can go the distance whenever he touches the ball. He is also a very effective receiver out of the backfield. 2026 New York Jets Defense: Much was expected of the Jets defense last year in the wake of the Aaron Glenn hiring. New York had an elite defense under Robert Saleh for a couple of seasons, but regressed once Saleh was fired. Glenn, who did a great job with the Lions' stop unit, was supposed to fix things, but he made everything worse instead. The Jets surrendered the eighth-most yardage in the NFL last year, even though they had mega talents like Quinnen Williams and Sauce Gardner on their roster for half the season. The Jets dealt both of those players, but they brought in so many seasoned veterans this offseason to aid Glenn in his second year. There will be two new starters on the three-man front: T'Vondre Sweat and David Onyemata. Sweat is a young run plugger who can apply some pressure for a nose tackle, while Onyemata is great in every regard. They, along with Harrison Phillips, will provide the Jets with a much better defensive line than what the team had in that area last season. Every grouping in the front seven was addressed this offseason. The edge rush was bolstered by the No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, David Bailey. The Texas Tech product was the best pass rusher in the class, and he figures to be a force for the Jets. His bookend will be former first-round selection Will McDonald, who notched a team-high eight sacks last year. Bailey and McDonald will create plenty of havoc for opposing quarterbacks. The new player at inside linebacker is Demario Davis, who is a complete wonder because he has continued to perform on a high level despite his advanced age. Davis will turn 38 at the end of the 2026 season, yet he's coming off an incredible year with the Saints. Unless he regresses, he'll provide the Jets with far better play than what they had at inside linebacker last year. Davis will start next to Jamien Sherwood, a player who thrives against the run but can be beaten in coverage. New York added some talent in the secondary as well. The big name is Minkah Fitzpatrick, who happened to be Miami's top defender last year. Fitzpatrick turns 30 in November, but he's obviously playing at the top of his game. He'll be a huge upgrade next to Andre Cisco, an athletic safety who missed nine games in 2025. Nahshon Wright is another new addition, and he'll be an upgrade over what the Jets had at cornerback following the Gardner trade last season. Wright is not nearly the star Gardner is, but he's a solid starter. He'll play opposite Brandon Stephens, the lone bright spot in New York's secondary during the second half of 2025. Another new cornerback, D'Angelo Ponds, will operate in the slot. He's a second-round rookie with potential, but it's unclear how he'll perform right away. 2026 New York Jets Schedule and Intangibles: Jason Sanders is the Jets' new kicker. Sanders has had success in the past as Miami's kicker. Punter Austin McNamara had a solid rookie year, finishing eighth in net punting, all while constantly placing the oppositon inside the 20. The Jets have a fourth-place schedule, but they still have some tough opponents like the Lions, Bears, Chargers, Broncos, and of course, the Patriots and Bills twice each. 2026 New York Jets Rookies: Go here for the Jets Rookie Forecast , a page with predictions like which rookie will bust and which rookie will become a solid starter. 2026 New York Jets Positional Rankings (1-5 stars): Quarterbacks Offensive Line Secondary Running Backs Defensive Line Special Teams Receivers Linebackers Coaching 2026 New York Jets Analysis: Many publications list the Jets among the worst teams in the NFL, but their evaluations are incorrect. Geno Smith stinks, and there are a couple of weaknesses, but the Jets have some explosive playmakers, a solid offensive line, and quality veterans on the defensive side of the ball to keep them competitive in most games this year. Projection: 6-11 (3rd in AFC East) 2025 Projection: 7-10. 2025 Actual Result: 3-14. 2024 Projection: 11-6. 2024 Actual Result: 5-12. 2023 Projection: 12-5. 2023 Actual Result: 7-10. 2022 Projection: 3-14. 2022 Actual Result: 7-10. 2021 Projection: 4-13. 2021 Actual Result: 4-13. 2020 Projection: 3-13. 2020 Actual Result: 2-14. 2019 Projection: 10-6. 2019 Actual Result: 7-9. 2018 Projection: 5-11. 2018 Actual Result: 4-12. 2017 Projection: 2-14. 2017 Actual Result: 5-11. 2016 Projection: 6-10. 2016 Actual Result: 5-11. NFL Draft Team Grade: A Grade Goals Entering the 2026 NFL Draft: The Jets have holes everywhere. They need a franchise quarterback, but won't have the chance to land one. They can at least set it up so that they have a friendlier environment for the one they draft in 2027. Interior line help and receivers are needed. The defense must be overhauled as well. 2026 NFL Draft Accomplishments: Unlike the Raiders, the Jets understood that they have to find weapons for their franchise quarterback, even if they don't have one right now. They will eventually have one - I have them selecting Arch Manning in my 2027 NFL Mock Draft - and when they do, that signal-caller will be put into a great situation. The Jets used their top pick on David Bailey to strengthen the defense, but they went to work on their skill players after that. They obtained nice values with Kenyon Sadiq and Omar Cooper to complement Garrett Wilson. The Sadiq pick was panned by some clueless publications, but he'll likely be a terrific intermediate threat for Manning or whichever quarterback the Jets land next year. Cooper was a nice find at the end of Round 1. Following the Sadiq and Cooper selections, the Jets went back to focusing on their poor defense. They made a number of quality selections, with every single pick scoring a "B" or higher in the individual NFL Draft Grades page. These picks won't make the Jets much better right away because they still have no quarterback, but the front office accomplished its goal of setting up its next franchise signal caller for success. NFL Draft Individual Grades: 2. David Bailey, DE, Texas Tech A Grade David Bailey is the right pick. He is a proven edge rusher, while Arvell Reese is a one-year starter who happens to be a project because he has no natural position. Bailey will give the Jets a good chance to rattle Josh Allen and Drake Maye. 16. Kenyon Sadiq, TE, Oregon A Grade Multi-tight end formations have been en vogue lately, so this pick makes sense despite the Jets having a talented tight end in Mason Taylor. Kenyon Sadiq figures to be a great weapon for the Jets, who are starved for play-makers outside of Garrett Wilson. Arch Manning has to love this selection because he’s currently slotted to the Jets in our 2027 NFL Mock Draft . 30. Omar Cooper, WR, Indiana A Grade The Jets are giving Arch Manning quite the arsenal, selecting Omar Cooper after getting Kenyon Sadiq. They were starved for offensive firepower, and they may now have plenty of it. Cooper should be a big upgrade across from Garrett Wilson, and he provides with plenty of value because he easily could have gotten him in the 16-21 range. 50. D’Angelo Ponds, CB, Indiana B Grade D’Angelo Ponds has size issues, but if it wasn’t for those, he would’ve been a first-round pick. He was terrific at Indiana and has a good chance of being a big upgrade for a Jets secondary that lost Sauce Gardner. 103. Darrell Jackson, DT, Florida State B+ Grade Darrell Jackson is a big nose tackle who can offer a bit of pass-rushing upside, and I thought there was a chance he’d go in the third round. This is a solid pick by the Jets, who have had issues stopping the run for a long time. 110. Cade Klubnik, QB, Clemson B Grade The Jets were screwed when Dante Moore decided to go back to college. They now have to tank for Arch Manning, but Cade Klubnik is a fine option here in case he ends up being a steal. I’m neutral on him, as he’s accurate but doesn’t have a strong arm. 188. Anez Cooper, G, Miami B+ Grade Anez Cooper is strong at the point of attack. He’s a stout run blocker. The Jets needed guard help entering the 2026 NFL Draft, and they found a solid prospect whom I mocked a round earlier. 228. V.J. Payne, S, Kansas State A- Grade V.J. Payne is a big safety who possesses great strength and some ability to play deep free safety. This has been a troubled position for a while, so the Jets did well to secure a prospect who could have gone earlier. I had Payne slotted near the end of Round 5. --Offseason Reports Lander-- Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Buffalo Bills Carolina Panthers Chicago Bears Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Early Draft Picks: OT/G Kadyn Proctor, CB Chris Johnson, ILB Jacob Rodriguez, WR Caleb Douglas, WR Chris Bell, TE Will Kacmarek, DE Trey Moore, ILB Kyle Louis. Dolphins Rookie Forecast Offseason Losses: QB Tua Tagovailoa, FB Alec Ingold, WR Tyreek Hill, WR Jaylen Waddle, WR Nick Westbrook-Ikhine, TE Darren Waller, OT Larry Borom, G James Daniels, G Liem Eichenberg, G Cole Strange, G Daniel Brunskill, DE Bradley Chubb, DT Benito Jones, ILB K.J. Britt, CB Rasul Douglas, CB Kader Kohou, S Ifeatu Melifonwu, S Ashtyn Davis, K Jason Sanders, P Jake Bailey. 2026 Miami Dolphins Offense: Miami's offseason was a perplexing one. The Dolphins signed Malik Willis away from the Packers in what appeared to be an attempt to build around a young quarterback who had some bright moments backing up "No Cookie" Jordan Love in Green Bay. However, the Dolphins then seemed to abandon that idea when they ditched their talented veteran receivers in favor of scrubs and young players. Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle once formed an explosive duo, but they're both gone. The Dolphins signed non-talents like Jalen Tolbert and Tutu Atwell, as they and the returning duo from last year, Malik Washington and Theo Wease Jr., will compete with rookies Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell for playing time in what appears to be the worst receiver corps in the NFL. Big things were expected from Washington last year when Hill got hurt, but he disappointed. Wease had a couple of nice games down the stretch, but it's not clear if he's a true NFL talent. Douglas and Bell have loads of potential, though Bell is coming off a torn ACL and may not be ready for Week 1. Douglas has an elite size-speed combination and possesses plenty of upside. Willis will also be able to throw to athletic tight end Greg Dulcich. Willis' top target will be De'Von Achane. The dynamic back is just as much of a receiver as a runner. Achane has caught 145 passes in the past two years, and given that both Hill and Waddle are gone, his role as a receiver should increase despite Mike McDaniels' departure. Achane, however, could be challenged to reach the 1,350 rushing yards he accumulated last year, given that the Dolphins will be in far more deficits. One area that was upgraded this offseason was the left side of the offensive line. Kadyn Proctor was drafted at No. 12 overall. With Patrick Paul and Austin Jackson entrenched as the starters at tackle, Proctor will begin his career at left guard before potentially moving to tackle in the future. Paul is a young tackle who has shown plenty of potential, so if Proctor lives up to his upside, and center Aaron Brewer continues to perform on a high level, Miami's left side of the offensive line should be solid. The right side of the offensive line is a different story, however. Jackson is highly injury-prone, and isn't very good when healthy anyway. Right guard Jonah Savaiinaea is young - he was chosen in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft - but he was one of the worst starting offensive linemen in the NFL last year. 2026 Miami Dolphins Defense: It wasn't too long ago that the Dolphins had a strong defense. They ranked 10th in yardage allowed two years ago and improved to fourth in that category in 2024. That ranking plummeted to 22nd, as the Dolphins lost key defensive pieces. Things have only gotten worse since then. Miami dealt its top edge rusher, Jaelan Phillips, to the Eagles at the trade deadline. Their pass rush diminished as a result, but they still had other talented players to get to the quarterback like Bradley Chubb and Chop Robinson. Now, Chubb is gone after signing with the Bills. This leaves Robinson as the only viable starter. The Dolphins signed Josh Uche and David Ojabo to compete with fourth-round rookie Trey Moore to be the bookend for Robinson. None of these options seem very promising, and frankly, it's not like Robinson is a sure thing either. He logged just four sacks last season, though he has a lot of potential as a recent first-round selection. The Dolphins' top returning pass rusher plays in the interior of the defensive line. That would be Zach Sieler, a very versatile player. Sieler had 5.5 sacks last season, and given the departure of talent on the edge, he'll need to have a much better year to give the Dolphins any sort of hope of rushing the quarterback consistently. Kenneth Grant, last year's first-round pick, will also need to step up his game after a dreadful rookie campaign. Miami's poor pass rush will put extra stress on a secondary that also lost talent this offseason. The Dolphins' best defender last year, Minkah Fitzpatrick, is no longer on the roster. The team's top cornerback from 2025, Rasul Douglas, is also gone. This defensive backfield can only be described as a train wreck. With Fitzpatrick off the roster, Miami's starting safeties will be pedestrian journeyman Lonnie Johnson and 2025 fifth-round pick Dante Trader, who struggled in brief action last year. The Dolphins at least used a first-round pick to address the cornerback group, selecting Chris Johnson late in the opening frame. Johnson is far from a finished product, however, so it may take him some time to develop. He'll start opposite JuJu Brents, who played only four games due to injury last season. At nickel, Jason Marshall will have to improve his play after being one of the worst slot corners in the NFL this past year. The strength of the Dolphins' defense is the linebacker corps, and not just by default. Jordyn Brooks is a tremendous player in his prime, while Tyrel Dodson is a quality two-down linebacker who thrives in run support. Miami used a second-round pick on Jacob Rodriguez to compete for snaps. 2026 Miami Dolphins Schedule and Intangibles: Jason Sanders is no longer Miami's kicker. The team signed Zane Gonzalez over from the Falcons. Gonzalez was 19-of-22 last year, drilling 7-of-9 from 50-plus. The Dolphins also imported their punter from the Falcons. Bradley Pinion was just 24 in net punting last year, but did a great job of pinning the opposition inside the 20. Miami has some winnable games on its schedule: at Raiders, at Vikings (if Kyler Murray is out), at Colts, and the two games against the Jets. 2026 Miami Dolphins Rookies: Go here for the Dolphins Rookie Forecast , a page with predictions like which rookie will bust and which rookie will become a solid starter. 2026 Miami Dolphins Positional Rankings (1-5 stars): Quarterbacks Offensive Line Secondary Running Backs Defensive Line Special Teams Receivers Linebackers Coaching 2026 Miami Dolphins Analysis: The Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL, but this is all by design. Miami's ownership has a history of intentionally tanking, and it's quite clear that the organization is trying to put itself in position to obtain Arch Manning atop the 2027 NFL Draft. Projection: 2-15 (4th in AFC East) 2025 Projection: 5-12. 2025 Actual Result: 7-10. 2024 Projection: 10-7. 2024 Actual Result: 8-9. 2023 Projection: 11-6. 2023 Actual Result: 11-6. 2022 Projection: 8-9. 2022 Actual Result: 9-8. 2021 Projection: 10-7. 2021 Actual Result: 9-8. 2020 Projection: 4-12. 2020 Actual Result: 10-6. 2019 Projection: 1-15. 2019 Actual Result: 5-11. 2018 Projection: 4-12. 2018 Actual Result: 7-9. 2017 Projection: 7-9. 2017 Actual Result: 6-10. 2016 Projection: 4-12. 2016 Actual Result: 10-6. NFL Draft Team Grade: B Grade Goals Entering the 2026 NFL Draft: The Dolphins are in a rebuild. They have so little talent on their roster that every position is a need, excluding the two in the backfield. They need to draft the best player available, though at least one early selection needs to be used on a receiver to give Malik Willis a chance. 2026 NFL Draft Accomplishments: For a while, it looked like the Dolphins disagreed that they needed to give Malik Willis any sort of receiving threat. They exited Round 1 without a receiver, though they were able to land a highly needed offensive tackle in Kadyn Proctor after moving down one spot and securing two fifth-round picks. The Dolphins then moved up for a cornerback when that was an unnecessary transaction. Just when it appeared as though the Dolphins would squander the 2026 NFL Draft, the team came through with one of the best values of the entire draft when they secured Chris Bell in the third round. Bell has ridiculous talent, but slipped because of injuries. It sounds like he'll be ready for the start of the season, so Miami lucked out that other teams foolishly passed on him. The Dolphins also used another second-day pick on a receiver, but that was a reach in Caleb Douglas. An even bigger reach was third-round blocking tight end Will Kacmarek. Aside from Bell, the best value the Dolphins obtained was second-round linebacker Jacob Rodriguez. He, Johnson, Trey Moore, and Kyle Louis should be able to help a putrid defense. Meanwhile, fifth-round receiver Kevin Coleman Jr. will provide some juice to the receiver group. Seventh-rund edge Max Llewllyn was a steal. Despite the rocky start, the Dolphins rebounded and had a strong draft. They had enough missteps to take them out of the "A" range, so a solid "B" feels right. NFL Draft Individual Grades: 12. Kadyn Proctor, OT, Alabama A- Grade The Lions were really hoping Kadyn Proctor would fall to them, but the Dolphins would have none of that. Proctor is risky with his weight, but there’s a ton of upside with this pick for the Dolphins, who have needed offensive line help for years. On top of that, they also picked up two fifth-round picks for free. Nice job! 27. Chris Johnson, CB, San Diego State D Grade Chris Johnson had gotten mid-round grades not too long ago, so this rise was unexpected. Still, it’s not a surprise that Chris Johnson went in the first round. I have two issues with this pick. First, there was no need to trade up for Johnson with several talented corners available. Second, Miami failed to address the weakest receiver room in the NFL in the first round, which is something they needed to do to make sure Malik Willis succeeds. 43. Jacob Rodriguez, LB, Texas Tech A+ Grade I loved the two top linebackers expected to go in this round. Jacob Rodriguez is an extremely instinctive linebacker who will undoubtedly make Miami’s defense much better. The rudderless Dolphins desperately needed a player like this, and you can say that they’re getting value because there was some chatter that Rodriguez could go at the end of Round 1. 75. Caleb Douglas, WR, Texas Tech D Grade Yikes! The Dolphins are addressing a need with a tall receiver, but that’s where the positives end. Caleb Douglas has terrible hands and happens to be a very weak receiver who needs to bulk up. He’s a project, and I had him going in the sixth round. 87. Will Kacmarek, TE, Ohio State MILLEN Grade I hate to issue another Millen grade because it seems excessive, but I didn’t have Will Kacmarek being drafted. He’s a blocking tight end who doesn’t offer much as a receiver. Tight ends like this are a dime a dozen. This is a waste of a third-round pick. 94. Chris Bell, WR, Louisville A+ Grade What a steal! Chris Bell was one of my favorite prospects on Day 2, and I thought he was good enough to go in the 30s. He’s an explosive receiver who makes big plays. He fell because of injury and character concerns, but if he can stay clean, he could emerge as Miami’s No. 1 receiver. 130. Trey Moore, DE, Texas B- Grade Trey Moore struggles in coverage, but has a great track record of generating pressure on the quarterback. The Dolphins had interest in Rueben Bain at No. 11, so it makes sense for them to take an edge rusher to replace Jalean Phillips. I had Moore in the fifth round. 138. Kyle Louis, OLB, Pittsburgh B- Grade Kyle Louis is a versatile linebacker with strong pass-rushing ability, but he’s undersized. He could be used as safety. He doesn’t have a set position, which is a problem, but the Dolphins might be able to figure out how to use him. 158. Michael Taaffe, S, Texas B Grade Michael Taaffe was strong in run support for the Longhorns. Miami’s safety situation is quite dismal, so any help is welcome. I had Taaffe going in this range. 177. Kevin Coleman Jr., WR, Missouri B Grade Kevin Coleman is an undersized receiver, but could play in the slot while doubling as a kick returner. The Dolphins have such a weak group of receivers that Coleman could contribute right away. I had him going five picks earlier, so the range makes sense. 180. Seydou Traore, TE, Mississippi State D Grade Seydou Traore is not someone I had in my top-400 prospects. He’s a tweener receiver-tight end, and I don’t think he has a role in the NFL. He’s an athletic prospect, but where does he play besides special teams? 200. D.J. Campbell, G, Texas B Grade D.J. Campbell had a lot of starting experience in college, but was penalized often. The Dolphins needed some offensive line depth and competition, and this range makes sense for Campbell. 238. Max Llewellyn, DE, Iowa A Grade Max Llewellyn improved his pass-rushing ability throughout his collegiate career. He has plenty of upside, as he could continue to improve. I love the potential here for the Dolphins; I had Llewellyn slotted in the fifth round. --Offseason Reports Lander-- Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Buffalo Bills Carolina Panthers Moore, G Austin Corbett, DE Bradley Chubb, DE Mike Danna, S Chauncey Gardner-Johnson, S Geno Stone. Draft Picks: DE T.J. Parker, CB Davison Igbinosun, ILB Kaleb Elarms-Orr, WR Skyler Bell, OT Jude Bowry. Bills Rookie Forecast Offseason Losses: QB Mitchell Trubisky, FB Reggie Gilliam, WR Curtis Samuel, G David Edwards, DE Joey Bosa, DE A.J. Epenesa, DT DaQuan Jones, DT Larry Ogunjobi, ILB Matt Milano, ILB Shaq Thompson, CB Taron Johnson, CB Tre'Davious White, CB Darius Slay, S Taylor Rapp, S Jordan Poyer, S Cam Lewis, K Matt Prater. 2026 Buffalo Bills Offense: Josh Allen and Stefon Diggs formed a deadly combination when they played together prior to 2024. Following Diggs' departure, Allen lacked a No. 1 receiver, which capped the absolute upside of Buffalo's offense. The Bills didn't do anything about this following the 2024 season, but they made amends for that mistake with a trade for D.J. Moore. Buffalo's decision to swap a second-round pick for Moore was panned by many analysts on social media, but it was a great decision. Moore is coming off a down year, but still has a couple of seasons remaining until he turns 30. He is very dangerous whenever he gets his hands on the ball. He didn't take well to Ben Johnson's offense, which would explain the regression in 2025. He'll be motivated to prove that the Bears were at fault for his poor season. Khalil Shakir will continue to be a big part of the scoring attack as the team's slot receiver. Joshua Palmer, Keon Coleman, and fourth-round rookie Skyler Bell figure to be involved as well, but there's not much hope with them. In addition to the receivers, Allen will be able to utilize his two talented tight ends, though there's concern at the position. Dalton Kincaid is not healthy. He's dealing with a knee issue, and the coaching staff stated that he will be on a limited snap count this year. Kincaid won't play as much in 2026, but he'll make his snaps count. There's also Dawson Knox, who posted big numbers last year when Kincaid was sidelined. Allen's best threat will continue to be James Cook. The dynamic back has been a touchdown machine over the past two seasons, and there's no reason to believe that will change. Cook, who rushed for 1,621 yards last year, has 109 receptions over the past three seasons. Allen and Cook were helped by a solid offensive line. The Bills have an excellent tandem of tackles with Dion Dawkins and Spencer Brown. Dawkins is the best blocker on the line, while Brown, a recent third-round pick, has developed into a quality right tackle. The interior blocking is not as good as the tackle play. In fact, Buffalo's top interior blocker from last year, David Edwards, signed a $61 million deal with the Saints. The Bills brought in Austin Corbett to replace Edwards. Corbett is a fine blocker, but he won't be as good as Edwards. The other starters in the interior figure to be Connor McGovern and O'Cyrus Torrence. McGovern is a fine player, while Torrence has struggled thus far in his career. 2026 Buffalo Bills Defense: The Bills traded for D.J. Moore, but this wasn't the only highly impactful move they made this offseason. They also made a major signing, acquiring Bradley Chubb. The former Bronco and Dolphin edge rusher can be a dominant player. He logged 8.5 sacks last year despite coming off a torn ACL. Now another year removed from that injury, Chubb should be a double-digit sack artist like he was in 2023. Chubb will join an edge rotation with Greg Rousseau, newly signed Mike Danna, and second-round rookie T.J. Parker. Rousseau had seven sacks in 2025, though he notched an impressive 55 quarterback pressures. Danna was once considered a young, promising player, but never lived up to it. Parker had a disappointing final year in college, but has loads of potential. The Bills will be hoping for more pressure from their three-man front. They should get that with the talented Ed Oliver, though it remains to be seen how Oliver will be able to play in the team's new 3-4 formation. The other starters on the front are slated to be T.J. Sanders and Deone Walker, who were chosen in the second and fourth rounds of the 2025 NFL Draft, respectively. This is not good news because neither was particularly effective last year. Walker was a mediocre player who could make a jump, but Sanders was dreadful. Any sort of bolstered pass rush obviously will be great for the secondary. The Bills added numerous players to this area of their defense, though Christian Benford and Maxwell Hairston will reprise their roles as the starting outside cornerbacks. Benford is normally a terrific player, but is coming off a bit of a down year. He's only 25, so he could easily rebound. Meanwhile, Hairston missed six games in his rookie campaign, but once he returned, he played relatively well. Buffalo added second-round pick Davison Igbinosun for depth purposes, as well as Dee Alford to play the nickel in the wake of Taron Johnson's departure. Johnson was great for the Bills, so he'll be missed. Alford wasn't nearly as good last year. Buffalo also signed a new safety, obtaining Chauncey Gardner-Johnson via free agency. Gardner-Johnson is a talented player, but has a history of injuries and locker room issues. Teams often have short-term success with him, so perhaps the Bills will experience the same phenomenon. Gardner-Johnson will start next to Cole Bishop, an extremely talented safety who is only 23. While the Bills will continue to play well against the pass, their inability to stop the run could continue to be an issue. Matt Milano, once a great linebacker, struggled mightily due to injury last year, and is now off the team. The lone remaining starter at the position, Terrel Bernard, has regressed in each of his three years as a starter, so that's a trend he'll need to reverse. The other linebackers competing for playing time are Dorian Williams and fourth-round rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr. Williams struggled in several starts last year, so this figures to once again be a problem area for Buffalo. 2026 Buffalo Bills Schedule and Intangibles: Tyler Bass had hip and groin injuries, causing him to miss all of 2025. He'll be back as the team's kicker. He was 24-of-29 in 2024. Buffalo has a new punter. Seventh-round rookie Tommy Doman Jr. will handle the punting duties. The Bills have a very difficult schedule. They open up against the Texans, Lions, Chargers, Patriots, and Rams. They later battle the Ravens, Chiefs, Bears, and Broncos. 2026 Buffalo Bills Rookies: Go here for the Bills Rookie Forecast , a page with predictions like which rookie will bust and which rookie will become a solid starter. 2026 Buffalo Bills Positional Rankings (1-5 stars): Quarterbacks Offensive Line Secondary Running Backs Defensive Line Special Teams Receivers Linebackers Coaching 2026 Buffalo Bills Analysis: The Bills found a No. 1 receiver for Josh Allen and enhanced their pass rush by signing Bradley Chubb. They have a very difficult schedule, but they're one of the best teams in the NFL. If their run defense is better than expected, they'll have a good chance to finally advance to the Super Bowl. Projection: 13-4 (1st in AFC East) 2025 Projection: 15-2. 2025 Actual Result: 12-5. 2024 Projection: 11-6. 2024 Actual Result: 13-4. 2023 Projection: 13-4. 2023 Actual Result: 11-6. 2022 Projection: 14-3. 2022 Actual Result: 13-3. 2021 Projection: 14-3. 2021 Actual Result: 11-6. 2020 Projection: 11-5. 2020 Actual Result: 13-3. 2019 Projection: 9-7. 2019 Actual Result: 10-6. 2018 Projection: 3-13. 2018 Actual Result: 6-10. 2017 Projection: 5-11. 2017 Actual Result: 9-7. 2016 Projection: 8-8. 2016 Actual Result: 7-9. NFL Draft Team Grade: C+ Grade Goals Entering the 2026 NFL Draft: Even though the Bills traded for D.J. Moore, they still could stand to add one more receiver so they can fully turn their weakness into a strength. The Bills also need to address their putrid run defense by acquiring defensive tackle and linebacker help. 2026 NFL Draft Accomplishments: Buffalo fans were understandably frustrated on Thursday because their team traded down twice from No. 26 and failed to make a pick in the first round. While they acquired some draft capital, they also allowed the Patriots to secure the final first-round tackle prospect in the first round, which could end up being detrimental in future matchups. The Bills eventually picked at No. 35, taking T.J. Parker. This was a solid selection, but Buffalo's other second-round choice was not, as it was a major reach on Davison Igbinosun. Even worse, the Bills squandered whatever capital they earned in an irresponsible trade up for him. They probably could have traded down and acquired him instead. Trades and Igbinosun aside, the Bills had a fine draft. I really like what they did on Day 3, securing plenty of quality values, including Jude Bowry, Skyler Bell, and Jalon Kilgore. Kilgore, in particular, was a tremendous bargain because he could have gone at the end of Round 2 with no complaints. The Bills definitely made a couple of mistakes in this draft - namely helping their arch rival and top competitor - but they didn't do a bad job overall. NFL Draft Individual Grades: 35. T.J. Parker, DE, Clemson B Grade This is a fine pick, as the Bills know that they need to battle some great quarterbacks in the AFC. T.J. Parker has a load of potential and was once viewed as a first-round prospect, but didn’t have a great final year. Perhaps he can live up to expectations in Buffalo. I personally would have preferred a receiver or one of the linebackers. 62. Davison Igbinosun, CB, Ohio State D Grade I’m not sure why the Bills thought they had to trade up for a cornerback I had in the fourth round. They could have just taken Davison Igbinosun in the third frame, and it wouldn’t have been that great either. Igbinosun is a big corner, but was heavily penalized in school. 102. Jude Bowry, OT/G, Boston College B+ Grade The Bills lost personnel on the offensive line this offseason, so it makes sense for them to make this pick. Jude Bowry can play both tackle and guard, and I thought he’d go in the Round 3-4 range. 125. Skyler Bell, WR, Connecticut A- Grade Another receiver had to be added to turn a weakness into a potential strength. Skyler Bell is a speedy receiver, but is weak and needs to bulk up for the NFL. I had him going in the third round, so there’s some value with this choice. 126. Kaleb Elarms-Orr, ILB, TCU B+ Grade I had Kaleb Elarms-Orr going at this exact pick in my mock draft, so I have to like it. The Bills desperately needed linebacker help, and Elarms-Orr is a fine pick here as an athletic linebacker with upside. 167. Jalon Kilgore, CB/S, South Carolina A+ Grade Jalon Kilgore is a very versatile and talented defensive back who can play cornerback and safety. He should have gone much earlier than this – I had him in the second and third round of my mock drafts – so the Bills are getting a steal in the middle of Round 5. 181. Zane Durant, DT, Penn State B Grade Zane Durant is a quick defensive tackle, but is a bit undersized. He can potentially help the Bills generate more quarterback pressure. I had him going in Round 6, so the range makes sense. 220. Toriano Pride Jr., CB, Missouri B Grade Toriano Pride Jr. has great speed, but is undersized and struggles to tackle. I had Pride going around this range. Buffalo has had depth issues at cornerback, so pride could help in that regard. 239. Tommy Doman, P, Florida C+ Grade Nothing exciting to say with this pick. The Bills took a player who gives the ball back to the other team. 241. Ar’maj Reed-Adams, G, Texas A&M B+ Grade Ar’maj Reed-Adams is a strong and lengthy blocker, but he’s not quick and commits lots of penalties. Protecting Josh Allen is paramount, so offensive line depth is welcome. I had Reed-Adams in the sixth round. --Offseason Reports Lander-- Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Buffalo Bills Carolina Panthers Chicago Bears Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns records.new_body: 2026 NFL Season Preview: New England Patriots - WalterFootball Skip to content Home 2026 NFL Season Preview: New England Patriots --Offseason Reports Lander-- Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Buffalo Bills Carolina Panthers Chicago Bears Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Dallas Cowboys Denver Broncos Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Kansas City Chiefs Los Angeles Chargers Los Angeles Rams Las Vegas Raiders Miami Dolphins Minnesota Vikings New England Patriots New Orleans Saints New York Giants New York Jets Philadelphia Eagles Pittsburgh Steelers Seattle Seahawks San Francisco 49ers Tampa Bay Buccaneers Tennessee Titans Washington Commanders New England Patriots 2026 NFL Season Preview: Veteran Additions: FB Reggie Gilliam, WR A.J. Brown, WR Romeo Doubs, G Alijah Vera-Tucker, DE Dre'Mont Jones, ILB K.J. Britt, CB Kindle Vildor, S Kevin Byard, S Mike Brown. Early Draft Picks: OT Caleb Lomu, DE Gabe Jacas, TE Eli Raridon. Patriots Rookie Forecast Offseason Losses: QB Joshua Dobbs, RB Antonio Gibson, WR Stefon Diggs, TE Austin Hooper, OT Vederian Lowe, DE K'Lavon Chaisson, DT Khyiris Tonga, OLB Anfernee Jennings, ILB Jack Gibbens, S Jaylinn Hawkins. 2026 New England Patriots Offense: It was predicted in this space last year that Drake Maye would have a Josh Allen-type "big leap" in his second season, but no one could have predicted how colossal his leap was. Maye transformed from an inconsistent rookie who showed flashes amid many mistakes to the MVP runner-up. Maye was incredible in his second year, and the scary thing for the opposition is that he can only get better with more experience and a bolstered supporting cast. The Patriots needed to give Maye two things. The first was a No. 1 receiver. Maye had good chemistry with Stefon Diggs, but Diggs is on the downside of his career. It was no secret that the Patriots had plans to acquire A.J. Brown, as everyone discovered via New England's top beat reporter. The trade was made on June 1, with the Patriots dealing a 2028 first-round pick for the stud receiver. Brown has never caught passes from an elite passer like Maye, and given how top receivers tend to produce in Josh McDaniels' offense, Brown could have his best season ever. Brown will also make the other skill players better because he'll be drawing so much attention from the defense. Romeo Doubs, signed over from Green Bay, will be a reliable slot receiver, while Kayshon Boutte and Mack Hollins will continue to make plays downfield. Hunter Henry, meanwhile, may lose touchdowns because of Brown's presence, but he'll still be a dependable target over the middle of the field. The second thing the Patriots had to address was the offensive line. Maye was sacked at least five times in every playoff game. Part of that was on rookie left tackle Will Campbell, but it was clear that Campbell was playing hurt. He was so bothered by his injury that the Seahawks discovered a tell with him, as Campbell's stance told them if the Patriots were going to run or pass. Campbell was much better when he was healthier earlier in the year. Now armed with better health and more experience, Campbell should be much improved in 2026. However, the Patriots sorely needed a better bookend for Campbell, and they may have gotten one with their first-round pick, Caleb Lomu. It remains to be seen how Lomu will perform, but he's a promising prospect coming out of Utah. The interior of New England's offensive line needed a makeover as well. The Patriots may have gotten a big upgrade by signing Alijah Vera-Tucker. The former Jet is an extremely talented and versatile lineman, but he's dealt with numerous injuries throughout his career thus far. He'll be a big upgrade at guard when healthy, and he can play tackle in a pinch if there are multiple injuries at the position. The other guard, Mike Onwenu, was the team's best offensive lineman last year. As for the final position in the interior, Jared Wilson will move from left guard to center. Wilson struggled at left guard last year, but he was just a third-round rookie. He may be better at center. The running backs will be pleased to be running behind an enhanced offensive line. Many were expecting TreVeyon Henderson to have a huge rookie campaign, but he never earned the coaches' trust because of his shoddy pass protection. This was a surprise because Henderson was lauded for his pass-protecting ability coming out of Ohio State. Perhaps that'll improve, and if it does, he may unseat Rhamondre Stevenson, who was solid last year. 2026 New England Patriots Defense: While many were shocked by the improvements New England's offense made last year, everyone likely suspected that the defense would be bolstered. Mike Vrabel had his fingerprints all over the defensive unit, improving the defense so much that it surrendered nearly a touchdown fewer per game. The Patriots allowed 24.5 points per game in 2024, but only 17.9 in 2025. Aside from Vrabel's elite coaching, the greatest factor for New England's defensive improvement was the bolstered pass rush. The Patriots spent nine figures on Milton Williams last offseason, and it paid dividends. Williams was just a rotational player on Philadelphia's stacked defensive line, but he became the key cog for the Patriots. Williams missed five games in 2025, but was otherwise dominant, especially in the playoffs. He'll continue to start alongside Christian Barmore and Cory Durden. Barmore is a talented player, but is coming off a down year. Still just 27, Barmore could rebound. Durden filled in well at the end of last year. Williams wasn't the only major signing to impact the pass rush. The Patriots also brought in Harold Landry, who thrived under Vrabel in Tennessee. Landry ended up leading the team in sacks with 8.5. Still, New England wanted even more of a pass rush, so the team acquired two new players this offseason. It signed Dre'Mont Jones, a talented and versatile front-seven player, and then spent a second-round pick on Gabe Jacas. These new defenders should be able to further enhance the pass rush. A bolstered pass rush can only help the cornerbacks, who played well last year. All three starters return, with Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis playing on the outside, and Marcus Jones being stationed in the slot. Gonzalez is one of the better corners in the NFL, while Davis performed well after coming over from Detroit. Jones was also solid in addition to being a major threat as a punt returner. There were changes at safety, but not for the better. Jaylinn Hawkins was excellent last year, but he's gone after signing with the Ravens. To fill the void, the Patriots signed Kevin Byard, who used to be a terrific player in Tennessee. He's now 33, however, so his best days are long gone. Byard will start next to 2025 fourth-round pick Craig Woodson, who had a rough beginning to his rookie year, but improved as the season progressed. At linebacker, the Patriots had some amazing play from Robert Spillane. The former Raider and Steeler was elite in run support and strong in coverage. He'll start next to Christian Elliss, who was mediocre last year. 2026 New England Patriots Schedule and Intangibles: The elephant in the room is the scandal involving Mike Vrabel and the top Patriots beat reporter, Dianna Russini. The two were involved in an affair that has prompted many to call for Vrabel's firing. While it's unlikely that the Patriots will fire their stellar coach, the scandal could serve as a distraction. Since 2003, the Patriots are 153-47 at home. The magic vanished following Tom Brady's departure, but Drake Maye was 8-3 as a host in 2025. The Patriots have had kicking woes for a couple of years prior to 2025. They decided to use a sixth-round pick on Andy Borregales to provide a solution. It worked, as Borregales was 27-of-32, including a perfect 4-of-4 from 50-plus. Another sixth-round pick, Bryce Baringer, was obtained in 2023. He was 19th in net punting in 2024 and 23rd in that category last year. The Patriots had the second-easiest schedule in the NFL last year. Things are more difficult this time. Tough opponents include the Seahawks, Jaguars, Bears, Lions, Chargers, Chiefs, and Bills twice. They still have some easy opponents like the Raiders, Steelers, Jets twice, and Dolphins twice. 2026 New England Patriots Rookies: Go here for the Patriots Rookie Forecast , a page with predictions like which rookie will bust and which rookie will become a solid starter. 2026 New England Patriots Positional Rankings (1-5 stars): Quarterbacks Offensive Line Secondary Running Backs Defensive Line Special Teams Receivers Linebackers Coaching 2026 New England Patriots Analysis: The Patriots endured poor coaching and inexperience at quarterback in 2024. With Drake Maye improving, and Mike Vrabel joining the team, New England reached the Super Bowl. However, part of the equation was having the easiest schedule in the conference. The Patriots' road will be more challenging in 2026, and it remains to be seen how much of a distraction the Vrabel scandal will cause. However, the Patriots have also made big improvements to the weak points of their roster, so perhaps they won't suffer a big decline after all. Projection: 10-7 (2nd in AFC East) 2025 Projection: 8-9. 2025 Actual Result: 14-3. 2024 Projection: 3-14. 2024 Actual Result: 4-13. 2023 Projection: 5-12. 2023 Actual Result: 4-13. 2022 Projection: 10-7. 2022 Actual Result: 8-9. 2021 Projection: 8-9. 2021 Actual Result: 10-7. 2020 Projection: 11-5. 2020 Actual Result: 7-9. 2019 Projection: 11-5. 2019 Actual Result: 12-4. 2018 Projection: 14-2. 2018 Actual Result: 11-5. 2017 Projection: 14-2. 2017 Actual Result: 13-3. 2016 Projection: 12-4. 2016 Actual Result: 14-2. NFL Draft Team Grade: B+ Grade Goals Entering the 2026 NFL Draft: New England's primary goal is clear. Drake Maye must be protected after he was sacked at least five times in every playoff game. Multiple offensive linemen must be acquired to give Maye a better chance next year. Meanwhile, the defense must acquire some help in the secondary, with both cornerback and safety being areas of need. 2026 NFL Draft Accomplishments: The Patriots had a dilemma. They were drafting at No. 31, yet all of the first-round tackles were flying off the board. They had to trade up, and they were lucky enough to find an unusual partner in the Bills, who allowed them to obtain the final opening-round tackle on the board. New England secured Caleb Lomu, who could provide a big upgrade for New England at right tackle. The Lomu pick earned the Patriots an "A," as did the second-round choice, Gabe Jacas, who provided great value at No. 55. That's where the overwhelming positivity ends, however, as none of New England's seven other draft choices scored better than a "B" grade. This began with the third-round selection, Eli Raridon, who should have gone later because of his checkered injury history. None of the picks made on Day 3 really stood out, but none of them were overly horrible either. While the Patriots had a mixed bag of draft scores, what helped was that they addressed their weak offensive line twice. They could have spent a third pick on a blocker, as some of the wasted third-day choices could have been used to help Maye's protection. Still, the Patriots did well overall. NFL Draft Individual Grades: 28. Caleb Lomu, OT, Utah A Grade We’ve seen some sketchy trade-ups, but this was a great one. Caleb Lomu was the final tackle available in the first round, and he easily could have gone to the 49ers or Chiefs. Drake Maye was sacked at least five times in every single playoff game, so New England had to obtain someone like Lomu. 55. Gabe Jacas, DE, Illinois A Grade The Patriots have traded up again, and I like that they did so once more. Gabe Jacas could have been chosen early in the second round as a quick and strong defensive end. He’s a good player in run support and the pass rush, so the Patriots are getting a quality upgrade on the edge. 95. Eli Raridon, TE, Notre Dame C Grade It’s not a surprise that the Patriots drafted a tight end, with Hunter Henry aging. Eli Raridon is a good route runner with plus athleticism, but carries a very checkered injury history. I thought he would go later than this because of his injuries. 171. Karon Prunty, CB, Wake Forest B Grade Karon Prunty is fine for this range for the Patriots, who needed to bolster secondary depth. Prunty is a talented zone corner, but he’s very weak and needs to beef up for the NFL. 196. Dametrious Crownover, OT, Texas A&M B Grade Dametrious Crownover has a big body and needs to improve his conditioning. If he can, he could end up competing for a starting job if the Patriots have injuries up front. I had him going in this range, so this is a nice choice for the Patriots, as any sort of quality blocking is welcome. 212. Namdi Obiazor, LB, TCU C Grade Namdi Obiazor is an athletic and productive linebacker, but he’s small and may not have much of a role outside of special teams. I didn’t have him being drafted. 234. Behren Morton, QB, Texas Tech C- Grade Behren Morton is accurate, but doesn’t see the field well and makes poor decisions. This is not a pick I would have recommended. Why not just go with Garrett Nussmeier? 245. Jam Miller, RB, Alabama B- Grade Jam Miller was not impressive last year and appeared to be weighed down by injuries. Maybe he can overcome them and be a decent backup behind TreVeyon Henderson, but that probably won’t happen. 247. Quintayvious Hutchins, DE/OLB, Boston College C+ Grade Quintayvious Hutchins is an extremely fast edge rusher with a high motor, but is severely undersized. He might just be too limited to be in the NFL. --Offseason Reports Lander-- Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Baltimore Ravens Buffalo Bills Carolina Panthers Chicago Bears Cincinnati Bengals
